Set 1.q: 1. Where was Mahatma Gandhi arrested during the Quit India Movement?
Set 1.explanation: After the resolution of the Quit India Movement was passed, Gandhiji was arrested in Bombay on 9 August, 1942. After that, he was kept under detention at the Aga Khan Palace in Poona (Pune).

Set 1.q: 2. Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: In the year 1946, the Constituent Assembly of India was elected by the Provincial Assemblies.
Jawaharlal Nehru, M.A. Jinnah and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel were members of the Constituent Assembly of India.
The First Session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held in January 1947.
The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 January 1950.
Set 1.explanation: According to the Cabinet Mission Plan, elections to the Constituent Assembly were held in July, 1946. For the Constituent Assembly, 296 members were elected from British India, including 292 provincial representatives and 4 representatives from the Chief Commissioners’ Provinces. Of these, 208 were from the Congress, 73 from the Muslim League, and 15 were elected from other parties or as independent candidates. Muhammad Ali Jinnah was not a member of the Constituent Assembly of India. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9 December, 1946. Its temporary President was Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha. In the second meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December, 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as its permanent President. The Constitution of India was adopted, enacted, and given to ourselves on 26 November, 1949, and it came into force on 26 January, 1950.

Set 1.q: 3. Choose the correct chronological order of the following battles: A. Third Battle of Panipat B. Battle of Haldighati C. Second Battle of Tarain D. Battle of Asirgarh
Set 1.explanation: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761 A.D. between the Afghans and the Marathas. In this battle, the Afghans were led by Ahmad Shah Abdali and the Marathas were led by Sadashiv Rao Bhau. The Marathas were defeated in this battle. The Battle of Haldighati was fought in 1576 A.D. between the army of Maharana Pratap and the Mughal army, in which the Mughal side was led by Man Singh. In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 A.D.), Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan. In 1601 A.D., Asirgarh came under the control of the Mughals during the reign of Akbar.

Set 1.q: 4. With reference to forced labour (Vishti) in India during the Gupta period, which of the following statements is correct?
options: It was considered a source of income for the state, a kind of tax paid by the people.
It was completely absent in the Madhya Pradesh and Kathiawar regions of the Gupta Empire.
The forced labourer was entitled to weekly wages.
The eldest son of the labourer was sent as a forced labourer.
Set 1.explanation: In the land-grant inscriptions of the Gupta-Vakataka period, Vishti (begar/forced labour) is mentioned in the context of taxes, royal dues, and exemptions granted from them. In the Riddhapur copper plate of Prabhavati Gupta, the land grants has been described as exempt from taxes and vishti. Therefore, vishti was understood as a labour tax as well as a royal due under the authority of the state/king. Although evidence of the begar system is found from the Mauryan period itself, during the Gupta period it became a form of tax received by the king on different occasions. Under this system, labourers, artisans, and peasants were compulsorily required to work for the king or the state, for which they were not given any payment. This practice was most prevalent in Madhya Pradesh and Kathiawar. This practice of begar continued from generation to generation, but it did not have any rule like primogeniture; it applied to all workers.

Set 1.q: 5. Which of the following social reforms were initiated by William Bentinck? 1. Abolition of the Sati practice 2. Abolition of slavery 3. Removal of the provision of disqualification on account of religious conversion 4. Suppression of organized gangs of Thugs
Set 1.explanation: Lord William Bentinck became the Governor-General of the Bengal Presidency in 1828 A.D. In 1829 A.D., through the ‘Bengal Sati Regulation’, he declared the practice of sati illegal and punishable. During Bentinck’s period itself, the Charter Act, 1833 took the initiative to abolish slavery, but its complete legal abolition took place through the Indian Slavery Act of 1843. Bentinck also launched a campaign against gangs of Thugs and tried to suppress them. Bentinck also worked for education and freedom of the press. In 1835 A.D., he returned to England. The provision of disqualification on the ground of religious conversion was removed in 1850 A.D. Therefore, statements (1), (2), and (4) are correct. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Set 1.q: 6. Which of the following industrialists served as the treasurer of the A.I.C.C. for a long time and also went to jail in 1930?
Set 1.explanation: Jamnalal Bajaj was a prominent industrialist and Congress worker associated with the Gandhian national movement. He was one of the close associates of Gandhiji. He served as the treasurer of the Indian National Congress for a long time. He was imprisoned in 1923 for participating in the Nagpur Flag Satyagraha and again in 1930 during the Civil Disobedience Movement.

Set 1.q: 7. With reference to Chandragupta-II, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? 1. The strongest evidence of his victory over the Shakas is the silver coins of this ruler. 2. The weight of these coins was approximately 33 grains.
Set 1.explanation: The most important archaeological evidence of Chandragupta II’s victory over the Shakas is his silver coins. After defeating the Western Kshatrapas, he issued silver coins based on their pattern. According to John Allan, after the conquest of Saurashtra, Chandragupta II issued silver coins closely imitating the Kshatrapa coins. This proves statement (1) to be correct. Regarding the weight of the coins, A. S. Altekar considered the theoretical weight of Gupta silver coins to be about 33 grains, although variations in their weight are also found. Therefore, statement (2) is also correct.

Set 1.q: 8. Which of the following pairs (Philosophy-Propounder) is correctly matched?
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching of the given philosophies and their propounders is as follows— Vaisheshika – Kanada (kanva) Nyaya – Gautama Purva Mimamsa – Jaimini Vedanta Philosophy/Uttara Mimamsa – Badarayana

Set 1.q: 9. Which one of the following views about the Revolt of 1857 is correct?
options: Indian historians have described it as the Indian Revolt.
British historians have called it the War of Independence.
It made the ruling system of the East India Company in India virtually defunct.
This revolt was carried out to reform the administrative system in India.
Set 1.explanation: The Revolt of 1857 was a widespread uprising of soldiers and people against the rule of the East India Company, after which a decisive change took place in the governance of India. Its most important result was that the Company’s rule came to an end, and in 1858 A.D., the administration of India was placed under the British Crown. Therefore, in the context of the Revolt of 1857, the idea given in option (c) is correct, while the other statements are not correct.

Set 1.q: 10. Who presided over the session of the 'All India Trade Union Congress' held at Nagpur in the year 1929?
Set 1.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the session of the All India Trade Union Congress (A.I.T.U.C.) held at Nagpur in 1929. It was also in the Nagpur session that the A.I.T.U.C. split due to differences between the communists and the moderates.

Set 1.q: 11. The place where pre-Ashokan Brahmi script has been discovered is-
Set 1.explanation: Evidence of the pre-Ashokan Brahmi script of the fourth century B.C. has been found at Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka. Evidence of this type of script has also been found in inscriptions from some other places, namely Piprahwa, Sohgaura and Mahasthan. Scholars do not agree on the period of these inscriptions. Some scholars consider them contemporary with Ashoka, while others consider them to have been inscribed after Ashoka.

Set 1.q: 12. In the Partition Council formed under the chairmanship of Lord Mountbatten, the Indian National Congress was represented by- 1. Abul Kalam Azad 2. Jawaharlal Nehru 3. Sardar Patel 4. Rajendra Prasad
Set 1.explanation: The Partition Council was a body formed in 1947 to conduct the administrative work related to the partition of India. It was chaired by Lord Mountbatten. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Dr. Rajendra Prasad represented the Indian National Congress in this Council. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 1.q: 13. Who founded the 'Theosophical Society'?
Set 1.explanation: The Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875 A.D. by Madame H. P. Blavatsky, Colonel Henry Steel Olcott, William Quan Judge and others. In 1882 A.D., the founders of this Society established its headquarters at Adyar, near Madras, now Chennai, which later became its International Headquarters. The official objects of the Society were to promote universal brotherhood, to encourage the study of comparative religion, philosophy and science, and to investigate the unexplained laws of Nature and the powers hidden in man.

Set 1.q: 14. Match List-I (Emperor) with List-II (Tomb): A. Babur B. Akbar C. Jahangir D. Shah Jahan | 1. Lahore 2. Agra 3. Kabul 4. Sikandara
Set 1.explanation: The correctly matched order is as follows— List-I (Emperor) Babur (1526–1530 A.D.) Akbar (1556–1605 A.D.) Jahangir (1605–1627 A.D.) Shah Jahan  – List-II (Tomb)– Kabul– Sikandara– Lahore– Agra (1628–1658 A.D.)

Set 1.q: 15. Consider the following statements- 1. The Factories Act, 1881 was passed to fix the wages of industrial workers and to allow workers to form trade unions. 2. N. M. Lokhande was a pioneer in organizing the labour movement in British India.
Set 1.explanation: The objective of the Factories Act, 1881 was neither to fix the wages of workers nor to give labourers/workers the right important contribution consists of the compositions included in the Guru Granth Sahib/Adi Granth. He made Hansi and Ajodhan the centres of his activities. to form trade unions. This Act mainly contained limited provisions related to holidays for children, working hours, machinery safety, inspection and accident reporting. Therefore, statement (1) is incorrect. N. M. Lokhande (Narayan Meghaji Lokhande) was a pioneer in organizing the labour movement in India. In the 19th century, he is remembered not only for improving the miserable condition of workers in handlooms and textile mills, but also for taking bold initiatives on issues such as caste and communal matters. Therefore, only statement (2) is correct.

Set 1.q: 16. What was the objective of Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858)? 1. To abandon any idea of annexing Indian states to the British Empire 2. To place Indian administration under the British Crown 3. To regulate the East India Company's trade with India
Set 1.explanation: The British Government enacted an Act in 1858 A.D. The title of this Act was “An Act for the Better Government of India.” Through this Act, the rule of the East India Company in India was ended, and the British Government took the administration of Indian territories directly into its own hands. Under this Act, Queen Victoria issued a proclamation in 1858 A.D., in which it was declared that from then onward the governance of India would be carried on by, and in the name of, the British government through the Secretary of State. The Governor-General was given the title of Viceroy, which meant that he was the representative of the government. In short, British paramountcy over India was firmly established. At the same time, through Queen Victoria’s proclamation, the princely states were assured that their existence would continue. It is clear that it was declared that any idea of annexing Indian states into the British Empire had been abandoned. In 'The History of India' published by Britannica, p. 261, it is mentioned– “The announcement reversed Lord Dalhousie’s prewar policy of political unification through princely state annexation.”

Set 1.q: 17. The ideas of which of the following Sufi saints have been included in the Sikh religious scripture 'Adi Granth'?
Set 1.explanation: Sheikh Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar was a Sufi saint of the Chishti order, popularly known as “Baba Farid.” Through his efforts, the Chishti order gained popularity in India. His most

Set 1.q: 18. Consider the following Mughal rulers and arrange them in chronological order: I. Farrukhsiyar II. Jahandar Shah III. Bahadur Shah IV. Muhammad Shah
Set 1.explanation: The periods of the Mughal rulers, in chronological order, are as follows— Bahadur Shah I (1707–1712 A.D.), Jahandar Shah (1712–1713 A.D.), Farrukhsiyar (1713–1719 A.D.) and Muhammad Shah “Rangila” (1719–1748 A.D.). Therefore, it is clear that the intended answer will be option (c).

Set 1.q: 19. Consider the following statements- 1. The last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, was killed by his commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Shunga. 2. The last Shunga king, Devabhuti, was killed by his Brahmin minister Vasudeva Kanva... 3. The Andhras deposed the last ruler of the Kanva dynasty.
Set 1.explanation: The ambitious person who founded the Shunga dynasty by killing the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha around 185–184 BCE is known in history as Pushyamitra Shunga. The last king of the Shunga dynasty, Devabhuti, was extremely indulgent. He was killed as a result of the conspiracies of his minister Vasudeva. According to the Vayu Purana, the last Kanva ruler Susharma was killed by his servant of Andhra origin, Simuka (Sindhuka).

Set 1.q: 20. During the reign of which Mughal emperor were the Upanishads translated into Persian?
Set 1.explanation: The Persian translation of the Upanishads was prepared during the reign of Shah Jahan by Prince Dara Shikoh under the title ‘Sirr-i-Akbar’. It contains translations of about 52 Upanishads. Because of Dara’s tolerance and liberal outlook, Lane-Poole called him ‘Little Akbar’. Moreover, Shah Jahan also conferred the title ‘Shah Buland Iqbal’ on Dara. ‘Majma-ul-Bahrain’ is Dara’s original work.

Set 1.q: 21. The Elephanta Caves were mainly excavated for use by the followers of which of the following religions?
Set 1.explanation: The Rashtrakutas and other dynasties contributed to the construction of the famous cave temples of Elephanta. Seven cave temples are found here, which contain sculptures related to Hinduism, mainly related to Shiva. The famous Trimurti image of Shiva is found here.

Set 1.q: 22. Which one of the following animals was not represented in the seals and terracotta artefacts found in Harappan culture?
Set 1.explanation: The cow is not depicted on the seals and terracotta objects of the Harappan culture, whereas depictions of the elephant, rhinoceros, tiger, deer, sheep, etc. are found. The cow gained importance in the Vedic period. that

with special instructions to keep India united as far as possible.

Set 1.q: 24. Which extremist leader of the freedom struggle was sentenced to six years' imprisonment in 1908?
Set 1.explanation: In 1908, Bal Gangadhar Tilak was tried for sedition on the basis of articles published in ‘Kesari’. He was sentenced to six years’ transportation and fined Rs. 1000, and was sent to Mandalay Jail in Myanmar.

Set 1.q: 25. Name the Chola ruler who conquered the northern part of Sri Lanka.
Set 1.explanation: The Chola ruler Rajaraja I attacked Sri Lanka, conquered northern Sri Lanka, and annexed it to his kingdom. In the conquered region, Rajaraja destroyed Anuradhapura, made Polonnaruwa the capital of this region, and named it ‘Jananatha Mangalam’ (some sources also mention the name Jananatha Pura). Rajaraja was a follower of Shaivism and had assumed the title ‘Shivapadasekhara’.

Set 1.q: 26. The first organisation founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy was-
Set 1.explanation: In 1815 CE, Raja Rammohan Roy, with the help of his young supporters, founded the ‘Atmiya Sabha’ to propagate the monotheistic view of Hinduism. Atmiya Sabha was Raja Rammohan Roy’s early reformist institution, where religious, social, and philosophical questions were discussed.

Set 1.q: 27. Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
Set 1.explanation: Among the given options, the rulers who introduced the administrative departments are— Diwan-i-Mustakhraj – Alauddin Khalji (Revenue Department) Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi – Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Agriculture Department) Diwan-i-Khairat – Firoz Tughlaq (Charity Department) Diwan-i-Riyasat –  Alauddin Khalji (Market Control Department)

Set 1.q: 28. Consider the following statements with reference to the Simon Commission- 1. It visited India twice. 2. Its second visit was from 11 October 1929 to 13 April 1930.
Set 1.explanation: The Indian Statutory Commission, commonly known as the Simon Commission after its chairman Sir John Allsebrook Simon, visited India twice. Its first visit to India was from February 3 to March 31, 1928, and its second visit was from October 11, 1928, to April 13, 1929. Therefore, it is clear that the second statement is false.

Set 1.q: 29. The 'Quit India Movement' was the result of- (1) disappointment of Indians with Cripps proposals. (2) threat of Japanese invasion. (3) Gandhiji's writings inciting violent means. (4) a resolution passed by the A.I.C.C. in August 1942.
Set 1.explanation: The Quit India Movement was a widespread nationalist movement that began in August 1942 with the demand for the immediate end of British rule. The Indian leadership was disappointed with the proposals of the Cripps Mission because they did not provide for the immediate transfer of power. At the same time, Japan’s advance up to Burma also increased the fear of an attack on India. On August 8, 1942, the Congress approved the Quit India Resolution. Therefore, statements (1), (2), and (4) are correct. Statement (3) is incorrect because Gandhiji considered the movement to be a non-violent mass struggle and did not incite people to violence.

Set 1.q: 30. Nagara, Dravida and Vesara are-
options: the three main ethnic groups of the Indian subcontinent.
the three main language groups into which the languages of India can be divided.
the three main styles of Indian temple architecture.
the three main musical gharanas prevalent in India.
Set 1.explanation: Nagara, Dravida, and Vesara are the three main styles of Indian temple architecture. The Nagara style is mainly prevalent in northern India. The Dravida style spread in South India, especially in the region between the Krishna River and Cape Comorin. The Vesara style developed from a mixture of the Nagara and Dravida styles. Since this style was mainly used by the Chalukya rulers of South India, it is also called the Chalukya style.

Set 1.q: 31. Match List-I with List-II: A. Bardoli Satyagraha B. Indian Peasants Institute C. Bengal Praja Party D. Bakasht Struggle | 1. Swami Shraddhanand 2. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel 3. Fazlul Huq 4. N.G. Ranga
Set 1.explanation: In 1928, the Gandhian movement and satyagraha achieved considerable success in the Bardoli taluka of Surat district. The Mehta brothers and other local leaders had been carrying out organisational, social, and constructive work in this region since 1920. The conditions arose after 1922 prepared the background for the Bardoli Satyagraha. In 1928, the peasant discontent that arose there was led by Vallabhbhai Patel, and it became famous as the Bardoli Satyagraha. Due to the success of this movement, the women of Bardoli gave Patel the title ‘Sardar’. The Indian Peasants’ Institute was founded by N. G. Ranga. In 1929, Fazlul Huq founded the Praja Party, which later became the Bengal Praja Party. This party later came to be known as the ‘Krishak Praja Party’. The Bakasht (self-cultivated land) struggle of Bihar is associated with Swami Shraddhanand Saraswati.

Set 1.q: 32. According to Chinese sources, the ruler of Sri Lanka, Meghavarman, sent a mission... to which of the following Gupta kings for permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya?
Set 1.explanation: The contemporary ruler of Sri Lanka (Sinhala) during the time of the Gupta ruler Samudragupta (335–375 CE) was Meghavarna/Meghavarman. Chinese sources show that Meghavarman had sent a delegation with gifts to Samudragupta. With the permission of the Gupta ruler, he had a grand vihara constructed to the north of the Bodhi Tree for the Buddhist monks of Sri Lanka.

Set 1.q: 33. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding Vasco da Gama? (i) At the time of Vasco da Gama's visit to India in 1498, the ruler of Calicut was Zamorin. (ii) During his first voyage, he stayed in India for about one year. (iii) Vasco da Gama visited India again in 1501.
Set 1.explanation: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut on May 20, 1498. At that time, the ruler of Calicut was the Zamorin (Samuthiri). He welcomed Vasco da Gama. Vasco da Gama stayed in India for about three months and returned to Portugal with ships loaded with Indian goods. Vasco da Gama visited India again in 1502 CE and 1524 CE.

Set 1.q: 34. Match List-I with List-II: A. Taj-ul-Maasir B. Khazain-ul-Futuh C. Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi D. Fatwa-i-Jahandari | 1. Ziauddin Barani 2. Hasan Nizami 3. Amir Khusrau 4. Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching of List-I with List-II is as follows— List-I – List-II Taj-ul-Ma’asir – Hasan Nizami Khaza’in-ul-Futuh – Amir Khusrau Tarikh-i-Mubarak – Yahya bin Shahi Ahmad Sirhindi Fatwa-i-Jahandari – Ziauddin Barani Therefore, among the given options, option (a) is the correct answer.

Set 1.q: 35. Assertion (A): Babur wrote the 'Baburnama' in Turkish. Reason (R): Turkish was the official language of the Mughal court.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 1.explanation: Babur wrote the events related to his life in the Turkish language, which is known as ‘Tuzuk-i-Baburi’ or ‘Baburnama’. The official language of the Mughal court was not Turkish but Persian. Therefore, the answer will be option (c).

Set 1.q: 36. Consider the following statements- 1. When the Shimla Conference was held, Lord Mountbatten was the Viceroy. 2. The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny, 1946, took place when Indian sailors from Mumbai and Karachi rose against the government.
Set 1.explanation: The Shimla Conference was held in June 1945 during the tenure of Lord Wavell, not Lord Mountbatten. Therefore, statement 1 is incorrect. The Royal Indian Navy Revolt of 1946 began in Bombay with the Indian sailors of HMIS Talwar and later spread to Bombay Harbour, Karachi and other naval centres. The main causes of this revolt were poor food, racial discrimination and dissatisfaction with service conditions. Therefore, statement 2 is correct. Thus, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 1.q: 37. With reference to the religious history of medieval India, which of the following practices did the Sufi mystics pursue? 1. Meditation and control of breath 2. Severe ascetic exercises in a lonely place 3. Recitation of holy songs to arouse a state of ecstasy
Set 1.explanation: The emergence of Sufis in medieval India helped in spreading harmony in society. These Sufis used to practise yogic practices such as meditation and strict breath control. They performed rigorous yogic exercises in solitude and took the help of songs and music to spread unity and goodwill in society and to create spiritual ecstasy among the listeners.

Set 1.q: 38. The Barrah dacoity was the first major venture of the revolutionary terrorists of the freedom movement in-
Set 1.explanation: The site of the Barrah Dacoity of 1908 was located in East Bengal. This incident is associated with the revolutionary organisation of East Bengal, the ‘Dhaka Anushilan Samiti’.

Set 1.q: 39. The doctrine of Syadvada is associated with-
Set 1.explanation: Mahavira Swami was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism. He refused to accept divine origin, of the Vedas and opposed religious and social orthodoxies and hypocrisy. Syadvada is an important principle of Jainism/Jain philosophy. It is a relative principle associated with anekarthavada/anekantavada, according to which no final, one sided and absolute claim should be made about any object or statement; a statement should be understood conditionally with ‘syat’. Its seven forms of predication are called Saptabhangi-naya.
