Set 1.q: 41. Consider the following statements regarding the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS)- (1) On August 25, 2024, the Union Cabinet approved the UPS. (2) Under this scheme... 50 percent of the average basic pay drawn during the last 12 months... will be provided as an assured pension.
Set 1.explanation: The Unified Pension Scheme is a pension option available under the National Pension System for Central Government employees, under which assured pension is provided on the basis of qualifying service. Statement (1) is incorrect because the Union Cabinet approved the Unified Pension Scheme on August 24, 2024, not on August 25, 2024. Statement (2) is correct because under this scheme, on completion of a minimum qualifying service of 25 years, 50 percent of the average basic pay received during the last 12 months before retirement will be given as assured pension. If the service period is less than 25 years, the pension will be given on a proportionate basis, subject to a minimum service of 10 years. Therefore, only statement (2) is correct, so the correct answer is option (b).

Set 1.q: 42. Which of the following statements regarding the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is/are correct? 1. It determines the RBI's benchmark interest rates. 2. It is a 12-member body... 3. It functions under the chairmanship of the Union Finance Minister.
Set 1.explanation: The Monetary Policy Committee is a statutory committee constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. It decides the policy repo rate to achieve the inflation target. Statement 1 is correct because the Monetary Policy Committee decides the policy repo rate. It is generally considered the standard policy interest rate of the Reserve Bank of India. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Monetary Policy Committee is not a 12-member body, but a 6-member body. It has 3 members from the Reserve Bank of India and 3 members appointed by the Central Government. The tenure of the external members is generally 4 years; therefore, it is not reconstituted every year. Statement 3 is also incorrect because the Monetary Policy Committee is chaired not by the Union Finance Minister, but by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India. Therefore, only statement 1 is correct, so the correct answer is option (a).

Set 1.q: 43. Which of the following is not a part of the Indian money market?
Set 1.explanation: The money market is the market where short-term funds are transacted and short-term financial instruments are traded. In this question, “currency trade” should be understood in the sense of “money market.” IDBI and ICICI, as banking institutions, may be associated with the money market. Money market mutual funds also invest in short-term money market instruments. Whereas, NABARD is a development Financial Institution that mainly provider credit and support for agriculture, rural development, Cooperative banks, RRBs etc. Thus, it is not classified as money market institution as it does not participate in short term financing. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 1.q: 44. With reference to the 'Tea Board' in India, consider the following statements- 1. The Tea Board is a statutory body. 2. It is attached to the Ministry of Agriculture. 3. The head office is in Bengaluru. 4. Overseas offices in Dubai and Moscow.
Set 1.explanation: The Tea Board is a statutory body under the Government of India, constituted under the Tea Act, 1953 for functions related to the development and regulation of the tea industry. Statement 1 is correct because the Tea Board is a statutory body. Statement 2 is incorrect because it is not attached to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare; rather, it comes under the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Head Office of the Tea Board is not located in Bengaluru, but in Kolkata, West Bengal. Statement 4 is also incorrect because, according to the current official position, the Tea Board has only one foreign office, located in Moscow, not in Dubai. Hence, only Statement 1 is correct. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 1.q: 45. Which of the following is not a method of controlling inflation?
options: Control over the supply of money
Set 1.explanation: Inflation is a situation in which the general price level rises continuously. To control it, measures such as controlling demand, controlling money supply and regulating the distribution of essential commodities are adopted. Controlling demand is a method of controlling inflation because it reduces excess demand pressure on goods and services. Controlling money supply also helps in reducing inflation because it regulates liquidity and credit expansion in the market. Rationing of goods is also an administrative measure through which essential commodities are distributed in a controlled manner. In contrast, reducing interest rates is not a method of controlling inflation. When interest rates are reduced, loans become cheaper, consumption and investment increase, and demand in the market may rise. As a result, inflation may increase instead of decreasing. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 1.q: 46. In India, agricultural income tax can be levied by-
Set 1.explanation: Agricultural income tax means a tax imposed on income derived from agriculture. In India, the power to levy tax on agricultural income is placed in the State List of the Constitution. Option (a) is correct because tax on agricultural income falls under Entry 46 of the State List. Therefore, State Legislatures can make laws on this subject, and State Governments can levy such tax on the basis of those laws. The Central Government cannot levy income tax on agricultural income because Union income tax excludes agricultural income. Local governments also do not have independent constitutional authority to levy tax on agricultural income. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 1.q: 47. Match List-I (Revolution) with List-II (Associated with): A. Golden B. Grey C. Yellow D. Black | 1. Oilseed 2. Horticulture/honey 3. Petroleum 4. Fertilizers
Set 1.explanation: In India, specific increases in production in different sectors are associated with colour based revolutions in General Studies. The Golden Revolution is related to horticulture and honey production. The Grey Revolution is related to fertilizer production. The Yellow Revolution is related to oilseed production. The Black Revolution is generally considered to be related to petroleum production. Thus, the correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-1 and D-3. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 1.q: 48. From which year did the Census begin in India on a regular and scientific basis?
Set 1.explanation: Census is the regular enumeration of the population of a country and its related socio economic characteristics. In India, the system of regular, synchronous and scientific Census is considered to have begun in 1881. The first modern Census in India was conducted in 1872, but it was conducted in different parts of the country at different times. Therefore, it was a non-synchronous Census. The 1881 Census was the first synchronous and systematic Census, after which the tradition of decennial Census was established. From the updated perspective, decennial Censuses were conducted regularly from 1881 to 2011, while the 2021 Census remained postponed and the next Census has been notified for

Set 1.q: 49. Consider the following- 1. IFCI 2. ICICI 3. IDBI 4. UTI. The correct chronological order in which these were established is-
Set 1.explanation: Development finance institutions were established to provide medium- and long-term finance to industries. The Industrial Finance Corporation of India was established in 1948. The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India was established in 1955. The Unit Trust of India Act was passed in 1963 and came into force on 1 February 1964. The Industrial Development Bank of India came into existence on 1 July 1964. Therefore, the correct chronological order is 1, 2, 4, 3. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 1.q: 50. Financial sector reforms in India include-
options: Entry of private companies in the insurance
Set 1.explanation: The objective of financial sector reforms was to make banking, insurance, the interest-rate regime and financial markets more efficient, competitive and market oriented. Under financial sector reforms in India, the Cash Reserve Ratio and the Statutory Liquidity Ratio were reduced in a phased manner so that banks could have more resources available for lending and investment. The entry of private companies into the insurance sector was also an important reform, which increased competition and helped expand the sector. Similarly, deregulation of interest rates was also a major part of the reforms because it made interest rates more flexible according to market conditions. Hence, all the given options are part of financial sector reforms. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 1.q: 51. With reference to the judiciary of India, select the false statement-
options: Parliament can increase the number of judges of the Supreme Court.
Under Article 138, the Supreme Court can review its judgments/orders.
Under Article 215, every High Court is a Court of Record.
Under Article 129, the Supreme Court is a Court of Record.
Set 1.explanation: The Supreme Court has the power to review its judgments and orders, but this power is under Article 137, not Article 138. Article 138 deals with the enlargement of the jurisdiction and powers of the Supreme Court. Options (a), (c) and (d) are constitutionally correct.

Set 1.q: 52. Which of the following States does not have a second House of the Legislature?
Set 1.explanation: Under Article 168(1) (a) of the Constitution, at present, bicameral legislatures– Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council exist in six states of the country: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. It is noteworthy that under the Tamil Nadu Legislative Council Act, 2010, Parliament had also made provision for a Legislative Council in Tamil Nadu, but the date from which this provision would take effect has not been notified.

Set 1.q: 53. Under the Preventive Detention Act, a person may be detained without trial for-
Set 1.explanation: Under a law providing for preventive detention, a person can be detained for three months without trial. According to Article 22(4), if the detention is for more than three months, the case must be referred to an Advisory Board. Such a person can be kept in detention only when the Advisory Board is of the opinion that there is sufficient cause for such detention.

Set 1.q: 54. The aim of the Preamble to the Constitution of India is to secure to all its citizens- 1. Social and economic justice 2. Liberty of thought and expression 3. Equality of opportunity 4. Dignity of the individual
Set 1.explanation: The objective of the Preamble of the Constitution of India is to secure to all its citizens—social, economic and political justice; liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; equality of status and opportunity; and fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual.

Set 1.q: 55. How can the Speaker of the Lok Sabha be removed?
options: By a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the members present in the Lok Sabha
By a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha
By the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister
Set 1.explanation: According to Article 94(c), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha can be removed from office by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Lok Sabha. However, such a resolution cannot be moved unless at least 14 days’ prior written notice of the intention to move the resolution has been given.

Set 1.q: 56. Which of the following statements regarding a Money Bill is false?
options: It is introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
Article 109 mentions the special procedure regarding Money Bills.
Article 110 gives the definition of Money Bills.
Whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not is decided by the President.
Set 1.explanation: A Money Bill is a Bill that relates to the financial matters specified in the Constitution and cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha. Whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not is decided by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha under Article 110(3), and the Speaker’s decision is final. All the remaining statements are correct.

Set 1.q: 57. Which of the following is/are correct? (i) The 73rd and 74th Amendments made provision for a three-tier system... (ii) This system has been taken from Australia. (iii) The 74th Amendment Act is related to constitutional recognition to Panchayats.
Set 1.explanation: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments strengthened the local level of governance by giving a constitutional basis to local self-government. The 73rd Amendment added Part IX related to Panchayats, and the 74th Amendment added Part IXA related to Municipalities. Therefore, statement (i) is correct. Statement (ii) is incorrect because this provision has not been taken from the Constitution of Australia. Statement (iii) is incorrect because the 74th Amendment is related to Municipalities, not Panchayats. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 1.q: 58. The First Amendment Bill to the Indian Constitution was introduced in-
Set 1.explanation: The Constitution (First Amendment) Bill was introduced in Parliament on 12 May 1951 and, after being passed, it was enacted in June 1951. By the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, Articles 15, 19, 85, 87, 174, 176, 341, 342, 372 and 376 were amended, and two new Articles, 31A and 31B, along with the Ninth Schedule, were added to the Constitution.

Set 1.q: 59. The power of the High Court to issue a writ of mandamus covers-
Set 1.explanation: The Supreme Court, under Article 32, and the High Courts, under Article 226, have the power to issue writs of Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto for the protection of Fundamental Rights. However, while the Supreme Court can issue these writs only for the protection of Fundamental Rights, the High Courts can issue them for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights as well as other legal rights.

Set 1.q: 60. Match the following: A. Union List B. State List C. Concurrent List D. Residuary subjects | 1. Police 2. Space research 3. Census 4. Population control
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching is as follows: Union List – Census State List – Police and public order Concurrent List – Population control and family planning Residuary subjects – Space research (under the Union)

Set 1.q: 61. Choose the false statement(s): (i) Article 61 provides procedure for impeachment... (ii) The vacancy should not continue for more than 90 days. (iii) The term of office of the President is not fixed.
Set 1.explanation: The procedure for the impeachment of the President under Article 61 is a quasi-judicial procedure of Parliament; it is not correct to call it merely a legislative procedure. According to Article 62(2), a vacancy in the office of the President must be filled within 6 months, not within 90 days. The term of office of the President is fixed at 5 years under Article 56. Therefore, statements (i), (ii) and (iii), all three, are false. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Set 1.q: 62. Under which Article of the Constitution can the President of India suspend the enforcement of Fundamental Rights, except the rights under Articles 20 and 21?
Set 1.explanation: After the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, when a Proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 is in force, the President, under Article 359, may issue an order suspending the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution, except Articles 20 and 21. When an Emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression, the Fundamental Rights conferred by Article 19 are automatically suspended under Article 358.

Set 1.q: 63. Which of the following provisions is a part of both the Directive Principles of State Policy and the Fundamental Duties?
options: Participation of workers in the management of industries
Parents/guardians should provide opportunities for education to children
Set 1.explanation: In the Indian Constitution, ‘protection of the environment’ is included under the Directive Principles of State Policy in Article 48A and under the Fundamental Duties in Article 51A(g). Among the other options, participation of workers in the management of industries and the Uniform Civil Code are included only under the Directive Principles of State Policy in Articles 43A and 44 respectively, while the duty of parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children is included only under the Fundamental Duties in Article 51A(k).

Set 1.q: 64. With reference to the Indian federal system, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The States do not have the right to secede from the Union. 2. Mere advocacy of secession will be protected under freedom of expression.
Set 1.explanation: Under the Indian Constitution, a ‘Union of States’ has been established, in which the States do not have the right to secede from the Union. Parliament alone can admit or establish new States in the Union, change the area, boundaries or names of States, or create a new State by separating or merging parts of a State/States. However, the Constitution does not give any State the right to secede from the Union. Thus, statement 1 is correct. intermediate level may not be constituted in a State whose population does not exceed 20 lakh.

Set 1.q: 65. What is the structure of the governance system in the Panchayati Raj system?
options: One-tier structure at the village level
Two-tier structure at the village and block levels
Three-tier structure at the village, block and district levels
Four-tier structure at the village, block, district and state levels
Set 1.explanation: The Panchayati Raj system is the constitutional system of rural local self-government. According to Article 243B of the Constitution, local self-government under the Panchayati Raj system is three-tiered– at the village level, intermediate/block level and district level. However, a Panchayat at the

Set 1.q: 66. In North America, between which two lakes is Niagara Falls located?
Set 1.explanation: In North America, ‘Niagara Falls’ is located between Lake Ontario and Lake Erie. Niagara Falls is situated on the Niagara River on the border of the United States of America and Canada. The Niagara River connects Lake Erie and Lake Ontario.

Set 1.q: 67. In the 2011 Census, the population of which of the following states decreased?
Set 1.explanation: According to the Census of 2011, the decadal population growth rate of the Indian State of Nagaland during 2001–2011 was negative (–0.6%). The total population of Nagaland was 1,978,502 in 2011, whereas according to the 2001 Census, its population was 1,990,036. Thus, there was a total decline of 11,534 in its population.

Set 1.q: 68. Match List-I (Oil Refinery) with List-II (State): A. Haldia B. Jamnagar C. Kochi D. Numaligarh | 1. Assam 2. Kerala 3. Gujarat 4. West Bengal
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching of the given oil refineries and their respective States is as follows— (Oil Refinery) – (State) Haldia – West Bengal Jamnagar Kochi Numaligarh – Gujarat– Kerala– Assam

Set 1.q: 69. Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching of the projects given in the options and their respective rivers is as follows— (Project) Dulhasti – (River)– Chenab Sardar Sarovar – Narmada Nagarjuna Sagar – Krishna Ukai – Tapti

Set 1.q: 70. In which states of India is sugarcane produced the most?
options: Andhra Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir
Set 1.explanation: According to the data of *Agricultural Statistics at a Glance, 2024–25*, the order of the top 8 sugarcane-producing States in 2024–25 is as follows—Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Uttarakhand and Punjab. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Set 1.q: 71. In which ocean is Addu Atoll located?
Set 1.explanation: Addu Atoll is located in the Indian Ocean. It is the southernmost atoll of the Maldives. 8 Skeâerke=âle 72JeeR mebÙegòeâ (ØeejbefYekeâ) ØeefleÙeesefielee hejer#ee रफ कार्य हेतु

Set 1.q: 72. Match List-I (Islands) with List-II (Sovereign Country): A. Aleutian B. Bear C. Greenland D. Franz Josef Land | 1. Russia 2. Denmark 3. Norway 4. U.S.A.
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— (Islands of the – (Country having World)   Sovereignty) Aleutian Islands – U.S.A. Bear Island – Norway Greenland – Denmark Franz Josef Land – Russia

Set 1.q: 73. At the time of the summer solstice, the day will be 12 hours long-
Set 1.explanation: At the time of the summer solstice, the Northern Hemisphere has the longest day and the shortest night. In contrast, the Southern Hemisphere has the shortest day and the longest night. However, at the Equator, there is no difference in the duration of day and night. There, the day remains 12 hours long throughout the year. Hence, it is clear that at the time of the summer solstice, a 12-hour day will occur only at the Equator, because in the Northern Hemisphere the duration of the day at this time is much more than 12 hours. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 1.q: 74. Match List-I (Country) with List-II (Capital): A. Uzbekistan B. Tajikistan C. Kyrgyzstan D. Turkmenistan | 1. Tashkent 2. Dushanbe 3. Bishkek 4. Ashgabat
Set 1.explanation: The following are correctly matched— (Country) – (Capital) Uzbekistan – Tashkent Tajikistan – Dushanbe Kyrgyzstan – Bishkek Turkmenistan – Ashgabat

Set 1.q: 75. Match List-I (Mining Area) with List-II (Mineral Resources): A. Kalahandi B. Zawar C. Kolar D. Mosabani | 1. Gold 2. Copper 3. Bauxite 4. Zinc and Lead
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— (Mining Area) – (Mineral Wealth) Kalahandi – Bauxite Zawar – Zinc and Lead Kolar – Gold Mosabani – Copper

Set 1.q: 76. Match List-I (Mountain Peak) with List-II (Continent): A. Kosciuszko B. McKinley C. Elbrus D. Kilimanjaro | i. Europe ii. Africa iii. Australia iv. North America
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching is as follows—

Set 1.q: 77. 'Regur' is the name of which of the following?
Set 1.explanation: Black soil is locally known by different names such as Regur/Regad soil or cotton soil. In India, this soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and also in parts of western Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and other States.

Set 1.q: 78. Which of the following is related to 'Albedo'?
Set 1.explanation: Albedo is the ratio or percentage of the solar radiation received by a surface or object that is reflected back. Therefore, it is related to reflecting power or reflectivity. In the heat balance of the Earth, a part of the radiation coming from the Sun is reflected back into space by clouds, snow, ice and the Earth’s surface. This reflected part is called albedo.

Set 1.q: 79. Which of the following ocean currents is not a current of the Indian Ocean?
Set 1.explanation: The Benguela Current is a cold current of the South Atlantic Ocean. It flows northward along the western coast of south-western Africa. This current is called the Benguela Current after the place named Benguela in Angola, located on the western coast of Africa.

Set 1.q: 80. Match List-I with List-II: A. Vitamin B1 B. Vitamin B2 C. Vitamin B6 D. Vitamin B12 | 1. Cyanocobalamin 2. Pyridoxine 3. Riboflavin 4. Thiamine
Set 1.explanation: Vitamin B1 is also called thiamine. Vitamin B2 is known as riboflavin, Vitamin B12 as cyanocobalamin and Vitamin B6 as pyridoxine. Hence, the correct matching is option (b).

Set 1.q: 81. Which of the following plants does not help in nitrogen fixation?
Set 1.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria are found in the root nodules of leguminous crops such as gram, pea, beans and pigeon pea, which help in nitrogen fixation. In paddy fields, urea, blue-green algae, Azolla etc. are mainly used for the supply of nitrogen.

Set 1.q: 82. Consider the following and arrange them in increasing order of frequency - I. X-rays II. Visible light III. Infrared rays IV. Radio waves
Set 1.explanation: The increasing order of the given electromagnetic waves with reference to frequency is as follows— Radio waves < Infrared rays < Visible light < X-rays

Set 1.q: 83. Consider the following statement: A loaded cart has to be pushed with a greater force to set it in motion than the force required to keep it moving. Conclusion:
options: The weight of a moving object is less.
Once the cart starts moving, friction is less.
Set 1.explanation: It is more difficult to set a loaded vehicle in motion from rest than to keep it moving. The reason is that, initially, the maximum static friction between the vehicle and the surface has to be overcome. Once the vehicle starts moving, kinetic friction becomes comparatively less. Therefore, greater force is required in the beginning to move the vehicle. Hence, option (c) is correct.

Set 1.q: 84. Match List-I with List-II: A. Night blindness B. Rickets C. Scurvy D. Beri-beri | 1. Vitamin D 2. Vitamin C 3. Vitamin B1 4. Vitamin A
Set 1.explanation: Night blindness is an eye disease or symptom. This disease is caused by a deficiency of vitamin A. Rickets is a disease of the bones, which generally occurs in children. This disease is caused by a deficiency of vitamin D. Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of vitamin C. Beriberi is a deficiency disease caused by a deficiency of vitamin B1.

Set 1.q: 85. In the context of the evolution of organisms, which one of the following sequences is correct?
Set 1.explanation: In the evolutionary sequence of organisms, this question should be understood in the broader order of vertebrate classes. Among the given options, the sequence Salamander (amphibian group) – Python (reptile group) – Kangaroo (mammal group) is correct. Therefore, option (c) is the correct answer.

Set 1.q: 86. Which of the following causes 'malnutrition'? 1. Overnutrition 2. Undernutrition 3. Imbalanced nutrition
Set 1.explanation: Malnutrition is a condition in which the body does not get the proper amount or balance of energy and nutrients. In undernutrition, the body does not get essential nutrients in sufficient quantity. In overnutrition, excess nutrients may cause obesity and other health problems. In unbalanced nutrition, even though the quantity of food is sufficient, the proportion of essential nutrients is not proper. Therefore, malnutrition can occur due to all three—1, 2 and 3.

Set 1.q: 87. Two persons cannot hear each other on the surface of the Moon because-
options: their ears stop functioning on the Moon.
there is no atmosphere on the Moon.
they wear special types of space suits on the Moon.
sound travels at a very slow speed on the Moon.
Set 1.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave, which travels through a material medium such as air, water or solids. Therefore, a material medium is necessary for the propagation of sound waves. However, since the Moon does not have an atmosphere like the Earth, there is no material medium such as air. Hence, sound waves cannot propagate on the Moon. As a result, two persons on the surface of the Moon cannot hear each other speak.

Set 1.q: 88. The study of bones falls under which branch of science?
Set 1.explanation: Osteology – Study of bones Orology – Study of mountains Serology – Scientific study of blood serum Geology – Study of the Earth, its materials and geological processes

Set 1.q: 89. Assertion (A): A diamond shines more than a glass imitation... Reason (R): The refractive index of diamond is less than the refractive index of glass.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 1.explanation: The refractive index of diamond is higher than that of glass. As a result, its critical angle becomes smaller. Therefore, total internal reflection of light takes place from its various points. This is why a diamond shines more than a glass imitation of the same shape. Thus, statement (A) is correct, while reason (R) is incorrect.

Set 1.q: 90. Match List-I with List-II: A. Plague B. AIDS C. Baldness D. Malaria | 1. Protozoa 2. Fungus 3. Virus 4. Bacterium
Set 1.explanation: Plague is a deadly infectious disease caused by the bacterium 'Pasteurella pestis' or 'Yersinia pestis'. AIDS is a fatal disease affecting the human immune system, caused by HIV. Malaria is an infectious disease caused by the protozoan parasite called 'Plasmodium', whereas baldness is caused by fungus. Therefore, the correct matching is option (d). 9 Skeâerke=âle 72JeeR mebÙegòeâ (ØeejbefYekeâ) ØeefleÙeesefielee hejer#ee रफ कार्य हेतु

Set 1.q: 91. Which one of the following elements is found in liquid form at normal temperature?
Set 1.explanation: The state of an element at normal temperature depends on its melting point and boiling point. Bromine is a non-metal found in a liquid state at normal temperature. Hydrogen and oxygen are gases at normal temperature, while iodine is a solid. Therefore, among the given options, the liquid element is bromine.

Set 1.q: 92. Match List-I (Colour) with List-II (Combination): A. Magenta B. Teal C. Mauve D. Cyan | 1. Green and Blue 2. Red and Blue 3. Blue, Green and White 4. Blue, Red and White
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching is List-I  List-II (Colour)  (Combination) Magenta - Red and Blue Teal - Blue, Green and White Mauve - Blue, Red and White Cyan - Green and Blue

Set 1.q: 93. Consider the following- 1. Bacteria 2. Fungi 3. Viruses. Which of the above can be cultured in an artificial/synthetic medium?
Set 1.explanation: Bacteria can be cultured in artificial and synthetic media. Researchers have also rewritten the DNA of the 'E. coli' bacterium. Fungi can also be cultured in artificial and synthetic media, such as Potato Dextrose Agar and Sabouraud Dextrose Agar. Due to the absence of their own metabolic machinery, viruses are difficult to culture artificially. Therefore, option (a) is correct.

Set 1.q: 94. Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: In the presence of NaCl, the rate of setting of plaster of Paris increases.
Gypsum is added to cement to slow down its rate of setting.
All alkaline earth metals form hydrated salts.
Barium and strontium are found in free state in nature.
Set 1.explanation: Barium (Ba) and strontium (Sr) are not found in a free state in nature. They belong to Group 2 of the periodic table. The elements of this group are highly reactive. As soon as they come in contact with the environment, they react and form other compounds.

Set 1.q: 95. Which one of the following is not a unit of heat?
Set 1.explanation: Heat is a form of energy. Because of a temperature difference, heat is transferred from one substance to another, and this transfer always takes place from a substance at a higher temperature to a substance at a lower temperature. Heat is measured in calories, kilocalories, joules and kilojoules. The watt (W) is the unit of power.

Set 1.q: 96. Match List-I with List-II: A. Vitamin K B. Vitamin D C. Vitamin E D. Vitamin C | 1. Wheat germ oil 2. Lemon 3. Cod-liver oil 4. Alfalfa
Set 1.explanation: The correctly matched pairs are List-I - List-II Vitamin K - Alfalfa Vitamin D - Cod liver oil Vitamin E - Wheat germ oil Vitamin C - Lemon

Set 1.q: 97. Water is a good solvent for ionic salts because-
Set 1.explanation: Ionic salts are made up of ions and dissolve in polar solvents such as water. Water is a polar solvent and has a high dipole moment. Therefore, it is also a good solvent for ionic salts.

Set 1.q: 98. Which of the following is not found in fungi?
Set 1.explanation: Chlorophyll is not found in fungi. Fungi are heterotrophic organisms. In modern classification, they are placed not in the plant kingdom but in a separate kingdom called Kingdom Fungi. However, in earlier classification, they were placed under the plant group.

Set 1.q: 99. If an apple is released from an orbiting spacecraft, it will-
options: move along with the spacecraft at the same speed.
Set 1.explanation: Due to the Earth’s gravity, the spacecraft and the apple remain in free fall/orbital motion with the same acceleration. When released, the apple also has the same orbital velocity; therefore, the apple will move along with the spacecraft at the same speed.

Set 1.q: 100. If two soap bubbles of different diameters are brought into contact with each other through a tube, what will happen?
options: The size of both bubbles will remain the same.
The smaller bubble will become smaller and the bigger bubble will become bigger.
To attain the same size, the smaller bubble will become bigger and the bigger bubble will become smaller.
Both bubbles will burst as soon as they come into contact.
Set 1.explanation: The difference between the pressure inside and outside a soap bubble depends on surface tension and the radius of the bubble. The gas pressure inside a small bubble is higher than that inside a large bubble. Therefore, when they are brought in contact with each other through a tube, the small bubble will become smaller, while the large bubble will become larger.

Set 1.q: 101. Which one of the following types of waves is used in night vision devices?
Set 1.explanation: Infrared waves are a type of electromagnetic wave. Their wavelengths are longer than those of visible light. In night vision devices, especially in thermal imaging, infrared radiation emitted by humans and other warm objects is detected to see in the dark.

Set 1.q: 102. Match the following- (A) Joule (B) Ampere (C) Watt (D) Volt | 1. Current 2. Power 3. Work 4. Potential difference
Set 1.explanation: The joule is the unit of work. The ampere, watt and volt are the units of electric current, power and potential difference, respectively.

Set 1.q: 103. The founder of the Bihar Socialist Party was-
Set 1.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan is considered the founder of the Bihar Socialist Party. He played an important role in organizing the socialist movement in Bihar. Later, he became a prominent leader of the Indian socialist movement and the Total Revolution movement.

Set 1.q: 104. Who was the first Governor of Bihar after Independence?
Set 1.explanation: The first post Independence Governor of Bihar was Jairamdas Daulatram, whose tenure was from 15 August 1947 to 11 January 1948. Thereafter, Madhav Shrihari Aney was the second Governor of Bihar from 12 January 1948 to 14 June 1952.

Set 1.q: 105. Which of the following districts does not have the Dharwar geological structure?
Set 1.explanation: The districts of Bihar having Dharwar geological formations fall under south-eastern Bihar. These include Munger, Nawada and Jamui districts. Rohtas, on the other hand, is a part of south western Bihar. Vindhyan-type geological formations are found in this region. In Bihar, Vindhyan geological formations are found in the Kaimur and Son River Valley region of Rohtas.

Set 1.q: 106. According to the Bihar Budget 2026-27, the highest amount was allocated to-
Set 1.explanation: In the department wise Annual Scheme Outlay of the Bihar Budget 2026–27, ₹22,392.47 crore was allocated to the Rural Development Department. In comparison, ₹18,351.48 crore was allocated to the Education Department and ₹10,033.27 crore to the Health Department.

Set 1.q: 107. The secretary of the Bihar Socialist Party, formed in the year 1934, was-
Set 1.explanation: The first All India Congress Socialist Conference was organized by the Bihar Socialist Party in Patna in May 1934 and was convened by Jayaprakash Narayan. This conference was presided over by Acharya Narendra Dev. The first annual session of the Congress Socialist Party was held in Bombay in October 1934 under the chairmanship of Sampurnanand. In this meeting, the National Executive of the Congress Socialist Party was formed, and Jayaprakash Narayan was its General Secretary.

Set 1.q: 108. In the year 2026, the Directorate of Horticulture... received the Golden Peacock... Award for outstanding work in which area?
options: For the overall development of the Makhana value chain
Set 1.explanation: On 4 April 2026, it was announced that the Directorate of Horticulture, Department of Agriculture, Government of Bihar, would be honoured with the Golden Peacock Innovative Product/ Service Award 2026 for the holistic development of the makhana value chain. This award is given by the Institute of Directors (IOD).

Set 1.q: 109. The first account of Bakhtiyar Khilji's attack on Bihar is found in-
Set 1.explanation: Bakhtiyar Khilji was a Turkish Muslim invader. Under his leadership, Muslim invaders destroyed Nalanda University in 1193 AD. The famous Persian historian Minhaj-us-Siraj has described his invasions of Bihar in detail in his book Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

Set 1.q: 110. Among the following, which State/Union Territory in India has the maximum proportion of its geographical area under forest cover?
Set 1.explanation: According to ISFR 2023, the top three states/Union Territories of India in terms of the highest percentage of forest cover with respect to geographical area are as follows: Lakshadweep (91.33%), Mizoram (85.34%) and Andaman and Nicobar Islands (81.62%).

Set 1.q: 111. The greenhouse effect is the process-
options: in which a uniform temperature is obtained for growing plants.
in which the temperature of the atmosphere increases due to the absorption of infrared radiation by greenhouse gases.
in which barren mountains or hills are made green.
in which the colour of deep water appears green.
Set 1.explanation: Earth continuously emits long-wave infrared radiation, but carbon dioxide, chlorofluorocarbons, nitrous oxide, water vapour, methane and other greenhouse gases present in the atmosphere absorb part of this terrestrial infrared radiation and re emit it in all directions. Part of this radiation escapes into space, while some of it returns towards Earth’s surface. Due to this, extra heat gets accumulated in the lower part of the atmosphere and on Earth’s surface. This is known as the greenhouse effect.

Set 1.q: 112. Which of the following is not an in-situ method of plant conservation?
Set 1.explanation: For plant conservation, botanical gardens do not come under the in-situ method; they come under the ex-situ method. On the other hand, biosphere reserves, national parks and wildlife sanctuaries come under the in-situ method.

Set 1.q: 113. Match List-I (SDGs) with List-II (Related to): A. SDG-10 B. SDG-11 C. SDG-12 D. SDG-16 | 1. Sustainable Cities 2. Reduced Inequalities 3. Responsible Consumption 4. Peace, Justice
Set 1.explanation: The correct matching is as follows SDG - 10 – Reduced Inequalities SDG - 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities SDG - 12 – Responsible Consumption and Production SDG - 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

Set 1.q: 114. With reference to UNESCO's 'Creative Cities Network' (UCCN), consider the following statements: 1- Lucknow city... was included as a 'Creative City of Gastronomy'. 2- The official announcement was made at UNESCO's 43rd General Conference...
Set 1.explanation: The UNESCO Creative Cities Network, i.e., the UCCN, is a global network of cities that make culture and creativity the basis of sustainable urban development. In 2025, UNESCO included 58 new cities in this network. In this sequence, Lucknow was designated as a “Creative City of Gastronomy” in the Gastronomy category. This announcement was made on 31 October 2025 in the context of the 43rd General Conference of UNESCO held in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Thus, both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct.

Set 1.q: 115. Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the country's first government hospital-based 'AI Clinic' established in Greater Noida?
options: It was established at the Government Institute of Medical Sciences (GIMS).
It also became Uttar Pradesh's first public hospital-based medical incubator centre.
Technical support for this project was provided only by IIT Kanpur.
Its main focus was on clinical AI, medical imaging and data privacy.
Set 1.explanation: The country’s first government hospital-based AI clinic was established in January 2026 at the Government Institute of Medical Sciences, Greater Noida. Its objective is to test and validate AI based health technologies directly in the real-world clinical environment of a government hospital. Option (c) is incorrect, because institutions like IIT Madras and IIIT Lucknow are also involved in this initiative along with IIT Kanpur. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 1.q: 116. What was the official name of India's first fully solar-powered mobile ATM van launched by Tripura Gramin Bank (TGB)?
Set 1.explanation: “TGB on Wheels” is Tripura Gramin Bank’s solar powered mobile ATM and banking van initiative. Its objective is to provide banking services to rural and remote areas where access to a regular bank branch or ATM is difficult. Through this van, basic banking services along with ATM facility can also be provided. The importance of this initiative is not limited only to digital banking. It is a good example of green energy, rural financial inclusion and last-mile banking connectivity.

Set 1.q: 117. With reference to the 'Indusfood 2026' exhibition... consider the following statements: 1- It was the ninth edition... held in Greater Noida. 2- A major attraction... was the launch of the 'India-UAE Food Corridor'.
Set 1.explanation: Indusfood 2026 was the 9th edition of India’s flagship global food and beverage sourcing exhibition. It was organised by the Trade Promotion Council of India (TPCI) from 8 to 10 January 2026 at the India Expo Centre & Mart, Greater Noida. The event was associated with strengthening India’s food processing sector, food exports, and India’s role in the global food supply chain. The India–UAE Food Corridor initiative was one of the major attractions of this exhibition. This initiative was led by the Abu Dhabi Food Hub, and its objective was to strengthen food security, logistics, supply chains, and bilateral food trade between India and the UAE. Therefore, both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct.

Set 1.q: 118. Which film by filmmaker Subodh Khanolkar became the first Marathi film in history to be included in the preliminary-stage 'Contention List' of the Oscars?
Set 1.explanation: Filmmaker Subodh Khanolkar’s Marathi film 'Dashavatar' was in the news because it was included in the Academy’s Reminder List of productions eligible for the 98th Academy Awards, commonly referred to as the Oscar contention list. It was considered an important achievement for Marathi cinema, as it became the first Marathi film to reach this stage. It is important to note that inclusion in the contention list does not mean an Oscar nomination. It means that the film had fulfilled the Academy’s eligibility conditions and had entered the list of films under consideration for nominations.

Set 1.q: 119. What was the name of the Indian regional film in the Manipuri language that gained global recognition by being nominated in the 'Children's & Family Film' category at BAFTA?
Set 1.explanation: 'Boong' is a Manipuri language Indian film directed by Lakshmipriya Devi. The film received a nomination in the Children’s & Family Film category at the 2026 BAFTA Film Awards and later won in the same category. This achievement is significant because it brought special recognition to the Manipuri language and the regional cinema of Northeast India on the global stage.

Set 1.q: 120. Kaamya Karthikeyan was on a quest to achieve the distinction of becoming the youngest person to complete the 'Explorers Grand Slam'. Which conditions are mandatory?
options: Climbing the highest peak of each of the seven continents and swimming across seven deep oceans.
Climbing the highest peak of each of the seven continents and skiing to both the North and South Poles.
Completing the climb of Mount Everest from both the Nepal and China sides.
Trekking to the North Pole, the South Pole and the three main peaks of the Himalayas.
Set 1.explanation: The Explorers Grand Slam is considered one of the toughest challenges in adventure expeditions. To complete it, an adventurer or mountaineer has to accomplish two major goals. First, the Seven Summits, that is, climbing the highest peaks of all seven continents of the world. Second, reaching the North Pole and the South Pole by skiing or through polar expeditions.

Set 1.q: 121. As a step towards improving administrative convenience, which state government announced the formation of a new third district named 'Kushavati' carving it out of South Goa?
Set 1.explanation: The Government of Goa notified a new district named ‘Kushavati’ through a Revenue Department notification dated 31 December 2025. Before this notification, Goa had two districts— North Goa and South Goa. The new Kushavati district was formed by combining the Dharbandora, Sanguem, Quepem, and Canacona talukas of the erstwhile South Goa district. The district headquarters is Quepem. The district has been named after the Kushavati River, which flows through the region.

Set 1.q: 122. With reference to the administrative history of Odisha, consider the following statements: 1- Anu Garg... was appointed as the first woman Chief Secretary. 2- She succeeded Manoj Ahuja...
Set 1.explanation: Anu Garg is a 1991-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre. She was appointed Chief Secretary of Odisha and became the first woman to hold this post in the state. This was considered an important achievement in the administrative history of Odisha. She succeeded Manoj Ahuja, who retired on 31 December 2025. Therefore, both the given statements are correct.

Set 1.q: 123. With reference to the complete digitisation of judicial systems in India, consider...: 1- In Jan 2026, Kalpetta District Court was declared India's first fully paperless court. 2- Kerala High Court had already achieved the distinction...
Set 1.explanation: Kerala has played an important role in judicial digitisation in India. In January 2026, the Kalpetta Judicial District in Wayanad, Kerala, became India’s first district judiciary to adopt a completely paperless system. This means that the entire process, from e-filing of cases, digital scrutiny of documents, and case management to final orders, is conducted through digital means. The foundation of this system is the District Court Case Management System (DCMS), developed by the IT Directorate of the Kerala High Court. This is an important step towards making judicial proceedings more transparent, faster, and environment friendly.

Set 1.q: 124. Which statement is correct with reference to the appointment of Praveen Vashista as the new Vigilance Commissioner in the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)?
options: He was appointed by the Prime Minister of India under the CVC Act, 2003.
Praveen Vashista was a 1991-batch IPS officer of the Bihar cadre.
The Vigilance Commissioner is appointed by the President under Section 5(2) of the Central Vigilance Commission Act.
After taking oath, his tenure is fixed for a period of 6 years.
Set 1.explanation: Praveen Vashista was appointed as Vigilance Commissioner in the Central Vigilance Commission. His appointment was made by the President of India under Section 4(1) of the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003. He took the oath of office on 16 January 2026. Praveen Vashista is a 1991-batch Indian Police Service officer of the Bihar cadre. An important fact to remember is that the Central Vigilance Commission consists of one Central Vigilance Commissioner and a maximum of two Vigilance Commissioners. The tenure of a Vigilance Commissioner is not six years; rather, it is four years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. Therefore, the correct answer to this question is option (b).

Set 1.q: 125. Consider the following statements with reference to the meeting of the 16th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting (ADMM)-Plus Experts Working Group...: 1- This three-day strategic meeting was held in New Delhi... 2- This international meeting was jointly co-chaired by India and Malaysia.
Set 1.explanation: The Meeting of the 16th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus Experts Working Group on Counter Terrorism and the Final Planning Conference for Table Top Exercise was held in New Delhi from 14 to 16 January 2026. Its main subject was counter-terrorism cooperation. The meeting was co chaired by India and Malaysia. It was the third meeting of the 2024–2027 cycle, in which representatives from 11 ASEAN members, 7 dialogue partners, and the ASEAN Secretariat participated. Hence, both Statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Set 1.q: 126. Which of the following is the correct code regarding the 'Second Global Buddhist Summit'? 1- Organised on 24-25 January 2026 at Bharat Mandapam. 2- Organised by IBC in collaboration with Ministry of Home Affairs. 3- Main objective was to initiate dialogue...
Set 1.explanation: The Second Global Buddhist Summit was held on 24–25 January 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The theme of this summit was “Collective Wisdom, United Voice, and Mutual Coexistence”. It was organised by the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, and not in collaboration with the Ministry of Home Affairs. Therefore, Statement 2 is incorrect. The objective of this summit was to promote dialogue on contemporary and future global challenges through Buddhist philosophy. Hence, Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 1.q: 127. Which statement is incorrect with reference to the 'inaugural India International Conference on Democracy and Election Management' (IICDEM-2026)?
options: It was held for three days at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
It was organised by the India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM).
Only representatives from South Asian (SAARC) countries participated in this global conference.
During the conference, the documentary titled 'India Decides'... was showcased.
Set 1.explanation: Statement (c) is incorrect. Participation in IICDEM-2026 was not limited only to South Asian or SAARC countries. It was the inaugural and largest global conference of its kind hosted by India in the field of democracy and election management, in which nearly 100 international delegates from more than 70 countries participated. The conference also saw the participation of 42 Election Management Bodies, foreign missions, and national and international experts. It was held from 21 to 23 January 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, and was organised by IIIDEM. Excerpts from the docuseries titled “India Decides” were also screened during the conference.

Set 1.q: 128. Who released the book 'Chalice of Ambrosia: Ram Janmabhoomi - Challenge and Response', authored by Surendra Kumar Pachauri?
options: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath
Set 1.explanation: The book “Chalice of Ambrosia: Ram Janmabhoomi – Challenge and Response”, written by former Secretary to the Government of India Shri Surendra Kumar Pachauri, was released by Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan at the Vice President’s Enclave in New Delhi. This book presents the historical, legal, and civilisational aspects of the Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

Set 1.q: 129. Consider the following statements with reference to the regulatory process for Bulgaria's accession to the euro area as its 21st member: 1- Bulgaria adopted the euro as its official currency from 1 January 2026. 2- Under the Smooth Transition period...
Set 1.explanation: Bulgaria adopted the euro as its official currency from 1 January 2026 and became the 21st member of the euro area. Therefore, Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the parallel cash circulation of the lev and the euro in Bulgaria was only from 1 January to 31 January 2026. From 1 February 2026, euro banknotes and coins became the only legal tender in the country. Bulgaria joined the European Union on 1 January 2007.

Set 1.q: 130. Consider the following statements with reference to the country that assumed the 'rotating Presidency of the Council of the European Union' in January 2026: 1- Cyprus assumed the Presidency... 2- This was the first time in the history of Cyprus...
Set 1.explanation: Cyprus assumed the rotating presidency of the Council of the European Union for six months from 1 January 2026 to 30 June 2026. Therefore, Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because this was not Cyprus’s first presidency, but its second presidency. Cyprus became a member of the European Union in 2004 and had held the presidency of the Council of the EU for the first time from 1 July 2012 to 31 December 2012. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 1.q: 131. What was the historical background of 'Dev's Law', related to road safety, recently pledged by the UK Government?
options: It was made in honour of Dev Patel, a British minister.
It was introduced in memory of 'Dev Naran', an 8-year-old child of Indian origin who died in a road accident.
This law was brought only to set the speed limit for autonomous cars.
Under this law, the complete ban on drunk driving in Britain was abolished.
Set 1.explanation: ‘Dev’s Law’ is named in memory of Dev Naran, an 8-year old boy of Indian origin who died in a road accident in 2018 on the M6 motorway near Birmingham in the United Kingdom. After this, Dev Naran’s mother, Meera Naran, campaigned for road-safety reforms, especially for making safety technologies such as Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB) mandatory in new vehicles.

Set 1.q: 132. In January 2026, who formally became the 27th U.S. Ambassador to India after having previously served as Assistant to the President...?
Set 1.explanation: Sergio Gor became the 27th Ambassador of the United States to India. He was nominated by President Donald Trump in 2025 as the U.S. Ambassador to India, and the U.S. Senate confirmed his appointment in October 2025. In January 2026, he began his duties as ambassador in New Delhi and presented his credentials to President Droupadi Murmu on 14 January

Set 1.q: 133. For the first time in the 1,400-year history of the Church of England, which woman was appointed to its highest spiritual office, the 'Archbishop of Canterbury'?
Set 1.explanation: Sarah Mullally is the first woman in the history of the Church of England to become the Archbishop of Canterbury. This is a very important and senior religious position in the Church of England. She was chosen as the 106th Archbishop of Canterbury. Her nomination was announced in October 2025, and on 28 January 2026, she legally became the 106th Archbishop of Canterbury. It is important to note that she was not the first woman bishop of the Church of England; she is the first woman to become the Archbishop of Canterbury.

Set 1.q: 134. Consider the following statements regarding granting legal rights to the 'native stingless bees of the Peruvian Amazon': 1- They became the world's first insects to be granted legal rights... 2- According to the ordinance... these bees were responsible for pollinating more than 80% of Amazonian flora.
Set 1.explanation: Satipo Municipality, Peru, took an important step in the field of biodiversity conservation by granting legal rights to the native stingless bees of the Amazon region. This step is related to the concept of “Rights of Nature”, under which nature or natural entities are regarded not merely as resources, but as rights-bearing entities. These bees and their habitat were granted rights such as the right to exist, to maintain healthy populations, to have a pollution-free habitat, to have stable climatic conditions, to regenerate natural cycles, and to have legal representation. Set 1.q: 135. Which scientist, an eminent environmentalist of India and former Chair of the 'Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel' (WGEEP), died on January 7, 2026, at the age of 83?
Set 1.explanation: Professor Madhav Gadgil was one of India’s leading ecologists and environmental thinkers. He passed away on 7 January 2026 in Pune. He was the chairman of the Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel (WGEEP), constituted in 2010, which is also known as the Gadgil Committee. In 2024, he was honoured with UNEP’s Champions of the Earth award in the Lifetime Achievement category.

Set 1.q: 136. Demonstrating its forward-looking approach in the field of wildlife conservation, the Kerala Government declared which wildlife sanctuary as 'Kerala's first dedicated butterfly sanctuary'?
Set 1.explanation: The Kerala Government renamed the Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary, located in Kannur district, the Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary. After the recommendation of the State Wildlife Board, it was declared Kerala’s first dedicated butterfly sanctuary. The notification for the renaming was published on 26 December 2025.

Set 1.q: 137. American evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers was awarded the 'Tyler Prize'... for which groundbreaking scientific research?
options: For research on the migration patterns of insects in Amazonian forests.
For research on underground mycorrhizal networks and carbon sequestration.
For the genetic modification of global pineapple crops.
For the development of open-sea cage technology in marine fish farming.
Set 1.explanation: Toby Kiers was awarded the 2026 Tyler Prize for her significant research on underground mycorrhizal networks. Mycorrhizal networks are underground systems formed through symbiotic relationships between plant roots and fungi. These networks help provide nutrients and water to plants and also play a role in transferring carbon fixed by plants to the soil and fungal mycelium.

Set 1.q: 138. Under a bioscience-based public awareness policy, which bacterium was declared India's first official 'State Microbe' by the Kerala Government?
Set 1.explanation: Kerala became the first state in India to officially declare a microorganism as its “State Microbe”. The Kerala Government declared 'Bacillus subtilis' as the State Microbe. 'Bacillus subtilis' is found in soil, water, foods, and in the intestines of humans and animals. It is considered useful in areas such as health due to its probiotic properties, agriculture for plant growth and biocontrol, and industrial applications and bioremediation.

Set 1.q: 139. With reference to 'International Zebra Day', observed every year on January 31, which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched? 1- Grevy's zebra - Dry regions of Kenya and Ethiopia 2- Mountain zebra - Mountainous regions... 3- Plains zebra The most common and widespread species
Set 1.explanation: International Zebra Day is observed on January 31 to raise awareness about zebra conservation, habitat loss, and declining populations. Three major living species of zebra are recognized– Grevy’s zebra, mountain zebra, and plains zebra. Grevy’s zebra is mainly found in the semi-arid and arid regions of Ethiopia and northern Kenya. Mountain zebra is associated with the mountainous and rocky regions of Namibia, South Africa, and southwestern Angola. Plains zebra is the most common and widely distributed species. Therefore, all three pairs are correctly matched. Several scientific explanations have been given for zebra stripes.

Set 1.q: 140. India ranked 16th among 154 countries in the 'Responsible Nations Index (RNI) 2026'. This index was mainly based on which three dimensions?
options: GDP growth, per capita income and military power
Internal responsibility, environmental responsibility and external/global responsibility
Literacy rate, gender equality and health infrastructure
Foreign direct investment, export capacity and technological innovation
Set 1.explanation: The objective of the Responsible Nations Index (RNI) 2026 is to assess countries not merely on the basis of economic power, military capability, or GDP, but on the basis of “responsible national conduct.” This index is based on three core pillars of responsibility. First, internal responsibility, which includes citizens’ welfare, dignity, governance, justice, and basic services. Second, environmental responsibility, which covers aspects related to climate action, environmental protection, and sustainable development. Third, external/global responsibility, in which contributions to international peace, multilateral cooperation, and global public interests are evaluated. In RNI 2026, 154 countries were assessed. Singapore ranked first, while India ranked 16th. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 2.q: 1. In which field did Todar Mal earn fame?
Set 2.explanation: Todar Mal had earned fame in the field of land revenue. In the 24th year of Akbar’s reign (1580 A.D.), Akbar introduced a new revenue system called Ain-i-Dahsala (Todar Mal Settlement), giving the Mughal-period revenue system a standardized/organized form. The real originator of this system was Todar Mal. For this reason, it is also called the ‘Todar Mal Settlement’. At that time, Todar Mal was the revenue minister. Under this system, the average production of different crops during the previous ten years and their prevailing prices during the same period were calculated. One third of this average produce was considered the share of the state. The state’s revenue demand was fixed not in the form of grain but in cash.

Set 2.q: 5. Match List-I with List-II: A. Indian Association B. Poona Sarvajanik Sabha C. Bombay Presidency Association D. Madras Mahajan Sabha | 1. Ananda Charlu 2. Surendranath Banerjee 3. Mahadev Govind Ranade 4. Pherozeshah Mehta
6. Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: Battle of Buxar - Clive against Mir Jafar
Battle of Wandiwash - East India Company against the French
Battle of Chillianwala - Marathas against Dalhousie
Battle of Kharda - East India Company against the Nizam
Set 2.explanation: The Battle of Buxar was fought on October 22/23, 1764, between the combined forces of Shuja-ud-Daula, the Nawab of Awadh, the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam, and Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Bengal, and the British. The Battle of Wandiwash was fought on January 22, 1760, between the British and the French. In this battle, the French were defeated. The Battle of Chillianwala was fought on January 13, 1849. In this battle, the British army was led by Lord Gough, and the Sikh army fought under the leadership of Sher Singh. This battle ended without a decisive result. At the time of this battle, the Governor-General of India was Lord Dalhousie. The Battle of Kharda was fought in 1795 A.D. by the Marathas against the Nizam of Hyderabad, in which the Nizam was defeated. Therefore, it is clear that only pair (b) is correctly matched.

Set 2.q: 7. Consider the following statements- (1) In the Third Battle of Panipat, Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated Ibrahim Lodi. (2) Tipu Sultan died in the Third Anglo-Mysore War. (3) Mir Jafar conspired with the English for the defeat of Siraj-ud-Daulah...
Set 2.explanation: On January 14, 1761, in the Third Battle of Panipat, Ahmad Shah Abdali severely defeated the Maratha army led by Sadashiv Rao Bhau. According to J. N. Sarkar, there was hardly any family in Maharashtra that had not lost one relative or another, and some families were completely ruined. In the Third Anglo-Mysore War fought during 1790-92 A.D., Tipu Sultan was only defeated; he did not die. His death occurred during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799 A.D.). The war ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam. Tipu died in 1799 A.D. in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War. In the Battle of Plassey (1757 A.D.), Mir Jafar conspired with the British against Siraj-ud-Daulah. Among the other conspirators, the banker Jagat Seth, Rai Durlabh and Amin Chand (also found as Amichand) were prominent. Therefore, only the third statement is true.

Set 2.q: 9. Which of the following statements gives the correct definition of the Drain Theory propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji?
options: The resources of the country were being used in the interest of Britain.
A part of India's national wealth... was exported to Britain, for which India did not receive any real return.
Under the protection of imperial power, British industrialists were given opportunities to invest in India.
British goods were imported into India and thus the country was made poorer day by day.
Set 2.explanation: The nationalist definition of the outflow or drain of wealth meant the transfer of wealth, property and goods from India to England, in return for which India did not receive any equivalent economic, commercial or material benefit. Under the ‘Drain Theory’, emphasis was laid on these unrequited exports. Dadabhai Naoroji was the most prominent propounder of the theory of the Drain of Wealth. He presented his Drain Theory through his writings and books/pamphlets/papers—Poverty and Un-British Rule in India, The Wants and Means of India and On the Commerce of India.

Set 2.q: 10. During the reign of the Chola rulers, which of the following Variyams looked after the administration of gardens?
Set 2.explanation: In the village administration of the Chola period, ‘Variyam’ referred to the special committees that worked under the village assembly. These committees administered different areas of local administration. The committee that looked after garden management was called ‘Totta Variyam’, while Samvatsara Variyam was called the Annual Committee, Eri Variyam the Tank Committee, and Pon Variyam the Gold Committee.

Set 2.q: 11. Consider the following statements regarding the features of Buddhist philosophy: 1. The basic element of Buddhist philosophy is found in the teachings of Gautama Buddha. 2. Instead of getting entangled in philosophical problems, Buddha always emphasized living a moral life...
Set 2.explanation: The main objective of Buddhist philosophy is to show the practical path to liberation from human suffering. Its basic foundation is the teachings of Gautama Buddha. Mahatma Buddha propounded the Four Noble Truths related to suffering and its solution. In the Four Noble Truths, craving is considered the cause of suffering, and the Eightfold Path has been prescribed for the cessation of suffering. Instead of getting entangled in philosophical problems, Buddha always emphasized moral life, the Middle Path and self effort for liberation from human suffering. Buddha wanted to lead humanity towards liberation.

Set 2.q: 12. Information about the guild of silk weavers is obtained from which of the following inscriptions?
Set 2.explanation: Explanation: The Dashapura (Mandsaur) inscription is related to the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I and Bandhuvarman. Bandhuvarman, mentioned in this inscription, was the local ruler/feudatory of Dashapura. This inscription mentions a guild of silk weavers, which built a Sun temple at Dashapura.

Set 2.q: 13. Who was the President of the Congress when India became independent?
Set 2.explanation: The President of the Indian National Congress was, at that time, the chief office-bearer of the Congress organization. When India became independent on August 15, 1947, the President of the Congress was Acharya J. B. Kripalani. He had become the President of the Congress at the Meerut Session of 1946 A.D.

Set 2.q: 14. Arrange the following foreign travellers in chronological order of their arrival in India- 1. William Hawkins 2. Ralph Fitch 3. Sir Thomas Roe 4. Nicholas Downton
Set 2.explanation: William Hawkins reached Surat in August 1608 aboard the East India Company’s ship Hector and reached the court of Mughal ruler Jahangir at Agra in April 1609. Ralph Fitch was one of the important early English travellers/traders who came to India. He reached Goa in 1583 AD. Sir Thomas Roe was the ambassador of King James I of England. He reached Surat in September 1615. Nicholas Downton came to India in 1614–15.

Set 2.q: 15. Which of the following kings issued some coins bearing the figures of Rama and Sita and the Devanagari legend 'Ram-Siya'?
Set 2.explanation: In the last years of his reign, around 1604–05 AD, Akbar issued rare coins bearing the figures of Rama and Sita. The inscription “Ramsiya Ram Siya” was written on these coins in Devanagari. On these coins, Rama is shown with a bow and arrow, and Siya or Sita is shown behind him.

Set 2.q: 16. Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched? (Traveller - Country)
Set 2.explanation: Ibn Battuta was a traveller from Morocco. He came to India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325–51 AD). Marco Polo was a famous traveller from Venice, Italy. He came to India during the time of the Pandya ruler Maravarman Kulasekhara (1268–1310 AD). The Iranian ambassador Abdur Razzaq came to Vijayanagara during the reign of Devaraya II (1422–46 AD). Nuniz was a Portuguese traveller and horse trader. He also visited Vijayanagara.

Set 2.q: 17. Whom did Rajendra Prasad consider the father of Pakistan?
Set 2.explanation: In his book India Divided, Rajendra Prasad held Lord Minto responsible for promoting the system of separate electorates and communal policy in India. This policy later paved the way for the partition of India. Therefore, according to the given options, option (c) is the correct answer. However, it should be kept in mind that there is no established source to prove that Rajendra Prasad explicitly called Lord Minto the “father of Pakistan”. A direct mention of Lord Minto being called the “father of Pakistan” is found in Shriman Narayan Agarwal’s book Gandhian Constitution for Free India.

Set 2.q: 18. Which of the following was/were associated with the introduction of the Ryotwari Settlement in India during British rule? 1. Lord Cornwallis 2. Alexander Read 3. Thomas Munro
Set 2.explanation: The Ryotwari settlement was a system introduced by the British in India for the collection it was useful in trade credit and remittance.

Set 2.q: 19. Consider the following statements- 1. Saint Nimbarka was a contemporary of Akbar. 2. Saint Kabir was greatly influenced by Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi.
Set 2.explanation: There is a difference of opinion among scholars regarding the period of Nimbarkacharya. Some standard sources place him in the 12th–13th century, while some consider him a contemporary of Ramanujacharya, and some place him after Ramanujacharya. Therefore, Nimbarkacharya was not a contemporary of the Mughal emperor Akbar, whose reign was from 1556 to 1605 AD. On the other hand, Kabir is generally considered a saint-poet of the 14th–15th century. Although his period is disputed, it is generally considered to be from 1398 to 1518 AD. Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi lived in the 16th–17th century, approximately from 1564 to 1624 AD. Hence, both the given statements are false.

Set 2.q: 20. The province where the Indian National Congress did not form its government after the general elections of 1937 was-
Set 2.explanation: In July 1937, the Indian National Congress formed its ministries in six provinces. These provinces were Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar and the United Provinces. Later, Congress also formed coalition ministries with other allies in the North-West Frontier Province and Assam. A Congress government was not formed in Bengal. There, the Krishak Praja Party led by Fazlul Huq formed the government with the support of the Muslim League.

Set 2.q: 21. Jaita and Kumpa, who impressed Sher Shah with their bravery, belonged to which place?
Set 2.explanation: Jaita and Kumpa, who impressed Sher Shah with their bravery, belonged to Marwar. They were chiefs of Maldeo Rathore, the ruler of Marwar. Being impressed by the courage and valour of the Rajputs in the battle of Marwar, Sher Shah said, “I would have lost the empire of Hindustan for a handful of millet.”

Set 2.q: 22. Which of the following statements defines the nature of 'Hundi', frequently mentioned in post-Harsha period sources?
options: Advice given by the king to his subordinates
An order given by a feudal lord to his subordinates
Set 2.explanation: Hundi was a traditional written instrument of the Indian commercial and credit system. In the commercial context of the post Harsha/medieval period, its main meaning was a bill of exchange. Through this, a person or trader could receive payment at another place without carrying cash. Therefore, Battle of Daurah – 1532 AD Battle of Chausa – 1539 AD Battle of Kannauj – 1540 AD Battle of Samugarh – 1658 AD Therefore, it is clear that the required answer will be option (b).

Set 2.q: 23. Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order. 1. Battle of Daurah 2. Battle of Kannauj 3. Battle of Samugarh 4. Battle of Chausa
Set 2.explanation: The events given in the question are in the following chronological order— of land revenue. Alexander Read first introduced the Ryotwari system in 1792 in the Baramahal region of Tamil Nadu in the Madras Presidency. In 1820, when Thomas Munro became the Governor of Madras, he implemented it in the Madras Presidency. Munro’s disciple Elphinstone implemented it in the Bombay Presidency. This system was implemented in about 51 percent of the total area of British India, including Madras, some parts of Bombay, Assam, Coorg, etc.

Set 2.q: 24. Consider the following events- 1. Indigo Revolt 2. Santhal Rebellion 3. Deccan Riots 4. Sepoy Mutiny. The correct chronological order is-
Set 2.explanation: The sequence of the revolts given in the question is as follows— Santhal Rebellion – 1855–56 Sepoy Revolt – 1857 Indigo Revolt – 1859–60 Deccan Riots – 1875

Set 2.q: 25. Assertion (A): In 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its acceptance of the 'Cabinet Mission Plan'. Reason (R): The Muslim League joined the Interim Government formed in 1946.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 2.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan was accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League with great reluctance. The Congress was unhappy with the grouping of provinces, while the League was unhappy because Pakistan was not accepted. On 10 July 1946, Nehru said that grouping was not compulsory and that Assam and the North West Frontier Province, belonging to Groups C and B respectively, could refuse to join their groups. After this, the Muslim League rejected the Cabinet Mission Plan and adopted a resolution for Direct Action. Later, the Viceroy invited Jawaharlal Nehru of the Congress to form the Interim Government. The Muslim League was also asked to join it, but it refused. However, later, when the Viceroy again suggested it, the League accepted through its resolution of October 1946 to join the Interim Government in order to protect the interests of Muslims. Thus, it is clear that both the Assertion and the Reason are true, but the Reason does not explain the Assertion. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 2.q: 26. Which of the following edicts of Ashoka is fully dedicated to religious tolerance?
Set 2.explanation: In Ashoka’s Major Rock Edict XII, the growth of the essential values of all religious sects has been desired, and the measures to be followed for religious tolerance have been mentioned. In this edict, Ashoka said that a person should not excessively praise his own sect and condemn other sects. Doing so harms one’s own sect and increases disrespect towards other sects.

Set 2.q: 27. Rangpur, where a civilization contemporary with the Harappan civilization existed, is located in-
Set 2.explanation: Rangpur is located in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat. Evidence of pre-Harappan, Harappan and post-Harappan civilizations has been found here.

Set 2.q: 28. Identify the two major currencies of the Sultanate period using the following codes- 1. Dam 2. Jital 3. Rupiya 4. Tanka
Set 2.explanation: The two major coins of the Sultanate period were the jital and the tanka. Iltutmish was the first Turkish ruler of the Delhi Sultanate who issued coins bearing purely Arabic inscriptions. His contribution to the currency system was the greatest among the rulers of the Delhi Sultanate, because he introduced two major coins, namely the silver tanka and the copper jital. Shashgani was also a silver coin.

Set 2.q: 29. The Sufi saint who believed that devotional music is a means of reaching closer to God is-
Set 2.explanation: The credit for spreading the Chishti order in India goes to Sheikh Muinuddin Chishti. In Sufi practice, sama was the tradition of remembering God through spiritual music and mystical singing. The Chishtis believed that sama, or music, was a means of reaching closer to God.

Set 2.q: 30. Match List-I (Tirthankara) with List-II (Their Emblems): A. Parshvanatha B. Adinatha C. Mahavira D. Shantinatha | (i) Bull (ii) Lion (iii) Serpent (iv) Deer
Set 2.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— List-I – List-II (Tirthankaras) – (Their symbols) Parshvanatha – Serpent Adinatha Mahavira Shantinatha

Set 2.q: 31. The image of Lord Buddha is sometimes shown with a hand gesture called the 'Bhumisparsha Mudra'. What does it symbolize?
options: Buddha's calling upon the earth to watch over Mara...
Buddha's calling upon the earth to bear witness to his purity and chastity despite Mara's temptations.
Buddha's reminding his followers that all of them arise from the earth...
In this context, both statements (a) and (b) are correct.
Set 2.explanation: –  –  – Bull Lion Deer Buddha’s ‘Bhumisparsha Mudra’ means maintaining the purity and continuity of his austerity. Buddha’s ‘Bhumisparsha Mudra’ represents Buddha’s invocation of the earth to witness his purity despite the temptations of Mara (Kamadeva). Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 2.q: 32. Match the following- A. Panini B. Vatsyayana C. Chanakya D. Kalhana | 1. Kamasutra 2. Rajatarangini 3. Ashtadhyayi 4. Arthashastra
Set 2.explanation: The author of ‘Ashtadhyayi’ was the grammarian Panini. Ashtadhyayi is his famous work. The author of ‘Kamasutra’ was Vatsyayana. Chanakya, the Prime Minister of Chandragupta Maurya, wrote the famous treatise on political science, ‘Arthashastra’. Kalhana wrote the history of Kashmir in ‘Rajatarangini’.

Set 2.q: 33. Consider the following statements with reference to the PM SVANidhi Scheme- 1. This scheme was launched on June 1, 2020. 2. In August 2025, its lending period was extended up to March 31, 2030. 3. This scheme was launched to provide collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors.
Set 2.explanation: The PM SVANidhi Scheme is a micro-credit scheme launched to provide collateral-free working capital loans to urban street vendors. Statement 1 is correct because the PM SVANidhi Scheme was launched on June 1, 2020. Statement 2 is correct because in August 2025, approval was given to extend the lending period under this scheme up to March 31, 2030. Statement 3 is also correct because the objective of this scheme is to provide collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors to run or restart their businesses. Hence, all three statements are correct. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 2.q: 34. A 'closed economy' is an economy in which-
options: the money supply is fully controlled
neither exports nor imports take place
Set 2.explanation: A closed economy is an economy that has no economic relations with the rest of the world. In such an economy, there is no foreign trade. Option (d) is correct because in a closed economy there are neither exports nor imports. Control of the money supply is related to monetary policy, so option (a) is not correct.
