Set 3.q: 20. Match List-I (Molecule) with List-II (Metal present): A. Vitamin B12 B. Haemoglobin C. Chlorophyll D. Chalcopyrite | 1. Magnesium 2. Cobalt 3. Copper 4. Iron
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: In this question, biomolecules and minerals have to be matched with the principal metal present in them. Vitamin B12 is associated with cobalt; therefore, one of its names is cobalamin. Haemoglobin is the red pigment of blood and contains iron, which plays an important role in the transport of oxygen. Chlorophyll is the green pigment of plants and contains magnesium. Chalcopyrite, or copper pyrite, has the formula CuFeS2 and is considered a major ore of copper. Thus, A-2, B-4, C-1 and D-3 is the correct matching. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 3.q: 21. Which of the following chemicals is used in mosquito repellents?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Among the given options, pyrethrin is used in mosquito repellent products. Pyrethrin is an important chemical used in mosquito control and insect-repellent products. It affects the nervous system of mosquitoes.

Set 3.q: 22. The soil in which insectivorous plants grow, there is a deficiency of-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Insectivorous plants generally grow in soil where nitrogen is deficient. These plants cannot fulfil their nitrogen requirement by absorbing nitrogenous substances from the soil. They fulfil their nitrogen requirement by trapping and digesting insects. For this purpose, they have specially modified leaves and digestive juices. Examples— Nepenthes, Dionaea, Drosera, Utricularia, etc.

Set 3.q: 23. Walking on ice is more difficult than walking on a road because-
options: Ice is harder than the road.
The road is harder than ice.
When we push with our feet, ice does not exert any reaction force.
Ice has less friction than the road.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Frictional force plays a very important role in walking. When we walk on a road, the foot pushes the road backward. In return, the road exerts a static frictional force on the foot in the forward direction. This force helps us move forward. The surface of the road is relatively rough; therefore, there is sufficient grip between the foot or shoe and the road. On the surface of ice, friction is very low; therefore, the foot does not get a proper grip and the possibility of slipping increases. Hence, walking on a road is easy, whereas walking on ice is difficult. light energy into electrical energy. A traditional

Set 3.q: 24. The essential protein required for blood clotting is-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Major proteins such as fibrinogen, globulin and albumin are found in blood plasma. Among these, fibrinogen is related to blood clotting. When the body is injured, platelets and tissue factor activate the process of clot formation. In this process, thrombin converts fibrinogen into fibrin. The fine fibres of fibrin form a net-like structure in which blood cells get trapped and a clot is formed. Therefore, fibrinogen is the essential protein required for the formation of a blood clot.

Set 3.q: 25. The colour of brass becomes dull in air due to the presence of-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Brass is an alloy made of copper and zinc. The colour of brass becomes dull due to the presence of hydrogen sulphide in the air.

Set 3.q: 26. Which of the following is/are used as biofertilizer(s)? 1. Azolla 2. Blue-green algae 3. Alfalfa
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Biofertilizers can generally be divided into the following main categories— i. Nitrogen-fixing biofertilizers – Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospi rillum, Acetobacter, blue-green algae and Azolla ii. Phosphorus-solubilizing biofertilizers – Bacillus, Pseudomonas, Aspergillus iii. Composting inoculants/accelerators – Cellulolytic organisms (Trichoderma), lignolytic organisms (Humicola) iv. Plant growth-promoting rhizobac teria – Pseudomonas, etc. Thus, blue-green cyanobacteria, and algae, Azolla or are biofertilizers, whereas alfalfa is a type of leguminous plant.

Set 3.q: 27. German silver is an alloy of-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: German silver is mainly an alloy of copper (Cu), nickel (Ni) and zinc (Zn). It is used in the manufacture of utensils and other objects. Its surface appears shiny like silver; hence, it is called German silver. Bronze is made from an alloy of copper and tin.

Set 3.q: 28. In which of the following fruits is iron found in abundance?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: In terms of iron content, karonda is considered the most suitable among these options; therefore, the correct answer is option (b) karonda. Vitamin C is also found in karonda. Vitamin C helps in collagen formation in the body; therefore, it is useful in the process of wound healing. Iron is an essential component of haemoglobin in our blood. Haemoglobin is a protein found in red blood cells, which helps in carrying oxygen to the tissues of the body.

Set 3.q: 29. A photoelectric cell is a device that-
options: Converts light energy into electrical energy
Converts electrical energy into light energy
Converts light energy into chemical energy
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: A photoelectric cell is a device that produces electrical energy or an electrical signal when light is incident on it. Therefore, it is considered a device that converts phototube-type photoelectric cell has a photosensitive emitter and a collector electrode. When light of a suitable frequency is incident on the emitter, electrons are emitted from it and current can flow in the external circuit. Solar or photovoltaic cells also produce electrical energy from light, but they are based on the photovoltaic effect in a semiconductor. Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 3.q: 30. Xylem and phloem are absent in-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Xylem is the tissue concerned with the transport of water and minerals, whereas phloem is the tissue concerned with the transport of food. Together, they form the vascular tissue system of plants. Xylem and phloem are found in Pteridophyta; therefore, Pteridophyta are also called vascular cryptogams. In contrast, true xylem and phloem are absent in Bryophyta. For this reason, Bryophyta are small in size and depend more on water. They are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they can live on land, but water is necessary for their sexual reproduction. In Thallophyta, too, true roots, stems, leaves and vascular tissues are not developed. Therefore, true xylem and phloem are absent in both Bryophyta and Thallophyta.

Set 3.q: 31. The cause of great diversity among organisms is-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The basic genetic source of diversity in organisms is mutation. Mutation is a change in DNA or genes that can give rise to new genetic variations. If these changes occur in germ cells and are passed on to the next generations, they can become the basis of hereditary diversity. Evolutionary processes like natural selection act on these hereditary variations, as a result of which diversity among organisms increases and, in the long run, it may contribute to the formation of new species. Therefore, the correct answer is mutation.

Set 3.q: 32. What is a geostationary position?
options: When the Earth stops revolving around the Sun.
When an object is situated between the Moon and the Earth.
When an object moves around the Earth with the same angular speed as the Earth, such that it remains at a fixed distance...
When an object is at a fixed distance from the Earth.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: When an object moves around the Earth at a speed synchronized with the Earth’s rotation so that it appears stationary above a fixed place on the Earth, it is called a geostationary state. Geostationary satellites work on this principle. The orbit of such satellites is circular, and they complete one revolution around the Earth in about 24 hours. Since their orbital period is the same as the Earth’s rotation period, these stationary. satellites appear 3

Set 3.q: 33. One's Eyes water while peeling onions because onions release-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: When the cells of an onion break due to peeling or cutting, the sulphur-containing compounds present in them come in contact with enzymes. In this process, sulfenic acid is formed first. It is very unstable and later forms a compound called syn-propanethial S-oxide. This compound reaches the eyes, causes irritation, and stimulates the lacrimal glands to produce tears. Among the given options, the correct option related to tears caused by onions is sulfenic acid, whereas the actual tear-causing compound is syn-propanethial S-oxide.

Set 3.q: 34. The layer in the Earth's atmosphere called the ionosphere makes radio communication possible. Why? 1. The presence of ozone reflects radio waves towards the Earth. 2. The wavelength of radio waves is very long.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Radio communication becomes possible due to the presence of electrically charged particles in the ionosphere. The reflection or bending back of radio waves by the ionosphere depends on their frequency and the charged particles present in the ionosphere. Therefore, neither statement 1 nor statement 2 is correct.

Set 3.q: 35. The formation of WBCs and the destruction of RBCs take place in-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The average lifespan of red blood cells in the body is about 120 days; after this, they are destroyed in the spleen. Lymphocytes and neutrophils are two major types of white blood cells; lymphocytes are agranular, whereas neutrophils are granular. Some WBCs, such as lymphocytes, are formed in the spleen. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 3.q: 36. Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: The boiling point of an aqueous solution is higher than the boiling point of pure water.
The addition of solutes to a solution increases its water potential.
The vapour pressure of water in a solution is lower than the vapour pressure in pure water.
When a solution is separated from water by a semipermeable membrane, the flow of water can be stopped by applying pressure.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: When a non-volatile solute is added to water, the vapour pressure of the solution becomes lower than that of pure water. Due to the decrease in vapour pressure, the solution requires a higher temperature to boil; therefore, its boiling point is higher than that of pure water. On adding a solute, the water potential does not increase; rather, it decreases or becomes more negative. When a solution is separated from water by a semipermeable membrane, water flows towards the solution by osmosis. This flow can be stopped by applying suitable external pressure to the solution. Hence, options (a), (c), and (d) are correct, whereas option (b) is not correct.

Set 3.q: 37. Water is transported in plants by-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Xylem is responsible for the conduction of water and mineral salts in plants. The main function of phloem is to transport food materials prepared in the green parts of the plant to other parts. This tissue is also called bast. It is made up of four types of cells, namely sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibres.

Set 3.q: 38. The enzyme that converts starch into glucose by hydrolysis is-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Starch is a complex carbohydrate. Its digestion begins in the mouth, where amylase present in saliva starts breaking down starch. Pancreatic amylase secreted by the pancreas also helps in the digestion of starch in the small intestine. Amylase first converts starch into maltose and smaller carbohydrates. Later, other intestinal enzymes convert them into simpler forms like glucose, which can be easily absorbed by the body. Therefore, the correct enzyme related to the hydrolysis of starch is amylase.

Set 3.q: 39. The reason for implementing the 'Permanent Settlement' in Bihar was-
options: The zamindars no longer having rights over land
The right of zamindars to voluntarily transfer hereditary rights over land
To determine a fixed amount of land revenue
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: During the time of Lord Cornwallis, the land revenue system was initially introduced in 1790 AD as a Decennial Settlement, which was established as the ‘Permanent Settlement’ on 22 March 1793. The main reason for implementing this system in Bihar was to determine a fixed amount of land revenue for the Company.

Set 3.q: 40. Who led the first Indian ministry formed in Bihar in 1937?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The first Bihar ministry, formed in 1937, was led by Muhammad Yunus from 1 April 1937 to 19 July 1937. Thereafter, Shri Krishna Singh led the ministry from 20 July 1937 to 31 October 1939.

Set 3.q: 41. Who formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The peasant movement in Bihar started under the leadership of Swami Sahajanand Saraswati. Sahajanand Saraswati founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha in 1929. In expanding this Sabha across the villages of Bihar, he received support from leftist leaders such as Karyanand Sharma, Rahul Sankrityayan, Panchanan Sharma, and Yadunandan Sharma. Swami Vidyanand was also a peasant leader of Bihar.

Set 3.q: 42. Arrange the following in chronological order of their formation- 1. Bombay Association 2. Madras Mahajan Sabha 3. Indian Association 4. Indian League
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The chronological order of establishment of the given organizations is as follows Bombay Association – August 1852 – Established with the cooperation of Dadabhai Naoroji, Jagannath Shankarsheth, and others. Indian League – September 1875 – Established by Shishir Kumar Ghosh. Indian Association – July 1876 – Established by Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose. Madras Mahajana Sabha – May 1884 – Established by S. Ramaswami Mudaliar, M. Veeraraghavachari, G. Subramania Iyer, and P. Ananda Charlu. Thus, the correct order is 1, 4, 3, 2. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Set 3.q: 43. Match List-I with List-II: A. Moplah Rebellion B. Pabna Rebellion C. Eka Movement D. Birsa Munda Rebellion | 1. Kerala 2. Bihar 3. Bengal 4. Awadh
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Moplah Rebellion took place in Malabar, Kerala, in 1921; the Pabna Revolt took place in Pabna, Bengal, from 1873 to 1876 AD; the Eka Movement took place in Awadh in 1921–22; and the Birsa Munda Rebellion took place in Bihar, present-day Jharkhand, around 1899–1900 AD.

Set 3.q: 44. Which Gupta ruler came to power by killing his elder brother?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Chandragupta II is known as the Gupta ruler who, according to traditional accounts, gained power by defeating his elder brother Ramagupta. This story is associated with Vishakhadatta’s ‘Devichandraguptam’. According to this account, Ramagupta proved unable to face the Shaka ruler and agreed to hand over his wife Dhruva Devi to the enemy. Chandragupta II opposed this humiliating situation, killed the Shaka ruler, and later killed Ramagupta. He then ascended the throne and married Ramagupta’s wife Dhruva Devi.

Set 3.q: 45. What was 'Uraiyur' famous for during the Sangam Age?
options: An important centre of spice trade
An important centre of cotton trade
An important commercial centre of foreign trade
An important centre of internal trade
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: ‘Uraiyur’, situated on the banks of the Kaveri River in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, was an important city of the Sangam period. During the Sangam age, ‘Uraiyur’ was a major centre for the trade of cotton and cotton textiles. Its description is found in the ‘Periplus of the Erythraean Sea’. In it, Uraiyur has been referred to as ‘Argaru’.

Set 3.q: 46. Read the following statements carefully- 1. The Brahmo Samaj supported monotheism. 2. The Arya Samaj contributed to the development of education. 3. The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: On 20 August 1828, Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj, whose original name was Brahmo Sabha. Its objectives were the worship of one God, opposition to idol worship, opposition to priestly domination, and rejection of the doctrine of incarnation. The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 AD by Dayanand Saraswati. The followers of the Arya Samaj made significant efforts in the field of spreading education. The Ramakrishna Mission was founded in 1897 AD by Swami Vivekananda.

Set 3.q: 47. Gandhi's first bold step in all-India politics was-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Gandhi’s first bold step in all-India politics was the Satyagraha launched in 1919 against the Rowlatt Act. Gandhiji used three political platforms for the Rowlatt Satyagraha—Home Rule League, certain Pan-Islamist groups, and the Satyagraha Sabha. It is noteworthy that before this, Gandhiji’s movements in Champaran, Kheda, and Ahmedabad were confined to particular regions. 4

Set 3.q: 48. Which of the following did not rebel against the control of the English East India Company?
options: Velu Thampi, the Diwan of Travancore
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Raja of Vizianagaram revolted against the Company’s rule in the last decade of the eighteenth century. The Poligars of Tamil Nadu revolted several times against the revenue and administrative policies of the Company, and Velu Thampi, the Diwan of Travancore, led a revolt against the British in 1808-09 AD. In contrast, the Nizam of Hyderabad did not revolt against the Company; rather, in 1798 AD, he accepted British protection and the Subsidiary Alliance system.

Set 3.q: 49. Who wrote the following lines? 'Now the desire for self-sacrifice is in our hearts, Let us see how much strength there is in the killer's arm.'
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The lines of the ghazal in question are by the poet Bismil Azimabadi. The real name of Bismil Azimabadi was Syed Shah Mohammad Hasan. He was born in 1901 in Hardas Bigha village near Patna. This ghazal was written in Urdu and was published in 1922, though some sources also mention 1921, in Qazi Abdul Ghaffar’s magazine ‘Sabah’.

Set 3.q: 50. Consider the following statements about the Mughal Mansabdari system... 1. 'Zat' and 'Sawar' ranks were granted. 2. Mansabdars were hereditary officers. 3. There were three categories of mansabdars. 4. They were paid salaries by the Diwan's office.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The word ‘Mansab’ means ‘rank’ or ‘position’, and ‘Mansabdar’ meant an officer who held a rank or position in the imperial army. Akbar’s Mansabdari system was based on the decimal system. Akbar introduced the ranks of ‘Zat’ and ‘Sawar’ in the Mansabdari system. ‘Zat’ referred to personal status and salary, while ‘Sawar’ referred to the number of cavalrymen. On the basis of Zat and Sawar, Mansabdars were divided into three classes. The first class included those who maintained Sawars equal to the number of their assigned Mansab. The second class included those Mansabdars whose number of Sawars was half or more than half of their assigned Mansab. The third class included those Mansabdars whose number of Sawars was less than half of their assigned Mansab. Mansabdars were not hereditary officers. They were paid either in cash or in the form of Jagir. Thus, code (d) is the correct answer.

Set 3.q: 51. 'Pankodakasannirodhe' was a fine levied by the Mauryan administration for-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: In the Mauryan administration, special attention was paid to urban administration and public sanitation. In Kautilya’s Arthashastra, there was a provision for punishment for making roads, highways, and public places dirty or obstructing them. ‘Pankodakasannirodhe’ was related to the fine imposed for causing water and mud to accumulate on the road or for throwing mud.

Set 3.q: 52. The tendency for increased litigation was visible after the introduction of the land settlement system of Lord Cornwallis in 1793. The reason for this is normally traced to which one of the following provisions?
options: Making the zamindar's position stronger vis-à-vis the ryot.
Making the East India Company an overlord of the zamindars.
Making the judicial system more efficient.
None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) above is correct.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: In the land revenue system of Permanent Settlement, or Zamindari system, introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 AD, the actual rights of the Zamindars over land were accepted, as long as they continued to collect rent and pay 10/11th of it to the government. But the territorial extent of the Zamindari was not fixed. Since rent-free grant lands, pastures, fallow lands, etc. were not clearly determined, legal disputes increased. The presence of many intermediaries between the Zamindar and the cultivator also increased the number of legal cases. It is clear that the required option is (d).

Set 3.q: 53. Which of the following parties did not support the 'Quit India Movement'?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Quit India Movement was started by the Congress in 1942 with the demand for immediate independence. However, at that time, not all political parties supported the Congress. The Hindu Mahasabha did not support this movement. The Communist Party of India supported the war efforts of the Allied Powers; therefore, its official policy was also not in favour of the Quit India Movement. The Unionist Party of Punjab also supported the British war efforts.

Set 3.q: 54. Which of the following kingdoms were associated with the life of the Buddha? 1. Avanti 2. Gandhara 3. Kosala 4. Magadha
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Among the Maha janapadas given in the options, the Mahajanapadas of Kosala and Magadha were related to the life of Buddha. Gautama Buddha travelled in both Magadha and Kosala for the propagation of his teachings. Avan ti and Gandhara were indirectly or later associated with Buddhism, but they are not regarded as places direct ly connected with the life of Buddha.

Set 3.q: 55. Match List-I (Explorer) with List-II (Birthplace): A. Christopher Columbus B. Jacques Cartier C. Sir Francis Drake D. Ferdinand Magellan | 1. Portugal 2. United Kingdom 3. Italy 4. France
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The correct matching is as follows List-I (Explorer)  - List-II (Birthplace) Christopher Columbus - Italy Jacques Cartier - France Sir Francis Drake - United Kingdom Ferdinand Magellan - Portugal Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

Set 3.q: 56. Match List-I with List-II: A. Rampa Rebellion B. Pabna Peasant Revolt C. Bengal Indigo Revolt D. Jaintia Rebellion | 1. 1859–60 2. 1879–80 3. 1860–63 4. 1873–76
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The correctly matched pairs are List-I Rampa Rebellion Pabna Peasant Revolt Bengal Indigo Revolt Jaintia Rebellion List-II 1879-80 1873-76 1859-60 1860-63

Set 3.q: 57. Consider the following events in the history of India- 1. Rise of Pratiharas under King Bhoja 2. Establishment of Pallava power under Mahendravarman I 3. Establishment of Chola power by Parantaka I 4. Pala dynasty founded by Gopala
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The correct chrono logical order of the events is Pallava power was consolidated under Mahendravarman I (600-630 AD), the Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala (750-770 AD), the rise of the Pratiharas took place under Mihira Bhoja, also called Bhoja I – 1758-63 Third Battle of Panipat – 1761 It is noteworthy that the wars fought between the British and the French in India are known as the Carnatic Wars.

Set 3.q: 58. Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
59. Gandhi's boycott of British-manufactured products became effective because Britain regarded India as a large-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Gandhiji’s boycott of British goods, especially foreign cloth, proved effective because, under the colonial system, India was a large market for British goods. Britain sold its industrial products in the Indian market and also obtained raw materials from India.

Set 3.q: 60. Who among the following said, 'India for Indians'?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati was a great philosopher, social leader and founder of the Arya Samaj. He gave the slogan “India for Indians.”

Set 3.q: 61. Consider the following statements: Ahadis were those troopers who- 1. offered their services alone 2. did not attach themselves to any chief 3. had the emperor as their immediate colonel 4. attached themselves to Mirzas
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: During the Mughal period, apart from the soldiers of the mansabdars, there were two other types of cavalry soldiers, known as ‘Ahadi’ and ‘Dakhili’. The Ahadi soldiers were appointed by the emperor and served as his bodyguards. Although they had no connection with the mansabdars, they were assigned to serve with the mansabdars on the direct orders of the emperor. They were directly under the emperor, and their recruitment, salary, clothing and horses were all provided by the state. A separate Diwan and Bakhshi were arranged for them. It is mentioned that one Ahadi cavalryman received a salary of Rs. 500, whereas an ordinary cavalryman received only Rs. 12 to Rs. 15. They were considered the most capable and loyal soldiers of the emperor.

Set 3.q: 62. By which of the following Acts was the Council of India abolished?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: During British rule, the Government of India Act, 1935 was passed. It was through this Act that the Council of India was abolished. The Act divided powers on the basis of Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists. It also abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced dyarchy at the Centre. Under the federation to be established by the Government of India Act, 1935, the residuary powers were given to the Governor General. 5

Set 3.q: 63. The upliftment of backward classes was the main programme of which of the following?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The upliftment of the backward classes was the main programme of the Satyashodhak Samaj. It was founded in 1873 by Jyotiba Phule. This movement was started for the welfare of Dalits and people belonging to lower castes. Phule criticised Brahmanical dominance, priestly domination and caste-based exploitation. His social and religious ideas are clearly seen in his works such as ‘Sarvajanik Satya Dharma Pustak’ and ‘Gulamgiri’.

Set 3.q: 64. On which occasion was 'Jana-Gana-Mana' sung for the first time?
options: Session of the Indian National Congress - 1896
Session of the Indian National Congress - 1905
Session of the Indian National Congress - 1911
Session of the Indian National Congress - 1919
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: ‘Jana-Gana-Mana’, originally written and composed in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore, was adopted in its Hindi version by the Constituent Assembly as the National Anthem of India on 24 January, 1950. It was first sung in December, 1911 at the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress.

Set 3.q: 65. The author of the book 'Zij Muhammad Shahi', written in 1773 AD and related to the knowledge of constellations, was-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Sawai Jai Singh of Amber, also known as Jai Singh II, was a Rajput ruler who founded the city of Jaipur and made it a centre of science and art. Jai Singh was also a great astronomer. He built observatories equipped with modern instruments in Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Banaras (Varanasi) and Mathura. To help people in astronomical observations, Jai Singh prepared a set of tables called ‘Zij Muhammad Shahi’. He also got Euclid’s Elements of Geometry translated into Sanskrit.

Set 3.q: 66. Which of the following among the Navaratnas of Chandragupta was associated with predictive astrology?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The efficient rule of Chandragupta II ‘Vikramaditya’ was also praised by the Chinese traveller Fahien. The Nine Gems of his court have remained famous through the ages. Among the Nine Gems, the greatest was the great poet Kalidasa, while Kshapanaka was an astrologer.

Set 3.q: 67. 'Dar-ul-Uloom' was established by-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Dar-ul-Uloom Nadwatul Ulama, generally known as Dar ul-Uloom, was established in 1898 in Lucknow. It was established by Nadwatul Ulama. Nadwatul Ulama was formed in 1892–1893 in Kanpur, and Maulana Shibli Nomani was among its founders. Due to the efforts of Maulana Syed Ahmad Mungeri, the Nadwatul Ulama Council established Dar-ul-Uloom in Lucknow. Shibli Nomani was also a chief teacher of Dar-ul-Uloom.

Set 3.q: 68. Which of the following is not correctly matched? (Newspaper : Founder)
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The journal ‘Tahzib ul-Akhlaq’ was edited by the Muslim reformer Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, not by Muhammad Ali Jinnah. Therefore, only option (c) is not correctly matched.

Set 3.q: 69. Where is the earliest evidence of humans found in India?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The first evidence of human fossil remains in India was obtained from the archaeological site called ‘Hathnora’ in the Narmada Valley, located in Sehore, Madhya Pradesh. It was discovered in 1982 by Arun Sonakia, a geologist associated with the Geological Survey of India.

Set 3.q: 70. The first ruler to accept the Subsidiary Alliance was-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Wellesley did not invent the Subsidiary Alliance; this system already existed. Probably Dupleix was the first European who provided his troops to Indian rulers on hire. From the time of Clive, almost all Governors-General had adopted this system. Wellesley’s special contribution was only that he developed it and used it in his relations with all the Indian rulers who came into contact with him. The first Subsidiary Alliance was made with Awadh in 1765, when the Company promised to protect its borders in return for a fixed sum of money, and Awadh agreed to keep an English Resident in Lucknow. Note: If the question asks about the first state to accept Wellesley’s Subsidiary Alliance, the answer will be Hyderabad.

Set 3.q: 71. With reference to Wood's Despatch of 1854, consider the following statements- 1. It recommended English as the medium of instruction for higher studies. 2. It emphasized women's education and vocational training.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Charles Wood’s Despatch emphasised that higher education should be imparted through the medium of the English language, but at the same time, it also stressed the development of vernacular languages. This Despatch also emphasised women’s education and vocational training. Therefore, statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Set 3.q: 72. When did Queen Victoria declare that Indian administration would be taken under the control of the British Crown?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Revolt of 1857 forced the British Government to end Company rule in India. After this, the Government of India Act, 1858 was introduced, and Queen Victoria’s Proclamation was issued on 1 November, 1858. This proclamation made it clear that the administration of India would now be directly under the British Crown instead of the East India Company. Lord Canning, who was the Governor-General at that time, became the first Viceroy of India. For administrative control, the post of Secretary of State for India was created in Britain, along with a 15-member Council of India to assist him.

Set 3.q: 73. The first archaeologist to excavate Harappa, but who could not understand its importance, was-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: A. Cunningham carried out limited excavation of the historically important mounds of Harappa in the Indian subcontinent and obtained some antiquities; however, he could not understand the importance of the Harappan mounds. Later, the real significance of the Indus Valley Civilisation came to light through the work of Daya Ram Sahni, Rakhal Das Banerji and John Marshall.

Set 3.q: 74. During the Indian freedom struggle, why did the Rowlatt Act create public anger?
options: It reduced the freedom of religion
It authorized the imprisonment of people without trial
It controlled the activities of trade unions
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: To suppress the growing revolutionary activities in India, the government constituted a committee in 1917 under the chairmanship of Justice Sidney A. T. Rowlatt. Its objective was to prepare an effective plan to suppress terrorist activities. On the basis of its recommendations, the Act passed in March 1919 came to be known as the Rowlatt Act. Under the Rowlatt Act, the British government could detain political prisoners/suspects for up to two years without trial. Therefore, this law was called the law of “no lawyer, no appeal and no argument.”

Set 3.q: 75. The reforms introduced by Sher Shah Suri included- 1. Revenue reforms 2. Administrative reforms 3. Military reforms 4. Reforms in the currency system
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Sher Shah Suri holds an important place in medieval India. As an empire-builder and administrator, he is considered a forerunner of Akbar. 1. Revenue Reforms – Sher Shah believed that for the stability of the empire, it was necessary for the peasants to be happy and satisfied. He also believed that a large amount of land revenue remained outstanding from the peasants, due to which the treasury suffered considerable loss. Therefore, land revenue should not remain in arrears. With this objective, Sher Shah introduced several reforms in the land system. 2. Administrative Reforms – Sher Shah first acquired knowledge of administration as the manager of his father’s jagir. Since he had served under the Mughals, he had experience of Mughal administration, military organization and financial system. This is why, due to the administrative ability displayed by Sher Shah during his short reign of five years, he is counted among the best sultans of Delhi. 3. Military Reforms – To strengthen his empire, Sher Shah introduced several reforms in military organization. He was greatly influenced by the reforms of Sultan Alauddin Khalji. To prevent dishonesty, he introduced the practice of branding horses and recording the descriptive rolls of soldiers. 4. Reforms in the Currency System – Sher Shah’s reign was a period of experimentation in the history of Indian currency. Regarding his currency reform, V. A. Smith wrote, “This rupee is the basis of the existing British currency.” Sher Shah replaced the old and worn-out coins with coins of pure gold, silver and copper. He issued a pure silver rupee weighing 178 grains and the copper dam. Therefore, Sher Shah Suri is credited with all the above mentioned reforms. 6

Set 3.q: 76. Consider the following statements- 1. Narasimha Saluva ended the Sangama dynasty... 2. Vira Narasimha deposed the last Saluva ruler... 3. Vira Narasimha was succeeded by Krishnadeva Raya. 4. Krishnadeva Raya was succeeded by Achyuta Raya.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Narasimha Saluva, the feudatory chief of Chandragiri, deposed Virupaksha II, the last ruler of the Sangama dynasty, seized the throne in 1485 AD and established a new dynasty known as the Saluva dynasty. Vira Narasimha deposed the son of Narasimha Saluva, Immadi Narasimha, who was the last ruler of the Saluva dynasty, and seized the throne. He laid the foundation of the Tuluva dynasty. After his death in 1509 AD, his younger brother Krishnadevaraya (1509 1529 AD) ascended the throne. Krishnadevaraya was succeeded by his half-brother Achyuta Deva Raya, who ascended the throne in 1529 AD. Therefore, all the above statements are correct.

Set 3.q: 77. Consider the following statements- The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for 1. provincial autonomy. 2. the establishment of a Federal Court. 3. an All India Federation at the Centre.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The present constitutional framework of India is largely based on the Government of India Act, 1935. The main provisions of the Government of India Act, 1935 were as follows: 1. establishment of an All-India Federation at the Centre, 2. introduction of dyarchy at the Centre, 3. establishment of autonomous government in the provinces in place of dyarchy, 4. bicameral central legislature, 5. provincial system of government, 6. provincial legislature, 7. division of powers between the Centre and the provinces, 8. establishment of the Federal Court, etc. Since all the three statements given in the question are based on the Government of India Act, 1935, the correct answer will be option (d).

Set 3.q: 78. Four important events in the life of Buddha and the four places associated with them are given below... (1) Birth (2) Enlightenment (3) First sermon (4) Death | (i) Sarnath (ii) Bodh Gaya (iii) Lumbini (iv) Kushinagar
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Gautama Buddha was born in 563 BC at Lumbini near Kapilavastu. He attained enlightenment at Uruvela, whose present name is Bodh Gaya, on the night of Vaishakha Purnima. He delivered his first sermon, known as Dharmachakrapravartana, at Rishipattana in Kashi, present-day Sarnath. He passed away at Kushinara, which is called “Mahaparinirvana” in Buddhist texts.

Set 3.q: 79. Consider the following statements- 1. The Factories Act, 1881, was passed to fix wages... 2. N. M. Lokhande was a pioneer in organizing the labour movement in British India.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Factory Act, 1881 was an early labour law of British India. Its main objective was to regulate, in a limited manner, the conditions of children working in factories. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Factory Act, 1881 was not passed to fix the wages of industrial workers or to give them the right to form trade unions. It mainly contained limited provisions related to child labour. Legal provision for trade unions was made later through the Trade Unions Act, 1926. Statement 2 is correct because N. M. Lokhande was one of the leading figures who organized the labour movement in British India. He organized the mill workers of Bombay and formed the Bombay Mill Hands Association in 1890. Therefore, only statement 2 is correct. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 3.q: 80. Match List-I with List-II- A. Sarkaria Commission B. C. Rangarajan Committee C. Parekh Committee D. Narasimham Committee | 1. Poverty 2. Infrastructure 3. Centre-State 4. Banking
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Sarkaria Com mission was constituted in June 1983 under the chairmanship of Jus tice R. S. Sarkaria. Its objective was to review the existing arrangement of powers, functions and responsi bilities between the Centre and the States. The C. Rangarajan Commit tee was constituted by the Planning Commission in June 2012 to review the methodology for measuring poverty. The Parekh Committee was constituted by the Ministry of Fi nance in December 2006 under the chairmanship of Deepak Parekh. Its objective was to identify the obsta cles in infrastructure financing and suggest measures to resolve them. The Narasimham Committee is re lated to banking sector reforms. The Narasimham Committee recom mended reforms related to making the Indian banking system stronger, more competitive and more effi cient. Therefore, the correct answer is (a) 3, 1, 2, 4.

Set 3.q: 81. Match Column-A with Column-B- A. National Agricultural Policy B. Marine Fishing Policy C. New Foreign Trade Policy D. Seventh Finance Commission | 1. 2004 2. 1978 3. 2000 4. 2014
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The National Agriculture Policy was announced in the year 2000. Its objective was to promote high and broad-based growth in the agricultural sector. In the context of the Marine Fishing Policy, the question refers to the Comprehensive Marine Fishing Policy, 2004, whose objective was to ensure the conservation, management and sustainable use of marine resources. The new Foreign Trade Policy has been linked with 2014 in the question; therefore, according to the answer key, it has been matched with 2014. In the context of the Seventh Finance Commission, 1978 is considered the year related to its report. Therefore, the correct answer is (d).

Set 3.q: 82. What is the name of the apex bank for providing agricultural refinance in India?
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Option (b) is correct, because the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, known as NABARD, is the apex development finance institution for agriculture and rural development in India. It was established on July 12, 1982, and its headquarters is in Mumbai. NABARD provides refinance facilities to banks and other financial institutions so that credit can be made available for agriculture and other productive activities in rural areas. The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank, the State Bank of India is a commercial bank, and the Imperial Bank is no longer an existing institution. Therefore, the apex institution providing agricultural refinance is NABARD. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 3.q: 83. Which one of the following best describes the nature of the 'Green Revolution' of the late sixties of the twentieth century?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Green Revolution of the late 1960s was not limited only to high-yielding variety seeds. It was a package technology in which the combined use of seeds, fertilizers and water, that is, irrigation, was necessary. Option (a) is incorrect, because the Green Revolution does not mean excessive cultivation of green vegetables. Option (b) was a programme related to agricultural development, but it does not describe the nature of the Green Revolution most accurately. Option (c) is partly correct, because the High-Yielding Variety Programme was an important part of the Green Revolution, but it does not explain the entire technological package. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 3.q: 84. Consider the following statements- 1. The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices recommends the Minimum Support Prices for 32 crops. 2. The Union Ministry of Consumer Affairs... launched the National Food Security Mission.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Minimum Support Price is the price announced by the government with the objective of providing price protection to farmers. The government determines it on the basis of the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices. Statement 1 is incorrect, because the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices recommends Minimum Support Prices not for 32 crops, but for 22 mandated agricultural crops. In addition, the prices of Toria and de husked coconut are fixed on the basis of the Minimum Support Prices of the respective crops. Statement 2 is also incorrect, because the National Food Security Mission was not launched by the Union Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution. It was launched in October 2007 as a centrally sponsored scheme and comes under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. Hence, both statements are incorrect, so the correct answer is option (d).

Set 3.q: 85. Which of the following measures is not a measure of selective credit control?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Selective credit control is a qualitative method of monetary policy through which the central bank controls the flow of credit for a particular sector, commodity or purpose. Changes in lending limits or margin requirements, credit rationing and moral suasion are measures of selective credit control. Through these measures, the central bank 7 the National Commission for even during a proclamation of influences the quantity and direction of credit for specific sectors or specific purposes. By contrast, selling government securities is an open market operation. It is a quantitative monetary measure that affects the liquidity and money supply of the banking system. Therefore, it is not a measure of selective credit control. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 3.q: 86. Which of the following connects all ATMs in India?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Option (c) is the correct answer, because the principal mechanism connecting the shared ATM network in India is the National Financial Switch, which is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India. The institution that connects India’s ATM network is the National Payments Corporation of India. The Indian Banks’ Association is an organisation of the banking sector, not the operator of the ATM network. National Securities Depository Limited is an institution related to the securities market. The Reserve Bank of India is the regulator of payment systems, but the shared ATM network is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 3.q: 87. Match List-I with List-II: A. Dutta Committee B. Wanchoo Committee C. Rajamannar Committee D. Chakravarty Committee | 1. Industrial licensing 2. Direct taxes 3. Centre-State relations 4. Monetary system
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Dutta Committee, 1969, was related to the review of industrial licensing policy. The Wanchoo Committee, 1971, was related to direct taxes. The Rajamannar Committee was related to Centre-State relations. The Chakravarty Committee, 1985, was related to the review of the working of the monetary system. Thus, the correct matching is— Dutt Committee – Industrial Licensing Wanchoo Committee – Direct Taxes Rajamannar Committee – Centre State Relations Chakravarty Committee – Monetary System

Set 3.q: 88. Which of the following is a point of difference between India's parliamentary system of government and Britain's parliamentary system of government?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Both India and Britain have a parliamentary system of government, but in India, Parliament is subject to the limitations of the Constitution. Indian laws can be judicially reviewed, whereas in Britain, the principle of parliamentary sovereignty is dominant and, generally, courts do not invalidate Acts of Parliament. Therefore, the main point of difference between the parliamentary systems of India and Britain is judicial review.

Set 3.q: 89. Who is not an ex-officio member of the National Human Rights Commission?
options: Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities
Chairperson of the Law Commission of India
Chairpersons of the National Commission for SCs and STs
Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: According to the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, the Chairpersons of the National Commission for Backward Classes, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, the National Commission for Minorities, Scheduled Castes, the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes and the National Commission for Women, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities are included as ex officio members of the National Human Rights Commission.

Set 3.q: 90. Consider the following statements regarding Fundamental Rights in India: 1. Guarantees against the actions of the State. 2. Listed in Part III. 3. Ensure social, economic and political justice. 4. Not like the Bill of Rights.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Fundamental Rights are judicially enforceable rights enshrined in Part III of the Consti tution. They mainly provide con stitutional protection to individuals against the arbitrary actions of the State. The Preamble of the Consti tution aims at social, economic and political justice; Fundamental Rights further this objective. Indian Funda mental Rights are compared with the Bill of Rights of the United States of America. However, the Directive Principles of State Policy also play a major role in social and economic justice.

Set 3.q: 91. A person shall not be disqualified for being chosen as a member of a Municipality on the ground of age, if he/she has attained the age of:
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: According to Article 243-V in Part IX-A of the Constitution, a person shall not be disqualified on the ground of being less than 25 years of age for being chosen as a member of a Municipality if he has attained the age of 21 years.

Set 3.q: 92. Which of the following constitutional powers is not vested in the President?
options: Returning an ordinary bill for reconsideration.
Returning a money bill for reconsideration.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Under Article 111, the President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration like other ordinary Bills. According to Article 110 of the Constitution, a Bill is deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with the matters specified in that Article. The other three options are constitutional powers of the President. In fact, such Bills can be introduced or moved only in the Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President under the provisions of Article 117.

Set 3.q: 93. Match List-I with List-II: A. Seventh Schedule B. Eighth Schedule C. Ninth Schedule D. Tenth Schedule | 1. Languages 2. Disqualification on defection 3. Distribution of legislative powers 4. Validation of certain Acts
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The following are correctly matched— Seventh Schedule - Distribution of legislative powers Eighth Schedule - Languages Ninth Schedule - Validation of certain Acts and Regulations Tenth Schedule - Disqualification on the ground of defection

Set 3.q: 94. Which of the following writs can the High Court issue for the protection of personal liberty?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: According to Article 226 of the Indian Constitution, a High Court can issue the writ of Habeas Corpus for personal liberty. Habeas Corpus means demanding the physical production of a person before the court. This writ applies in cases where a person is said to have been illegally detained. If the detention is found to be illegal, the detained person is immediately released. After the 44th Constitutional Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended Emergency; therefore, this writ has become very important for the protection of personal liberty.

Set 3.q: 95. In addition to Fundamental Rights, which of the following parts of the Constitution of India reflect the principles and provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948? 1. Preamble 2. DPSP 3. Fundamental Duties
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: On 10 December 1948, the United Nations General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in Paris. The Preamble, Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution reflect the principles and provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948. Article 29 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948, particularly reflects the Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights contains a total of 30 Articles.

Set 3.q: 96. Which Article of the Constitution provides protection to accused persons against double jeopardy and self-incrimination in respect of conviction for offences?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: According to Article 20(2) of the Constitution, no person can be prosecuted and punished more than once for the same offence. According to Article 20(3), no person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

Set 3.q: 97. Match the following Articles with their provisions: A. 54 B. 58 C. 66 D. 87 | 1. Qualifications for President 2. Election of VP 3. Election of President 4. Special address by President
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Article - Provision 54 58 66 87 - Election of the President- Qualifications for election as President- Election of the Vice-President- Special address by the President

Set 3.q: 98. Which of the following are appointed by the President of India? 1. Chairman of the Finance Commission 2. Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog 3. Chief Ministers of Delhi and Puducherry
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: According to Article 280(1), the Chairman of the Finance Commission is appointed by the President. Under Article 239AA(5) for Delhi and the Government of Union Territories Act, 1963 for Puducherry, the Chief Minister of the Union Territory is appointed by the President, and the other Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Chief Minister. The Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. The Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister. According to Section 54(1) of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, the Chief Minister is appointed by the Lieutenant Governor and not by the President. The Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister.

Set 3.q: 99. In the Indian political system, the executive functions under the .............. .
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: India has adopted the parliamentary system of government. In the Indian political system, the executive works under the legislature because the political executive is formed from among the members of the legislature, and the executive, i.e. the Council of Ministers, is collectively responsible to the legislature, i.e. the Lok Sabha. 8

Set 3.q: 100. The duty of the Pro tem Speaker is-
options: To conduct the proceedings of the House in the absence of the Speaker
To administer the oath to the members
To act as a substitute Speaker when the election of the Speaker is not possible
Only to check whether the members' certificates of election are valid
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: In a newly elected House, before the election of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, generally the senior-most member of the House is chosen as the Pro-tem Speaker. The Pro-tem Speaker administers the oath to the newly elected members.

Set 3.q: 101. The power to extend the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India with respect to any matter included in the Union List of legislative powers rests with-
options: The Ministry of Law, Justice and Company Affairs
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Under Article 138 of the Constitution, Parliament may, by law, enlarge the jurisdiction and powers of the Supreme Court. According to clause (1) of Article 138, Parliament has been given the power to extend the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India with respect to any matter included in the Union List.

Set 3.q: 102. With reference to the judiciary, select the correct statement(s): (i) Original Constitution had 9 judges. (ii) Present number is 34. (iii) High Court writ jurisdiction is wider. (iv) Resignation addressed to Chief Justice.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: In the original Constitution, the number of judges of the Supreme Court was eight (8); Parliament, through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019, increased it to 34, including the Chief Justice of India. High Courts, under Article 226, have writ jurisdiction for the protection of Fundamental Rights, constitutional rights and other statutory rights. However, the Supreme Court, under Article 32, has writ jurisdiction only for the protection of Fundamental Rights. All judges of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice of India, may submit their resignation only through a letter addressed to the President.

Set 3.q: 103. Who issues the 'Red List of Threatened Species'?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Red List of Threatened Species is released by the IUCN, i.e. the International Union for Conservation of Nature. The IUCN was established in the year 1948. In the Red List released by it, species are classified into categories such as Extinct, Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened, Least Concern, etc.

Set 3.q: 104. Consider the following statements related to the ecosystem- 1. The term 'ecosystem' was first used by A.G. Tansley. 2. Organisms that produce their own food are producers. 3. Consumers consume through photosynthesis. 4. Decomposers convert inorganic to organic.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The term ‘ecosystem’ was first used in print by A.G. Tansley in 1935. In an ecosystem, biotic components are divided into three main parts— (1) Producers, (2) Consumers, (3) Decomposers Producers are those organisms that prepare their own food through photosynthesis and chemosynthesis. Consumers are heterotrophic organisms. They do not perform photosynthesis. Decomposers convert complex organic substances into simple inorganic substances.

Set 3.q: 105. Where is the headquarters of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) located?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The headquarters of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) is located in New Delhi. Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai are the other places where the NGT holds sittings. The National Green Tribunal was established on 18 October 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 for the effective and speedy disposal of cases related to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources. This Tribunal functions on the principles of natural justice.

Set 3.q: 106. The ozone layer is mainly located in the-
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The ozone layer is mainly located in the lower part of the stratosphere. Its maximum concentration as a layer is found between 15 and 35 km. About 10 percent of ozone is found in the troposphere and 90 percent in the stratosphere. This layer prevents the harmful ultraviolet rays of the Sun from reaching the Earth.

Set 3.q: 107. With reference to Sri Lanka's first 'Blue Bond', consider the following statements: 1. It has been dually listed on NSE IX and Colombo Stock Exchange. 2. It is the first Blue Bond admitted for trading in India's IFSC.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: In February 2026, Sri Lanka’s first Blue Bond, an LKR 3 billion issuance by DFCC Bank PLC, was dually listed on NSE International Exchange (NSE IX) at GIFT City and the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE). It was also the first Blue Bond to be admitted for trading within India’s International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) jurisdiction.

Set 3.q: 108. With reference to the Airport Service Quality (ASQ) Awards... 1. Mangaluru International Airport selected in 'Best Airport at Arrivals'. 2. Presented by ICAO.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Mangaluru International Airport (MIA) was named the winner in the “Best Airport at Arrivals – Globally” category at the 2025 Airport Service Quality (ASQ) Customer Experience Awards for the second consecutive year. Earlier, MIA had also received recognition in the same category in 2024. Hence, statement 1 is correct. The ASQ Awards are associated with Airports Council International (ACI) World. These awards are given on the basis of real-time passenger feedback collected at airports through ASQ surveys. They are not conferred by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). Hence, statement 2 is incorrect. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a), 1 only.

Set 3.q: 109. Which of the following statements is not correct regarding the India-Canada Summit Talks 2026?
options: A meeting was held in New Delhi between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
Both countries agreed to cooperate on nuclear reactors such as SMRs.
Canada announced its decision to join India's International Solar Alliance.
Both countries set a target to increase bilateral trade to 100 billion dollars by 2030.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: During the India Canada Summit 2026, the two countries did not set a target of increasing bilateral trade to USD 100 billion by 2030. Officially, the target was to increase bilateral trade to about USD 50 billion by 2030. For this, both countries agreed to take forward the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) negotiations and conclude them by the end of 2026. Talks were held in New Delhi between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. Both countries also discussed cooperation on Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and advanced nuclear reactors. Canada also announced its decision to join the International Solar Alliance. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 3.q: 110. With reference to digital initiatives and administrative reforms, the recently announced 'Pragati' and 'Vikas' are related to which of the following?
options: New index of NITI Aayog's Aspirational Districts Programme
Women's Self-Help Group initiative of the Ministry of Rural Development
AI chatbot of Digital India Mission 2.0
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah formally unveiled the Census-2027 mascots, “Pragati” and “Vikas”, in New Delhi. “Pragati” has been presented as a female enumerator and “Vikas” as a male enumerator. These mascots are symbols of conveying messages related to Census-2027 to the public in an effective and citizen-friendly manner and of the equal participation of women and men in the resolve to make India a developed nation by 2047. On the same occasion, four digital tools/platforms related to Census-2027 were also soft launched.

Set 3.q: 111. The theme of World Wildlife Day 2026 has been chosen as 'Medicinal and Aromatic Plants: Conserving Health, Heritage and Livelihoods'. This theme emphasizes:
options: Only preventing the illegal trade in wild animals.
Conservation of medicinal and aromatic plants and livelihood security of local communities.
Restoration of marine biodiversity and coral reefs.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: World Wildlife Day is observed every year on 3 March. The theme for 2026 is “Medicinal and Aromatic Plants: Conserving Health, Heritage and Livelihoods.” The main focus of this theme is the role of medicinal and aromatic plants. These plants are linked to traditional medicine, human health, cultural heritage, biodiversity conservation and the livelihoods of Indigenous and local communities. Therefore, this theme emphasizes their conservation and sustainable use along with livelihood security for local communities. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 3.q: 112. Under the India-Israel Fisheries and Aquaculture Agreement 2026, how will the two countries enhance cooperation?
options: By building joint ships for deep-sea mining.
By establishing Indo-Israel Centres of Excellence (CoEs) in India and promoting advanced aquaculture technologies.
By establishing a free maritime trade corridor between the two countries.
By modernizing only traditional inland fisheries.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: On 26 February 2026, during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Israel, an MoU was signed between India and Israel on cooperation in the field of fisheries and aquaculture. It was signed by External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar on behalf of India and by Mr. Avi Dichter, Israel’s Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, on behalf of Israel. The objective of this agreement is to promote sustainable and technology-based fisheries and aquaculture in India. Under this, cooperation includes the establishment of Indo–Israel Centres of Excellence (CoEs) for Fisheries and Aquaculture, advanced Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS), water reuse technologies, automation-based farming, data driven aquaculture, aquatic disease management, mariculture, seaweed based systems, R&D, training and innovation. It will help strengthen India’s Blue Economy and the livelihoods of coastal and fishing communities. Therefore, option (b) is the correct answer. 9 This

Set 3.q: 113. With reference to the appointments of Governors and Lieutenant Governors in March 2026, consider the following pairs: 1. Delhi: V.K. Saxena 2. West Bengal: R.N. Ravi 3. Bihar: Lt. General (Retired) Syed Ata Hasnain
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: According to the press communique of the President’s Secretariat dated 5 March 2026, R.N. Ravi was appointed as the Governor of West Bengal and Lieutenant General (Retired) Syed Ata Hasnain was appointed as the Governor of Bihar. Therefore, pairs 2 and 3 are correct. Taranjit Singh Sandhu took over as the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, while Vinai Kumar Saxena was appointed as the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh. Hence, pair 1 related to Delhi is incorrect. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b), 2 and 3 only.

Set 3.q: 114. With reference to Safeena Husain, included in TIME's 'Women of the Year 2026' list, consider the following statements: 1. Founder of 'Educate Girls'. 2. Honoured with Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2025.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Safeena Husain is the founder of “Educate Girls”. The initial work of the organisation was linked to Rajasthan, and it was formally established as an independent organisation in 2007. This organisation works to bring out of-school girls into formal education, increase enrolment and strengthen girls’ education in rural areas. In 2025, Educate Girls/Foundation to Educate Girls Globally was honoured with the prestigious Ramon Magsaysay Award. It became the first Indian non-profit organisation to receive this honour. Therefore, both statements are correct.

Set 3.q: 115. Which statement is true with reference to the recently released book 'Mahatma: A Great Communicator'?
options: Its author is Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya.
The book is based on Mahatma Gandhi's military strategic skills.
It analyzes how Mahatma Gandhi made khadi, the charkha and silence effective means of communication.
It has been published only in English by a private foreign publisher.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The author of “Mahatma: A Great Communicator” is Dr. Dhiraj Kakadia, Additional Director General, Akashvani. This book was released by Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya at Gandhi Darshan, Rajghat, New Delhi. The book focuses on Mahatma Gandhi’s effective mass communication skills. It explains how Gandhiji used symbols and practices such as khadi, the charkha and silence as effective means of public awareness and communication of ideas during the freedom movement. This book has been published in Hindi, English and Gujarati by the Publications Division, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India.

Set 3.q: 116. What is the main geostrategic objective of NATO's military exercise 'Cold Response 2026', conducted in the Arctic region?
options: To control China's naval activities in the Pacific Ocean.
To strengthen the collective security, Arctic warfare capability and strategic presence of NATO member countries in harsh Arctic conditions.
To protect scientific research centres on the Antarctic continent.
To prepare a counter-terrorism security mechanism for the Suez Canal trade corridor.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: “Cold Response 2026” was a Norwegian-led, NATO associated biennial winter military exercise held from 9–19 March 2026, mainly in northern Norway, northern Finland and the maritime areas off the coast of northern Norway. Its objective was to strengthen the collective defence preparedness, Arctic/cold-weather operational capability, interoperability and strategic presence of NATO allies in harsh Arctic/High North conditions. This exercise was also part of NATO’s enhanced vigilance activity, Arctic Sentry, which aims to strengthen NATO’s deterrence capability and defence posture in the Arctic and High North region. Due to Russia’s military activity in the Arctic, China’s growing interest, climate-change-driven opening of sea routes, and energy/critical mineral resources, the geostrategic importance of this region has increased.

Set 3.q: 117. What is the main focus of Project 'HANUMAN' launched by the Andhra Pradesh government?
options: To enhance drone-based security in the border areas of the state.
To reduce human-wildlife conflict through AI-based systems and rapid response units.
To protect crops from monkey menace in rural areas.
To promote afforestation near religious tourism sites.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Project HANUMAN — Healing and Nurturing Units for Monitoring, Aid and Nursing of Wildlife — launched by the Government of Andhra Pradesh is an initiative related to reducing human wildlife conflict and promoting human-wildlife coexistence. It was launched by Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and Forest and Environment Minister Pawan Kalyan. The project includes a total of 100 special vehicles, including 93 Rapid Response and Rescue Vehicles and 7 wildlife ambulances, 4 wildlife rescue and treatment centres, and an AI-based wildlife monitoring and early warning system. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 3.q: 118. Consider the following statements with reference to Mobile World Congress (MWC) 2026: 1. Held in Barcelona, Spain. 2. India formally announced 'India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026'.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The Mobile World Congress (MWC) 2026 was held from 2–5 March 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. India’s Union Minister of Communications Jyotiraditya M. Scindia led India’s engagements and inaugurated the Bharat Pavilion. Through this pavilion, India’s telecom manufacturing capabilities and innovation ecosystem were showcased. On the same platform, the IMC 2026 Curtain Raiser was unveiled, and it was announced that the India Mobile Congress 2026 would be held from 7–10 October 2026 in New Delhi. Therefore, both statements are correct.

Set 3.q: 119. Who became the first Indian economist to be honoured with the 'Alumni Award for Professional Achievement' by the University of Chicago?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Indian economist Dr. K. V. Subramanian was honoured by the University of Chicago with the Professional Achievement Award under its Alumni Awards. He became the first Indian economist to receive this honour in the 85-year tradition of the University of Chicago Alumni Awards. Dr. Subramanian served as the 17th Chief Economic Adviser to the Government of India from 2018 to 2021 and later served as India’s Executive Director at the IMF, representing India and South Asia.

Set 3.q: 120. What is the primary geographical and social focus area of the 'Statement of Intent' (SoI) signed by NITI Aayog and UNICEF India in March 2026?
options: Improving the health of slum dwellers only in metro cities.
Improving maternal and child nutrition and health outcomes in Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks.
Running a special malaria control programme in the North-Eastern states.
Developing digital infrastructure for higher education in tribal areas.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: The main objective of the Statement of Intent signed between NITI Aayog and UNICEF India is to strengthen nutrition and health outcomes in Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks. collaboration focuses on improving maternal and child nutrition outcomes in underserved and high-priority areas.

Set 3.q: 121. Which author of the famous book 'India Unbound' was recently honoured with the 'Lifetime Libertarian Award'?

Set 3.q: 125. Consider the following statements regarding the appointment of High Court judges: 1. President appointed Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari as CJ of Madras High Court. 2. Appointment falls completely within the special prerogative of the Governor.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: According to the notification dated 5 March 2026, the President appointed Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari as the Chief Justice of the High Court of Madras under Article 217(1) of the Constitution of India. According to Article 217(1), the appointment is made by the President, and there is a constitutional provision for consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State concerned. In practice, this process moves forward on the basis of the recommendations of the Supreme Court Collegium. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 3.q: 131. With reference to the main administrative and technical changes in Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 recently approved by the Union Cabinet, which of the following is not correct?

Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, the duration of the mission has been extended up to December 2028. A major strategic change has been made in it. Now, the focus of the mission is not only on pipelines or infrastructure creation, but also on long-term service delivery of regular, adequate and safe drinking water, operation and maintenance, sustainability of water sources, digital monitoring and Gram Panchayat-based accountability. Under the “Sujalam Bharat” digital framework, a system of unique Sujal Gaon or Service Area IDs has been introduced for the digital mapping of villages/service areas. Through the “Jal Arpan” process, the formal handover of drinking water schemes/ assets and the participation of Gram Panchayats have been promoted. Therefore, option (b) is not the correct answer.

Set 3.q: 134. According to the SIPRI report 'Trends in International Arms Transfers, 2025', consider...: 1. During 2021-2025, India remained the world's largest arms importer. 2. At the global level, USA is the largest exporter of arms (42%).

Set 3.q: 136. With reference to the renowned historian Professor K. N. Panikkar, who recently passed away... 1. Professor of Modern Indian History at JNU... 2. Famous work is 'Against Lord and State...'

He was also the President of the Indian History Congress in 2008. Set 3.q: 138. Which country has become the first to approve the world's first iPS cell-derived therapy 'AMCHEPRY' for the treatment of Parkinson's disease?
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Japan became the first country to approve the allogeneic iPS cell-derived dopaminergic neural progenitor cell product AMCHEPRY for the treatment of Parkinson’s disease. In Parkinson’s disease, dopaminergic neurons in the brain are damaged. This causes a deficiency of dopamine, leading to tremors, stiffness, slow movement and balance-related problems in patients. In AMCHEPRY, dopaminergic neural progenitor cells are prepared from allogeneic iPS cells. These are transplanted into the putamen region of the brain so that they can help compensate for the deficiency related to the dopamine system. iPS cell technology is considered a highly important achievement of modern regenerative medicine. For the original discovery in this field, Japanese scientist Shinya Yamanaka, along with Sir John B. Gurdon, received the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Therefore, the correct answer to this question is Japan.

Set 3.q: 139. Consider the following statements regarding Google's ambitious USD 15 billion 'America-India Connect'... 1. Subsea gateway in Visakhapatnam. 2. Most landing stations currently in Mumbai and Chennai. 3. Submarine cables carry >95% global internet traffic.
Set 3.explanation: Explanation: Google’s America India Connect initiative is associated with the five-year, USD 15 billion AI infrastructure investment announced in India. Under this, a new international subsea gateway will be established in Visakhapatnam/Vizag. India’s existing international submarine cable connectivity has mainly been concentrated at the landing points of Mumbai and Chennai. Therefore, the Visakhapatnam gateway will increase route diversity and network redundancy. This will provide alternative connectivity in case of any disruption or disaster on a major cable-landing route. This initiative also includes new subsea paths and strategic fiber-optic routes connecting India with Singapore, South Africa and Australia. Submarine cables are fiber-optic cables laid on the seabed, and a very large part of global internet traffic passes through them. Hence, all three statements are correct.

This designation is associated with the UN’s #MakeASafetyStatement global road safety awareness campaign, which echoes the Second Decade of Action for Road Safety 2021–2030. The aim is to increase awareness in the field of road safety and reduce deaths and injuries caused by road accidents, with the target of halving road traffic deaths and injuries by the year 2030.

Set 4.q: 1. Among the persons engaged in the following occupations, who are at risk of permanent changes in the DNA of their cells? 1. Those conducting research using the carbon-14 isotope 2. X-ray technicians 3. Coal miners 4. Dyers and painters
Set 4.explanation: DNA is a nucleic acid that carries the genetic information of organisms. A permanent change in DNA is called a mutation. The factors that cause mutations are called mutagens. These mutagens may be physical or chemical. Carbon-14 is a radioactive isotope. Researchers working with Carbon-14 may face radiation-related risk in cases of unsafe exposure or internal contamination. X-ray technicians may also be exposed to ionising radiation; therefore, they have a risk of DNA damage or mutation. Dyers and painters remain occupationally exposed to dyes, paints, solvents and certain chemicals. Some of these substances may show genotoxic or mutagenic effects. On the contrary, in this question, coal miners are not included among the major risk groups for permanent changes in DNA. Therefore, the correct code is 1, 2 and 4, i.e. the correct answer is option (c).

Set 4.q: 7. The reason for fatigue felt in muscles after prolonged hard physical work is
options: Slight wear and tear of muscle fibres
Set 4.explanation: During prolonged strenuous physical work, muscles require more energy. When the supply of oxygen is not sufficient to meet this requirement, partial anaerobic breakdown of glucose/glycogen takes place in the muscles and lactic acid is formed. The accumulation of lactic acid may cause fatigue or cramps in the muscles. During rest, and when blood circulation increases through massage or warm water, the oxygen supply to the muscles increases, which helps in the breakdown and removal of lactic acid.

Set 4.q: 8. The technique of chromatography is used for
Set 4.explanation: Chromatography is an important separation technique, whose main purpose is to separate the different components of a mixture. In this technique, the components of a mixture behave differently with two phases—the stationary phase and the mobile phase. The component that has greater affinity for the mobile phase moves relatively farther, while the other components lag behind. Due to this difference, the components of the mixture are separated. It is worth noting that the name chromatography is related to colours because initially it was used to separate coloured substances. However, in modern science, it is used for the separation, identification and purification of both coloured and colourless substances. Therefore, among the given options, the most appropriate answer is—to separate substances from a mixture.

Set 4.q: 9. Match List-I with List-II: A. Auxin B. Gibberellin C. Cytokinin D. Abscisic acid | 1. Cell growth 2. Cell division 3. Growth inhibitor 4. Apical dominance
Set 4.explanation: Plant hormones control the growth, development and various responses of plants. Auxin is produced in the apical part of the plant and helps in maintaining apical dominance by inhibiting the growth of lateral buds. Gibberellin promotes growth in plants, especially the elongation of the stem or axis. The main function of cytokinin is to promote cell division. Abscisic acid is a growth-inhibiting hormone and is also associated with plant responses under adverse conditions. Therefore, the correct matching is A-4, B-1, C-2 and D-3, which is given in option (b).
