Set 8.q: 26. During the Indian freedom struggle, the Khudai Khidmatgars, also known as the Red Shirts, called for
options: the union of Pashtun tribal areas of the north-west with Afghanistan
the adoption of terrorist tactics and methods to terrorize the colonial rulers and finally remove them
the adoption of communist revolutionary ideology for political and social reform
Pathan regional nationalist unity and a struggle against colonialism
Set 8.explanation: The Khudai Khidmatger Movement was led by Khan Abdul Ghaffar khan. He was also known as ‘Frontier Gandhi’ because the made non-violence the foundation of his political Struggle. Members of his organisation wore red shirts; therefore, they were called ‘Red Shirts’. The objective of this movement was to promote regional unity, social reform, education, and political awareness among the Pashtun (Pathan) society. It was associated with the non-violent struggle against British colonial rule and played an important role in the Indian National Movement, expecially in Civil Dis-Obedience Movement. The Khudai khidmatgar's did not call for the merger with Afghanistan, nor did they advocate a communist revolution or the adoption of communist ideology. Their main appeal was for Pashtun regional/ national unity and resistance against British colonialism. Therefore, option (d) is correct.

Set 8.q: 27. Who issued silver coins with a Sanskrit inscription on one side?
28. Who moved the Purna Swaraj Resolution at the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress?
Set 8.explanation: The resolution of Purna Swaraj was presented by Gandhiji in the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress. J. L. Nehru was the President of the Lahore Session of 1929, and under his presidency, the Congress formally accepted the demand for Purna Swaraj. Speaking in his presidential address at this session, Nehru said, “Today we have only one goal, the goal of freedom. For us, freedom means complete independence.” It should be noted that in this Lahore Session itself, the Nehru Report was rejected, in which only Dominion Status had been demanded.

Set 8.q: 29. In which of the following relief sculpture inscriptions is ‘Ranyo Ashoka’ (King Ashoka) mentioned along with the stone portrait of Ashoka?
Set 8.explanation: A Buddhist stupa is located at Kanaganahalli on the bank of the Bhima River in Kalaburagi district of Karnataka. Here, a portrait of Emperor Ashoka with his queen has been carved on stone, below which ‘Ranyo Ashoka’ (King Ashoka) is written in the Brahmi script.

Set 8.q: 30. The Congress policy of prayer and petition ultimately came to an end
options: under the leadership of Aurobindo Ghosh
under the leadership of Bal Gangadhar Tilak
under the leadership of Lala Lajpat Rai
under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi
Set 8.explanation: In the early Moderate phase of the Congress, the policy of prayer, petition, and constitutional representation was adopted to obtain reforms from the British government. Due to the limited results of this policy, extremist nationalist ideology emerged within the Congress. Bal Gangadhar Tilak considered Swaraj, Swadeshi, boycott, and mass struggle to be more effective means. Tilak is regarded as the principal leader of this policy. Therefore, the correct answer is (b).

Set 8.q: 31. Who gave the slogan ‘Inquilab Zindabad’?
Set 8.explanation: The slogan Inquilab Zindabad was coined by Maulvi Hasrat Mohani, while Bhagat Singh and his revolutionary companions popularised this slogan.

Set 8.q: 32. The success of the Theosophical Society in India was mainly due to
Set 8.explanation: In 1879, Colonel Olcott and Madame Blavatsky came to India and established the headquarters of the Theosophical Society at Adyar, near Madras. In 1889, Mrs. Annie Besant became a member of this society, and after coming to India in 1893, she played the most active role for the society. Mrs. Annie Besant regarded ancient Hinduism as one of the most profound and spiritual religions in the world. Theosophy, or Brahma Vidya, supported the spiritual philosophy of Hinduism, the theory of karma, and the theory of the rebirth of the soul. The Theosophical Society was a movement associated with the religious and cultural renaissance of modern India. For this reason, Annie Besant was able to connect the Indian people with it, which became the main reason for its success.

Set 8.q: 33. Who among the following negotiated the Subordinate Alliances of 1817–18 with the Princely States of Rajputana?
Set 8.explanation: The negotiations for the subsidiary treaties of 1817–18 with the princely states of Rajputana were conducted by Charles Metcalfe. Lord Hastings appointed Charles Metcalfe, the then Resident of Delhi, as the negotiator to ensure British paramountcy over Rajputana and Rajputana’s neutrality towards the Marathas and the Pindaris.

Set 8.q: 34. Match List-I with List-II: A. British Indian Association B. Bombay Presidency Association C. Central National Mohammedan Association D. Servants of India Society | 1. Gopal Krishna Gokhale 2. K.T. Telang 3. Radhakanta Deb 4. Syed Ameer Ali
Set 8.explanation: The British Indian Association was established in Calcutta in October 1851. Its founding members Rajendralal included Mitra, Radhakanta Deb (President), Harish Chandra Mukherjee, Debendranath Tagore (General Secretary), etc. The Bombay Presidency Association was established in Bombay in 1885. Its founding members included Firoz Shah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji, K. T. Telang, etc. Syed Ameer Ali established the Central National Muhammadan Association. Gopal Krishna Gokhale formed the Servants of India Society in 1905.

Set 8.q: 35. The Third Sangam was held at
Set 8.explanation: Sangam means an assembly or council. The literature composed by Tamil poets in these assemblies, or Sangams, is called “Sangam literature.” During the Sangam Age, three Sangams were organised in South India under the patronage of the Pandya kings— First Sangam Place – Madurai Presided over by – Sage Agastya Second Sangam Place – Kapatapuram (Alaivai) Presided over by – Sage Agastya (later Tolkappiyar) Third Sangam Place – Madurai Presided over by – Nakkirar

Set 8.q: 36. In which Industrial Policy Resolution was the idea of the ‘Joint Sector’ for industrial development in India proposed?
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: India’s second industrial policy was announced in April 1956. This policy was inspired by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru’s socialist outlook and the concept of a “socialistic pattern of society.” Its main objective was to accelerate the pace of industrialisation in the country and strengthen the role of the public sector in economic development. In this policy, priority was given to the expansion of the public sector and cooperative sector, more equal distribution of income and wealth, and control over monopolistic tendencies.

Set 8.q: 37. Consider the following expenditure heads in the Bihar Budget 2026–27: 1. Revenue Expenditure – ₹2,84,134 crore 2. Capital Outlay – ₹39,377 crore 3. Net Expenditure – ₹3,24,925 crore. Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
Set 8.explanation: Revenue expenditure is related to regular expenses such as general administration, salaries, pensions, interest, grants, and subsidies, while capital outlay is related to asset creation. In the Bihar Budget 2026–27, revenue expenditure is estimated at ₹2,84,134 crore, capital outlay at ₹39,377 crore, and net expenditure, that is, total expenditure excluding debt repayment, at ₹3,24,925 crore. Therefore, all three pairs are correct, and the correct answer is (d) 1, 2 and 3.

Set 8.q: 38. Which of the following is not a cause of low productivity in Indian agriculture?
Set 8.explanation: The major reasons for the low productivity of Indian agriculture include population pressure, disguised unemployment, and the small size of landholdings. Greater dependence of the population on agriculture increases pressure on agriculture, disguised unemployment reduces the real productive contribution of labour, and small landholdings limit the use of mechanisation and modern technology. On the other hand, cooperative farming is a means of agricultural development, because small farmers can jointly use resources through it.

Set 8.q: 39. Which of the following is correct about the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
options: It grants loans to any country.
It grants loans only to developing countries.
It grants loans only to member countries.
It grants loans to the central bank of a country.
Set 8.explanation: The International Monetary Fund is an international financial institution that provides financial assistance to its member countries to deal with balance-of payments difficulties and economic crises. It does not lend to just any country, nor is it limited only to developing countries. Unlike development banks, the IMF does not provide loans for any specific development project; rather, it helps member countries restore economic stability. Therefore, the correct answer is (c) It gives loans only to member countries.

Set 8.q: 40. Consider the following statements with reference to Jananayak Karpoori Thakur Kisan Samman Nidhi: 1. It is a state-level farmer income-support scheme... 2. Under this scheme, farmers will receive ₹3,000 per year. 3. This amount will be in addition to the Central Government’s PM-KISAN scheme.
Set 8.explanation: According to the Bihar Budget 2026–27, the Jannayak Karpoori Thakur Kisan Samman Nidhi is a state-level farmer income-support scheme of the Bihar government. Under this scheme, farmers will be given ₹3,000 per year. This amount will be in addition to the ₹6,000 per year received under the Central Government’s Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi. Therefore, all three statements are correct, and the correct option is (d).

Set 8.q: 41. Which of the following institutions together constitute the World Bank? 1. International Bank for Reconstruction and Development 2. International Finance Corporation 3. International Development Association 4. International Monetary Fund
Set 8.explanation: The World Bank Group consists of five institutions— the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Development Association, the International Finance Corporation, the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, and the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes. Among the options given in the question, only 1, 2 and 3 are related to the World Bank Group. The International Monetary Fund is not part of the World Bank Group. Therefore, the correct answer is (a) 1, 2 and 3.

Set 8.q: 42. V. V. Giri National Labour Institute is located in
Set 8.explanation: The V. V. Giri National Labour Institute is located in Noida, Uttar Pradesh. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India. It was established in 1974 for the purpose of labour-related research, training, and education. Therefore, the correct answer is (a) Noida.

Set 8.q: 43. Excise duty on liquor is levied by
Set 8.explanation: Excise duty on alcoholic liquors for human consumption is levied by the State governments. Under Entry 51 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, the States have been given the power to levy excise duty on alcoholic liquors for human consumption manufactured or produced in the State. Entry 8 of the State List is related to the regulation of production, manufacture, possession, transport, purchase and sale of intoxicating liquors, whereas the clear basis for taxation is Entry 51.

Set 8.q: 44. Match List-I with List-II: A. Grey Revolution B. Pink Revolution C. Silver Revolution D. Red Revolution | (1) Onion production (2) Tomato and meat production (3) Egg production (4) Fertilizer
Set 8.explanation: According to the given options, the Grey Revolution is related to fertilizers, the Pink Revolution is related to onion production, the Silver Revolution is related to egg production, and the Red Revolution is related to tomato and meat production. Therefore, the correct matching is A–4, B–1, C–3, D–2, and the correct answer is (b).

Set 8.q: 45. Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
Set 8.explanation: After the formation of the First Lok Sabha, its first sitting was held on May 13, 1952. On May 15, 1952, Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was elected as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha. His tenure continued until his death on February 27, 1956. Thus, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 8.q: 46. A person can contest a Panchayat election if that person has completed
Set 8.explanation: The age-related provision for Panchayat elections is given in Article 243F of the Indian Constitution. According to this provision, if a person has attained the age of 21 years, he cannot be disqualified from being chosen as a member of a Panchayat merely on the ground that he is less than 25 years of age. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 8.q: 47. Which one of the following Chief Justices of India acted as President of India?
Set 8.explanation: Justice M. Hidayatullah was the Chief Justice of India and also served as the Acting President. In 1969, V. V. Giri resigned from the office of Vice-President to contest the Presidential election. At that time, a vacancy arose in both the offices of the President and the Vice-President. In such a situation, the Chief Justice of India has to discharge the functions of the President. For this reason, Justice M. Hidayatullah served as the Acting President from July 20, 1969 until V. V. Giri assumed the office of President on August 24,

Set 8.q: 48. Who was the Chairman of the first Law Commission of independent India?
Set 8.explanation: The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory body, which is constituted by the Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India. The first Law Commission of independent India was constituted in the year 1955. The then Attorney General of India, M. C. Setalvad, was appointed as its Chairman. As per the current update, the Chairperson of the 23rd Law Commission is Justice (Retd.) Dinesh Maheshwari.

Set 8.q: 49. Under the Indian Constitution, which of the following does the concentration of wealth violate?
Set 8.explanation: Under the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution, it is provided that the State shall, in particular, direct its policy in such a manner that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good [Article 39(b)]; and that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment [Article 39(c)]. Thus, concentration of wealth violates the Directive Principles of State Policy under the Indian Constitution. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 8.q: 50. Consider the following statements: I. The Chief Election Commissioner... is paid a salary equal to that of a Supreme Court Judge. II. The term of office... six years or 65 years. III. An Election Commissioner may resign by writing to the Chief Election Commissioner.
Set 8.explanation: At present, the Election Commission of India consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and two other Election Commissioners, who are appointed by the President. The Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners have the same status as Judges of the Supreme Court of India and receive salary and allowances equivalent to those of such Judges. The term of office of the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commissioners is 6 years from the date on which they assume office or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. Thus, statements I and II are correct. Statement III is not correct, because an Election Commissioner may, at any time, resign from his office by writing under his hand addressed to the President, and not to the Chief Election Commissioner. In other words, Election Commissioners address and submit their resignation to the President, because the President is their appointing authority.

Set 8.q: 51. Match the following correctly: A. Art. 19(1)(b) B. Art. 20 C. Art. 21 D. Art. 19(1)(d) | (i) To move freely... (ii) Procedure established by law (iii) To assemble peaceably... (iv) Protection in respect of conviction...
Set 8.explanation: The correct matching is as follows Art. 19(1)(b) – To assemble peaceably and without arms Art. 20 – Protection in respect of conviction for offences Art. 21 – Procedure established by law Art. 19(1)(d) – To move freely throughout the territory of India Therefore, the correct sequence is A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(i). Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 8.q: 52. Who proposed the merger of the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission?
Set 8.explanation: M. V. Mathur had proposed the merger of the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission. This proposal was related to the duplication of functions of both institutions and the need for better coordination in the assessment of financial assistance to the States. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution, whereas the Planning Commission was an extra constitutional body. At present, NITI Aayog is functioning in place of the Planning Commission. Therefore, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 8.q: 53. If the annual Union Budget is not passed by the Lok Sabha, then
options: the budget is amended and presented again.
the budget is sent to the Rajya Sabha for suggestions.
the Union Finance Minister is asked to resign.
the Prime Minister tenders the resignation of the Council of Ministers.
Set 8.explanation: If the Annual Union Budget is not passed by the Lok Sabha, it means that the government has lost its majority in the Lok Sabha. In such a situation, the Prime Minister will tender the resignation of the Council of Ministers. According to Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This means that the Union Government can remain in office only as long as it enjoys the majority support of the Lok Sabha. Thus, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 8.q: 54. Which of the following are the functions of the Election Commission of India? 1. To conduct elections for Speaker/Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha and Chairman of Rajya Sabha. 2. To conduct elections for municipalities... 3. To decide all doubts and disputes arising out of elections.
Set 8.explanation: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, whereas the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the members of the respective Houses. Disputes arising from elections are decided by the judiciary. Elections to Municipalities and Municipal Corporations are conducted by the State Election Commission. Thus, none of the given statements is correct.

Set 8.q: 55. Consider the following statements: 1. The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. 2. The Public Accounts Committee consists of members of the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and some well-known persons from industry and trade.
Set 8.explanation: The main function of the Public Accounts Committee is to examine the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General on the Appropriation Accounts of the Government of India. This committee has a total of 22 members. Out of these, 15 members are elected from among the members of the Lok Sabha by the method of proportional representation through the single transferable vote, while 7 members are elected by the Rajya

Set 8.q: 56. The Sarkaria Commission was established to review which of the following relations?
options: Between the Prime Minister and the President
Between the Legislature and the Executive
Between the Centre and the States
Between the Executive and the Judiciary
Set 8.explanation: To examine Centre State relations and to suggest measures for strengthening them, a commission was constituted in June 1983 under the chairmanship of Justice R. S. Sarkaria. B. Sivaraman and S. R. Sen were its other two members. The commission submitted its report in January 1988.

Set 8.q: 57. A candidate in a Lok Sabha election forfeits his/her security deposit if he/she fails to secure—
Set 8.explanation: In a Lok Sabha election, the security deposit of a candidate is forfeited when he is not elected and does not secure more than 1/6 of the total valid votes polled by all candidates. In other words, if he secures 1/6 or less of the valid votes, his security deposit is forfeited. Thus, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 8.q: 58. Assertion (A): Tanks are a major means of irrigation in Peninsular India. Reason (R): Most of the rivers of the Peninsular region are rain-fed.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) explains (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) does not explain (A).
Set 8.explanation: Due to the rocky and undulating nature of the land in the peninsular region, the development of large canal systems and wells in many parts has not been as easy as in the alluvial plains of North India. Besides this, most rivers of Peninsular India are rain-fed, due to which there is often a lack of regular water supply in canals during the dry season. In such a situation, tanks serve as a major means of irrigation in Peninsular India. Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka, situated in the Western Ghats, and flows westward in an arc-shaped course before joining the Arabian Sea. Hence, statement (a) is incorrect. Karwar and Kaiga are located on the banks of this river. The Deccan Plateau is a triangular plateau region located to the south of the Narmada River. The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats form its western and eastern edges, respectively. The Western Ghats are a high and extensive mountainous region running parallel to the Arabian Sea coast, and the slope gradually becomes gentle towards the east. The major rivers originating from the Western Ghats and flowing eastwards follow the slope and form deltas in the Bay of Bengal. Hence, the reason (R) is correct.

Set 8.q: 59. Which canal system in India is among the oldest and most developed in the world?
Set 8.explanation: One of the oldest and well-developed canal systems of India is the Ganga Canal. It was constructed by the then Maharaja of Bikaner, Shri Ganga Singh, and was completed in the year 1927. This canal takes off from the Sutlej River near Hussainiwala, close to Firozpur.

Set 8.q: 60. Which state of India is the only diamond-producing state?
Set 8.explanation: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2024, Madhya Pradesh is the only producer of diamond in India. In the year 2023-24(P), a total of 349 carats of diamond was produced in Madhya Pradesh.

Set 8.q: 61. Assertion (A): The Kali River, in the southern part of India, is an east-flowing river. Reason (R): The Deccan Plateau is higher on its western edge and has a gentle slope towards the Bay of Bengal in the east.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 8.explanation: The Kali River originates near Diggi village in Sabha. No minister can be elected as a member of this committee. As per convention, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha appoints a member of the Opposition as the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee. Therefore, statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false, because there is no provision for electing any outside person related to industry and trade, apart from members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, to the Public Accounts Committee.

Set 8.q: 62. With reference to ‘Lake Victoria in Africa’, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. This lake is surrounded by four countries. 2. It is located in the African Rift Valley.
Set 8.explanation: Lake Victoria, one of the Great Lakes of Africa, is located among three countries—Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya. Lake Victoria is not located in a rift valley. It is situated in a shallow plateau depression between the Western and Eastern Rift Valleys.

Set 8.q: 63. According to the Census of 2011, which of the following states had the highest population growth rate?
Set 8.explanation: State Population Growth Rate (2011 Census) Arunachal Pradesh 26% Bihar Meghalaya Punjab

Set 8.q: 64. The basis for determining the standard time of a place is—
Set 8.explanation: The standard time of a place or region is determined on the basis of longitude. Generally, for a country, an appropriate longitude is selected as the standard meridian, and the local time of that meridian is accepted as the standard time of the whole country or region. The International Date Line is located approximately at 180° longitude. Set 8.q: 65. Match List-I with List-II: A. Cauvery B. Krishna C. Narmada D. Chambal | 1. Almatti 2. Mettur 3. Gandhi Sagar 4. Sardar Sarovar
Set 8.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Dam – River Almatti Dam – Krishna River Mettur Dam – Cauvery River Gandhi Sagar Dam – Chambal River Sardar Sarovar Dam – Narmada River Thus, it is clear that option (b) is the correct answer.

Set 8.q: 66. The Strait of Hormuz is located—
options: Between the Black Sea and the Dead Sea
Between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman
Between the Arabian Sea and the Red Sea
Between the Red Sea and the Mediterranean Sea
Set 8.explanation: The Strait of Hormuz is located between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman. It connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and further with the Arabian Sea. Iran is located to its north, while the Musandam Peninsula of Oman is located to its south. It is one of the important sea routes of the world.

Set 8.q: 67. Basaltic lava rocks were formed on the Deccan Plateau of India in—
Set 8.explanation: The Deccan Plateau is famous for its basaltic lava rocks. These rocks were formed by the deposition of fluid basaltic lava that came out during massive volcanic eruptions. These rocks were formed from the Cretaceous to the Palaeocene period. Hence, on the basis of the given options, the correct answer will be option (a).

Set 8.q: 68. The Kumaon Himalaya is located between which of the following rivers?
Set 8.explanation: The Kumaon Himalaya is located between the Sutlej and Kali rivers. The part of the Himalayas lying between the Indus and Sutlej rivers is known as the Punjab Himalaya, the part lying between the Kali and Teesta rivers is known as the Nepal Himalaya, and the part lying between the Teesta and Dihang rivers is known as the Assam Himalaya.

Set 8.q: 69. Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
Set 8.explanation: The matching of the projects given in the options with their related rivers is as follows— (Project) – (River) Dulhasti – Chenab Indira Gandhi Canal – Sutlej Nagarjuna Sagar – Krishna Ukai – Tapti Thus, option (c) is not correctly matched.

Set 8.q: 70. In the north-western plain of India, the amount of winter rainfall caused by western disturbances gradually decreases—
Set 8.explanation: Western disturbances originate in the Mediterranean region, which cause winter rainfall in the northwestern parts of the Indian subcontinent. In the northwestern plains of India, the amount of winter rainfall caused by western disturbances gradually decreases from west to east. This is opposite to the normal pattern of south-west monsoon rainfall in the North Indian plains, which decreases from east to west. This rainfall is beneficial for Rabi crops.

Set 8.q: 71. Match List-I with List-II: A. Jaunsari B. Santhal C. Bhil D. Lepcha | 1. Jharkhand 2. Madhya Pradesh 3. Uttarakhand 4. Sikkim
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: (Tribe) – (Place of Residence) Jaunsari – Uttarakhand Santhal – Jharkhand Bhil – Madhya Pradesh Lepcha – Sikkim

Set 8.q: 72. Match List-I with List-II: A. Alps B. Vosges C. Vindhya D. Fujiyama | 1. Block Mountain 2. Volcanic Mountain 3. Fold Mountain 4. Residual Mountain
Set 8.explanation: The matching of the mountain ranges given in the options with their types is as follows— Alps – Fold Mountain Vosges – Block Mountain Vindhya – Residual Mountain Fujiyama – Volcanic Mountain

Set 8.q: 73. Radiation absorbed by plants results in—
Set 8.explanation: The light energy absorbed by plants is used in the light reaction of photosynthesis. In this process, photolysis of water takes place, in which water molecules break down to form oxygen, protons [H+] and electrons [e–]. The free oxygen goes into the atmosphere, while the electrons and H+ further help in the formation of energy-carrier molecules. Therefore, the main result of radiant energy received by plants is the photolysis of water.

Set 8.q: 74. Denitrification results in—
options: an increase in the amount of atmospheric nitrogen
an increase in the amount of lithospheric nitrogen
no effect on the amount of lithospheric and atmospheric nitrogen
Set 8.explanation: Nitrogen release, or denitrification, is an anaerobic process of the nitrogen cycle. In this process, nitrate and nitrite ions present in the soil are converted into nitrogen gas by denitrifying bacteria. This nitrogen gas returns to the atmosphere. Therefore, denitrification increases the amount of atmospheric nitrogen, while the amount of available nitrate in the soil decreases. Hence, the correct answer is (a).

Set 8.q: 75. Which of the following chemicals is used for ripening fruits?
Set 8.explanation: Calcium carbide [CaC2 ] reacts with moisture or water to produce acetylene gas [C2 H2 ], which can stimulate the ripening process of fruits. For this reason, it has been used for the artificial ripening of fruits. However, this method is harmful to health, and under food-safety rules in India, the ripening of fruits with calcium carbide/carbide gas is prohibited. For safe and permitted artificial ripening, ethylene gas is used in controlled quantities.

Set 8.q: 76. Pasteurization is related to—
Set 8.explanation: Pasteurization is a process by which pathogenic microorganisms present in liquids such as milk are destroyed or inactivated, thereby improving their shelf life. In the process of pasteurization, milk is kept at a temperature of 70°C to 85°C for 16 seconds. After that, it is rapidly cooled and preserved. This process was discovered by the French scientist Louis Pasteur. Hence, it is called pasteurization.

Set 8.q: 77. The working principle of an atomic bomb is nuclear fission of uranium, and the working principle of a hydrogen bomb is—
options: explosion of a bomb containing hydrogen gas
Set 8.explanation: The hydrogen bomb is based on the process of nuclear fusion. In it, enormous energy is released by the fusion of deuterium and tritium. It is based on an uncontrolled fusion reaction.

Set 8.q: 78. Which of the following hormones regulates blood calcium and phosphate in the human body?
Set 8.explanation: Parathyroid hormone regulates blood calcium and phosphate. Parathyroid hormone is secreted by the parathyroid glands, located on the posterior surface of the thyroid gland in the neck. This hormone regulates blood calcium and phosphate.

Set 8.q: 79. Match List-I with List-II: A. Ammeter B. Hygrometer C. Spring balance D. Barometer | 1. Pressure 2. Weight 3. Electric current 4. Relative humidity
Set 8.explanation: An ammeter is used to measure the electric current flowing in an electric circuit. A hygrometer is used to measure the relative humidity of the atmosphere. A spring balance is used to measure the weight of an object. A barometer is used to measure atmospheric pressure.

Set 8.q: 80. Which of the following temperature scales has no negative values?
Set 8.explanation: Temperature values on the Celsius, Fahrenheit and Réaumur scales can be negative, whereas temperature on the Kelvin scale cannot be negative.

Set 8.q: 81. Which one of the following is an insectivorous plant?
Set 8.explanation: The pitcher plant is an insectivorous plant. Its leaves are modified into pitcher-shaped structures. Digestive fluid is present inside the pitcher. Insects slip on its smooth surface and fall inside, and cannot come out. Later, they are digested with the help of digestive enzymes, and the plant obtains nutrients such as nitrogen from them.

Set 8.q: 82. Which of the following quantities has no unit?
Set 8.explanation: The ratio of the change in the original length or dimension of an object to its original length or dimension is called strain. Since it is the ratio of two quantities of the same kind, it is a dimensionless quantity and has no unit. In contrast, the unit of stress and pressure is pascal [N/m²], while the unit of force is newton.

Set 8.q: 83. Which of the following gases has the lowest percentage by volume in the atmosphere?
Set 8.explanation: In the atmosphere, nitrogen is found in about 78% by volume and oxygen in about 20.95% by volume. The amount of argon is about 0.93%. The amount of carbon dioxide is much less than these, around 0.04%. Therefore, among the given options, carbon dioxide has the lowest percentage in the atmosphere.

Set 8.q: 84. Highly dense stars are called—
Set 8.explanation: Stars with extremely high density are called neutron stars. They are generally extremely dense stellar remnants formed after the supernova explosion of massive stars. In them, matter remains compressed at a very high density.

Set 8.q: 85. As soon as a train starts moving, the head of a passenger sitting in it leans backward. The reason for this is—
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: Passengers lean backward when a train suddenly starts moving. The reason is that the lower part of the passenger’s body, which is in contact with the train, starts moving along with the train, but the upper part tries to remain at rest due to inertia of rest. As a result, the upper part of the passenger’s body bends backward.

Set 8.q: 86. The atmosphere exerts very high pressure on us, but we do not feel it because—
options: Our blood exerts a pressure slightly greater than atmospheric pressure.
Our bones are very strong and can bear this pressure.
The surface area of our head is very small.
Set 8.explanation: The atmosphere exerts pressure on our body from all directions, but under normal conditions we do not feel it because the internal pressure of the fluids and tissues present inside our body balances the external atmospheric pressure. Therefore, no unbalanced pressure is felt on the body. When we go underwater, external pressure increases with depth, so pressure is felt in the ears and some parts of the body.

Set 8.q: 87. ICT stands for—
Set 8.explanation: ICT stands for Infor mation and Communication Tech nology. ICT includes information technology as well as telecommuni cations, broadcasting media, and all types of audio and video processing and transmission.

Set 8.q: 88. The image formed by a concave mirror is real, inverted and equal in size to the object. What should be the position of the object?
options: Between the focus and the centre of curvature
Set 8.explanation: If the object is placed at the centre of curvature, the image formed by a concave mirror is real, inverted and of the same size as the object. It should be noted that if the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is concave, it is called a concave mirror.

Set 8.q: 89. Which one of the following is used as an explosive?
Set 8.explanation: Nitroglycerin is a heavy, colourless, oily explosive liquid. It is also known as glyceryl trinitrate.

Set 8.q: 90. Which one of the following is not a true fruit?
Set 8.explanation: When only the ovary takes part in the formation of a fruit, it is called a true fruit. On the other hand, when other parts of the flower, especially the thalamus, also take part along with the ovary in the formation of a fruit, it is called a false fruit or pseudocarp. In an apple, the edible fleshy part is mainly formed from the thalamus; therefore, apple is not a true fruit. Grapes, dates and plums are considered true fruits. mainly made from deer antlers. It was excavated in 1962-63 by Prof. V. K. Sinha.

Set 8.q: 91. Water can dissolve more substances than any other liquid because—
options: It is a good conductor of heat.
It is an oxide of hydrogen.
Set 8.explanation: Water is called a universal solvent because it can dissolve many substances. The main reason for this is the polar/dipolar nature of the water molecule. In a water molecule, the oxygen end is partially negative and the hydrogen end is partially positive. Due to this, water easily dissolves ionic and polar substances.

Set 8.q: 92. What is the reason for the absence of an atmosphere on the Moon?
options: It receives light from the Sun.
On it, the escape velocity is less than the root mean square velocity of gas molecules.
Set 8.explanation: The Moon has no atmosphere. An atmosphere is a mixture of many gases. The value of escape velocity on the Moon is about

Set 8.q: 93. In the official state-level audition held at the NIFT campus in Patna, who among the following was selected as ‘Miss Universe Bihar 2026’...?
Set 8.explanation: In the ‘Miss Universe Bihar 2026’ event held at the NIFT campus in Patna, Rupali Bhushan from Khagaria was selected as ‘Miss Universe Bihar 2026’. With this victory, she will represent Bihar in the grand finale of ‘Miss Universe India 2026’. In the competition, Nikita Kumari was the first runner up and Khushi Singh was the second runner-up.

Set 8.q: 94. Which statement is incorrect with reference to ‘Baraila Lake’ located in Vaishali district of Bihar...?
options: This lake is spread over about 1,625 hectares, a part of which was declared a bird sanctuary in 1997.
This lake is connected with the ‘Noon River’ and other local water streams...
This sanctuary is named after the famous ornithologist Dr. Salim Ali and freedom fighter Jubba Sahni.
It has been declared Bihar’s first Ramsar site.
Set 8.explanation: Statement (d) is incorrect. Barela Lake, also known as Salim Ali Jubba Sahni Bird Sanctuary, is located in the Vaishali district of Bihar. It has not been declared the first Ramsar site of Bihar. Bihar’s first Ramsar site is Kabar Taal/Kanwar Lake, located in Begusarai, which was included in the Ramsar List in 2020.

Set 8.q: 95. Who is considered the Creator of Modern Bihar?
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: Sachchidanand Sinha was a famous political leader, educationist, advocate and journalist of India. He is considered the ‘chief architect of the modern province of Bihar’. He was the soul of the ‘movement for the separation of Bihar from Bengal’, and the formation of Bihar and Orissa Province was the result of his tireless efforts. Sachchidanand Sinha was made the first temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly.

Set 8.q: 96. The earliest culture of the archaeological site of Chirand in Bihar is—
Set 8.explanation: The archaeological site named Chirand in the Saran district of Bihar belongs to the Neolithic culture. A large number of bone tools have been found here,

Set 8.q: 97. Recently, an agreement has been reached between the Government of Bihar and Cambodia’s Tourism Department... Which site is not included in this Buddhist Circuit...?
Set 8.explanation: Among the given options, Vaishali, Kesariya and Rajgir are associated with the major Buddhist sites of Bihar. Vaishali is famous for Lord Buddha’s last sermon and the Buddha relic stupa. Kesariya Stupa is located in East Champaran, and Rajgir is associated with the teachings of Lord Buddha and the Griddhakuta Hill. Shravasti is not in Bihar, but is a major Buddhist site located in Uttar Pradesh. Lord Buddha spent a long period and many rainy-season retreats there.

Set 8.q: 98. At which three places has the Central Government started site surveys for setting up nuclear power plants to make Bihar self-reliant...?
Set 8.explanation: In the context of the Central Government’s target of achieving 100 GW nuclear energy capacity by 2047, technical studies are being conducted for possible sites of nuclear power plants in Bihar. For this, site surveys are being conducted at three places—Siwan, Banka and Rajauli—for setting up nuclear power plants.

Set 8.q: 99. In April 2026, the Central Government announced that the Bihar Police would be awarded the highest national honour, the ‘President’s Police Colour Award’... Which of the following statements is false?
options: After receiving this honour, personnel... will be able to wear a special badge...
The Bihar Police has the highest participation of women in the country...
The Emergency Response System ‘Dial-112 (ERSS)’ has been appreciated at the national level.
Bihar is the first state in India to receive the honour of the ‘President’s Police Colour Award’ in the police category.
Set 8.explanation: Statement (d) is incorrect. In April 2026, it was announced that Bihar Police would be honoured with the ‘President’s Police Colour’, but it is not the first state police force in India to receive this honour. Among state police forces, this honour had already been received by the Uttar Pradesh Police in 1952. In the tradition of the ‘President’s Colour’, the first honour was given to the Indian Navy in 1951.

Set 8.q: 100. After returning from South Africa, Gandhiji launched his first successful Satyagraha in—
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: After returning from South Africa in January 1915, Gandhiji launched his first successful Satyagraha in the Champaran district of Bihar in 1917. In 1916, a farmer from Champaran, Rajkumar Shukla, met Gandhiji in Lucknow and requested him to come to Champaran. By the end of the 19th century, German chemical dyes had replaced indigo in the market. As a result, the European planters of Champaran were forced to stop indigo cultivation. The farmers also wanted to get rid of indigo cultivation. Taking advantage of the helplessness of the farmers, the European planters arbitrarily increased the rent and other illegal taxes to release them from the contract. Gandhiji started the Champaran Satyagraha against this exploitation of the farmers.

Set 8.q: 101. Recently, after notorious Maoist commander Suresh Koda surrendered to the ‘Special Task Force’ (STF)... Bihar has been declared completely ‘Naxal-free’. Which of the statements are correct?
Set 8.explanation: Maoist commander Suresh Koda surrendered in Munger after evading arrest for about 25 years. After this, the Bihar Police claimed that the armed Naxalite squads active in the state had come to an end. DIG Rakesh Kumar declared Bihar ‘Naxal-free’. However, in 2025, 3 LWE/Naxalite incidents were recorded in Bihar; therefore, statement 2 is incorrect. Hence, statements 1 and 3 are correct.

Set 8.q: 102. Prabhavati Devi was a freedom fighter from which region?
Set 8.explanation: The women of Bihar made an important contribution to the freedom movement. Among these women, Sarla Devi, Prabhavati Devi, Rajvanshi Devi, Suniti Devi and Radhika Devi are prominent. Prabhavati Devi was a freedom fighter from Patna.

Set 8.q: 103. To reduce population pressure on major cities, the Bihar Government has planned to develop 11 satellite cities. Under this plan... which two specially selected cities have been chosen?
Set 8.explanation: The Bihar Government has planned to develop 11 satellite cities, or greenfield townships, to reduce population pressure on major cities. In this plan, apart from the 9 divisional headquarters, Sitamarhi and Sonpur have been selected as special cities. Sitamarhi will be developed for religious tourism, while Sonpur will be developed as an extension of Greater Patna.

Set 8.q: 104. Which city of Bihar is surrounded by five hills?
Set 8.explanation: Rajgir city of Bihar is surrounded by five rocky hills, which are also mentioned in the Mahabharata and the Ramayana. The hills of Rajgir are famous across the world from religious, historical and tourism points of view. The names of the five hills of Rajgir are Vipulgiri, Ratnagiri, Udayagiri, Swarnagiri and Vaibharagiri. Gaya is surrounded on three sides by small and rocky hills, whose names are Mangala Gauri, Shring Sthan, Ramshila and Brahmayoni.

Set 8.q: 105. What is the ‘Sawaiya-Dedha Exchange Model’ related to the ‘Seed Bank’ established by progressive farmer Vijay Giri of West Champaran, Bihar?
options: Providing a 25% to 50% subsidy by the government on the purchase of seeds.
A farmer returns pure seeds to the bank after the harvest, equal to one-and-a-quarter or one-and-a-half times the quantity of seeds taken...
Exchanging hybrid seeds for organic manure.
Selling traditional seeds in international markets at one-and-a-half times the price.
Set 8.explanation: The seed bank established by farmer Vijay Giri of West Champaran is based on ‘community seed exchange’. Farmers take seeds from the seed bank and, after harvesting the crop, deposit 1.25 times or 1.5 times the quantity of pure seeds back into the bank. This promotes the conservation of local seeds, seed availability and agricultural biodiversity. Hence, the correct answer is (b).

Set 8.q: 106. Who led the Salt Satyagraha in Bhagalpur?
Set 8.explanation: On 6 April 1930, the Civil Disobedience Movement began under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. In Bihar, the Salt Satyagraha started on 15 April 1930 in Champaran and Saran districts by making salt from saline soil. In Bhagalpur, the Salt Satyagraha was led by Mahadevlal Sarraf, Deepnarayan Singh, Rameshwar Narayan Agrawal, Kailash Bihari Lal and Jahrul Hasan Hashmi.

Set 8.q: 107. In December 2025, under the first GPS-tagging campaign in Bhagalpur district by the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), which rare migratory bird was tagged and named ‘Sonbarsa’?
Set 8.explanation: In December 2025, the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), under Bhagalpur’s first GPS-tagging campaign, fitted a GPS-GSM transmitter on a female Greylag Goose. This migratory bird was named ‘Sonvarsha’. The objective of the campaign was to study the bird’s migration route, habitat use and behaviour.

Set 8.q: 108. During British rule, in which year did Bihar get the status of a separate province?
Set 8.explanation: In December 1911, on the arrival of British Emperor George V and Queen Mary in India, a Durbar was organized in Delhi to welcome them. At the Delhi Durbar, the Emperor declared the annulment of the Partition of Bengal. Along with this, it was also announced that Bihar and Orissa would be separated from Bengal to form a new Bihar Orissa Province. This division came into effect in 1912. On April 1, 1936, Orissa was separated from Bihar.

Set 8.q: 109. With reference to sustainable development, consider the following statements— (1) On the basis of the global indicator framework... the UN Secretary-General presents the annual SDG Progress Report. (2) The Global Sustainable Development Report is produced once every quarter...
Set 8.explanation: For monitoring the global progress of the Sustainable Development Goals, two types of reports are referred to under the United Nations framework. The first is the SDG Progress Report, which is prepared annually. This report is prepared by the United Nations Secretary-General in cooperation with the UN system, and it is based on the global indicator framework, data received from national statistical systems, and information compiled at the regional level. Therefore, statement (1) is correct. The second is the Global Sustainable Development Report (GSDR). It is not a general annual progress report, but a comprehensive report that strengthens the science policy interface. It is not presented quarterly. Under the present arrangement, it is prepared every four years, so that policymakers may receive scientific and evidence based support in the quadrennial SDG review discussions. Therefore, statement (2) is incorrect.

Set 8.q: 110. Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a standard measure of what?
Set 8.explanation: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) is an indicator for measuring pollution in aquatic ecosystems. It indicates the amount of oxygen consumed by bacteria and microorganisms while decomposing organic matter under aerobic conditions, that is, in the presence of oxygen, at a specified temperature.

Set 8.q: 111. Which of the following increase(s) the nitrogen content of the soil? 1. Excretion of urea by animals 2. Burning of coal by humans 3. Death of vegetation
Set 8.explanation: Nitrogen in the soil can increase through many natural and human-induced processes. Urea excreted by animals is nitrogenous waste. Soil microorganisms can convert it into ammonia/ammonium and further into nitrate, which can be absorbed by plants. Similarly, when vegetation decays, its leaves, stems, roots, etc. are decomposed by decomposers. Through this decomposition, organic nitrogen returns to the soil. Burning coal is not directly a process like adding manure, but its combustion produces nitrogen oxides. These gases can enter the atmosphere and reach the land through rain or atmospheric deposition, thereby adding reactive nitrogen to the soil. Therefore, all three statements are related to increasing nitrogen in the soil.

Set 8.q: 112. In May 2026, in which state/Union Territory of the country was approval granted for the establishment of the first dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Police Station...?
Set 8.explanation: In May 2026, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Sardar Taranjit Singh Sandhu approved the establishment of Delhi’s first dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) police station. The objective of this initiative is to effectively achieve the target of a “Drug-free Delhi” by the year 2027. The ANTF functions under the Crime Branch of the Delhi Police, and its main objective is to take effective action against drug trafficking, supply chains, financial networks, and organized drug networks.

Set 8.q: 113. Consider the following statements with reference to the ‘Rishikesh–Neelkanth Ropeway Project’: 1. It will be the country’s first ‘green ropeway’ project... 2. The National Board for Wildlife has directed that special wildlife corridors...
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: The proposed ropeway from Rishikesh/Triveni Ghat to Neelkanth Mahadev Temple in Uttarakhand is being developed as the country’s first ‘green’/wildlife sensitive ropeway project. This route is related to the Rajaji Tiger Reserve area. Therefore, in the project, emphasis has been laid on not obstructing the natural movement and traditional corridors of wildlife such as Asian elephants, leopards, sambar, chital, etc. This project, costing about ₹450 crore, will be approximately 6.5 km long and may reduce the travel time to about 15 minutes.

Set 8.q: 114. Under the ‘Pride of Hills’ initiative... which state has recently been allocated an amount of ₹4,900 crore?
Set 8.explanation: ‘Pride of Hills’ is a component of special development assistance for hill states under SASCI 2026-27. Under this, a total provision of ₹25,000 crore has been made, of which ₹4,900 crore has been allocated to Arunachal Pradesh. This amount has been provided to support capital expenditure and infrastructure-related needs, keeping in mind the difficult geographical conditions, limited revenue capacity, and developmental challenges of hill states.

Set 8.q: 115. Frederic Soyez, the renowned French international player, has recently been appointed as the new head coach of which Indian sports team?
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: Former French international hockey player and experienced coach Frederic Soyez has been appointed as the new head coach of the Indian junior men’s hockey team. He has replaced two-time Olympic medallist P.R. Sreejesh, whose contract ended in December 2025 after the FIH Men’s Junior Hockey World Cup 2025. Soyez has more than 15 years of top-level coaching experience. He has also coached the national men’s hockey teams of France and Spain. Therefore, the correct answer is option (a).

Set 8.q: 116. The book ‘Apnapan’, written by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and released in May 2026, is mainly based on the leadership style and work ethic of which personality?
Set 8.explanation: The book ‘Apnapan: Narendra Modi Sang Mere Anubhav’, written by Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan, is based on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s personality, leadership, working style, and his approach towards nation-building. Published by Prabhat Prakashan, this book was launched on May 26, 2026, at the NASC Complex, Pusa, New Delhi. In it, the author has mentioned his experiences with Prime Minister Modi from the 1991 Ekta Yatra to various public roles, along with organizational work, good governance, sensitivity, and crisis-time leadership during the Covid-19 period.

Set 8.q: 117. On the occasion of ‘Endangered Species Day’ in May 2026, India’s first ‘satellite-tagged Ganges soft-shell turtle’ (Nilssonia gangetica) was released in which of the following national parks?
Set 8.explanation: On the occasion of Endangered Species Day 2026, a conservation achievement related to India’s first satellite-tagged Ganges softshell turtle came to light in Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve, Assam. According to detailed reports, this adult turtle was fitted with a satellite transmitter on April 28, 2026, and released into its natural habitat on the northern bank of the Brahmaputra River. On May 15, 2026, on Endangered Species Day, this achievement was prominently highlighted. The objective of this initiative is to identify the turtle’s seasonal/daily movement, home range, and nesting breeding habitats.

Set 8.q: 118. Who has become the first female coach in history to join the coaching staff of England’s senior men’s Test cricket team?
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: Former England wicketkeeper-batter Sarah Taylor became the first female coach in England’s senior men’s setup. In June 2026, she was appointed as the short-term fielding coach of the England team for the three-Test series against New Zealand. Sarah Taylor was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in 2025. She was associated with England’s 2009 and 2017 50-over Women’s Cricket World Cup-winning teams and was also part of the 2009 Women’s T20 World Cup-winning team.

Set 8.q: 119. With reference to ‘National Dengue Day 2026’ declared by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: National Dengue Day is observed every year in India on 16 May.
The main theme of this day for the year 2026 is 'Community Participation for Dengue Control...'
The Health Ministry observes the entire month of July every year as ‘Anti-Dengue Month’.
Dengue is a bacterial disease, which spreads mainly through the bite of an Anopheles mosquito.
Set 8.explanation: Statement (d) is false. Dengue is not a bacterial disease; rather, it is a mosquito-borne viral disease. It mainly spreads through the bite of an infected Aedes aegypti mosquito, not through the Anopheles mosquito. In India, National Dengue Day is observed every year on 16 May. The theme for the year 2026 is “Community Participation for Dengue Control: Check, Clean and Cover”. The Ministry of Health observes the month of July as Anti Dengue Month.

Set 8.q: 120. What is the name of India’s first artificial intelligence (AI)-based combat aircraft being developed by Indian AI warfare company Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace (FWDA)...?
Set 8.explanation: Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace (FWDA), in collaboration with Portugal’s SKETCHPIXEL LDA, is working on a project related to the AI-based autonomous combat aircraft/UAV ‘FWD Kaal Bhairava E2A2’. The company has presented it as India’s first AI-based combat aircraft. It includes capabilities such as AI-based target identification, swarm coordination and encrypted communication.

Set 8.q: 121. The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC)... launched the country’s first ‘hydrogen-powered shuttle bus service’ in Delhi’s Central Vista area. Between which two stations will this service operate?
Set 8.explanation: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) launched a hydrogen-powered shuttle bus service in the Central Vista area from 15 May 2026. This service provides last-mile connectivity between the Central Secretariat and Seva Tirth metro stations and connects major government offices and sites in the Central Vista area. Under this initiative, Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) provided two hydrogen-powered buses to DMRC. This step is important for promoting green mobility, clean energy and environment-friendly public transport.

Set 8.q: 122. What is the official song of the ‘FIFA World Cup 2026’, to be jointly hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico in June 2026?
Set 8.explanation: The official song of the FIFA World Cup 2026 is ‘Dai Dai’. It has been performed by global artists Shakira and Burna Boy. FIFA released it on 15 May 2026 as the Official FIFA World Cup 2026 Song. The royalties from this song will support the FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund, which aims to provide children with access to quality education and football opportunities. The FIFA World Cup 2026 is being held from 11 June to 19 July 2026 in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

options: India has been nominated as the Chair of this Board till April 2028.
India is represented on this Board only by the country’s NITI Aayog.
India has been included in it as a member for the first time in the year 2026.
The main function of this Board is to examine monetary liquidity and credit parameters at the global level.

Set 8.q: 124. In May 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was honoured with the ‘Grand Cross of the Royal Norwegian Order of Merit’, the highest honour bestowed on foreign Heads of Government by which country?
Set 8.explanation: On 18 May 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred the ‘Grand Cross of the Royal Norwegian Order of Merit’ by Norway’s King Harald V in Oslo, the capital of Norway. It is Norway’s highest honour awarded to foreign heads of government. This honour is given for outstanding service in the interest of Norway and humanity. The Royal Norwegian Order of Merit was instituted in 1985 by King Olav V. This was the first visit by an Indian Prime Minister to Norway in 43 years.

Set 8.q: 125. Consider the following statements regarding the ‘Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026’... 1. After this amendment, the number of judges... has increased from 33 to 37. 2. Including the Chief Justice of India (CJI), the total number... will now be 38.
Set 8.explanation: On 16 May 2026, President Droupadi Murmu promulgated the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026. Through this Ordinance, Section 2 of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956 was amended, increasing the maximum sanctioned strength of judges, excluding the Chief Justice, from 33 to 37. Therefore, after including the Chief Justice of India, the total sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court is 38.

Set 8.q: 126. Where will India’s first ‘Mega Greenfield Shipyard’, based on Industry 4.0 technologies, be developed to achieve the goals of the ‘Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047’?
Set 8.explanation: India’s first mega greenfield shipyard will be developed at Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu. For this, a tripartite MoU was signed on 20 April 2026 among HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering Co., Ltd. (HD KSOE), National Shipbuilding & Heavy Industries Park, Tamil Nadu Limited (NSHIP-TN) and Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL). The proposed shipyard will have an annual capacity of 2.5 million GT. This project will promote advanced manufacturing, digital shipbuilding and green shipping technologies, and will make an important contribution to enhancing India’s shipbuilding capacity under the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.

Set 8.q: 127. Which Taiwanese bank became the first to open a bank branch at GIFT City in Gujarat, which hosts India’s International Financial Services Centre (IFSC)?
Set 8.explanation: Taiwan’s CTBC Bank Co., Ltd. has opened its branch at the International Financial Services Centre in GIFT City, Gujarat. With this, it became the first Taiwanese bank to establish a branch presence in GIFT City.

Set 8.q: 128. Which state has become the first in India to successfully complete all priority areas under Deregulation Phase I and Phase II... to promote ‘Ease of Doing Business’?
Set 8.explanation: Tripura became the first state in India to complete all the prescribed priority reform areas under Deregulation Phase-I and Phase-II of the national Compliance Reduction and Deregulation Initiative. Phase-I was launched in February 2025 and included 23 priority areas. Phase-II was launched in January 2026 and included 28 priority areas. Thus, Tripura completed a total of 51 priority reform areas. Under these reforms, procedures were simplified in areas such as land use, urban development, industry, labour, environment, tourism, health, education and digital governance. Digitisation of approvals, a single-window system, self-certification and reduction of unnecessary compliance burden strengthened the state’s investment friendly regulatory environment.

In it, microalgae absorb carbon dioxide through the process of photosynthesis and release oxygen. Set 8.q: 131. Who has become the first woman officer in the history of the Indian Air Force (IAF) to obtain the highly challenging and prestigious Category-A Qualified Flying Instructor (Cat-A QFI) qualification?
Set 8.explanation: Squadron Leader Saanya has become the first woman officer of the Indian Air Force to earn the prestigious qualification of Category-A Qualified Flying Instructor (Cat-A QFI). Cat-A QFI is considered the top instructor rating related to flying training in the Indian Air Force. This qualification reflects a high level of flying skill, professional efficiency, training capability, and the ability to train military aviators effectively.

Set 8.q: 132. The two new books written by Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta, ‘The Bench, the Bar, and the Bizarre’ and ‘The Lawful and the Awful’, were recently released by whom?
options: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant
Set 8.explanation: On 10 May 2026, in New Delhi, Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah released two books by Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta— ‘The Bench, the Bar, and the Bizarre’ and ‘The Lawful and the Awful’. Many dignitaries, including the Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant, were present on this occasion. These books compile humour, satire, human nature, and interesting legal incidents from courtroom life.

Set 8.q: 133. Who has become the first Indian player in history to qualify for the Chess event of the prestigious ‘Esports World Cup 2026’ by winning the ‘Road to EWC’ qualifier at DreamHack Atlanta in the USA?
Set 8.explanation: Indian Grandmaster Aravindh Chithambaram won the Road to EWC 26: DreamHack Atlanta chess qualifier held in Atlanta, USA. With this achievement, he became the first Indian player to qualify for the chess event of the Esports World Cup 2026.

Set 8.q: 134. What official theme has been set by the United Nations for ‘World Bee Day 2026’, observed every year on 20 May?
options: Bee Together for People and the Planet – A Partnership That Sustains Us All
Honey Production and Ecosystem Balance in Bihar
Set 8.explanation: World Bee Day is observed every year on 20 May. Its objective is to raise awareness about the role of bees and other pollinators in the ecosystem, agriculture, food security, and biodiversity. The official theme for 2026 is “Bee Together for People and the Planet – A Partnership That Sustains Us All”. This day is associated with the birth anniversary of Anton Janša, a pioneer of modern beekeeping.

Set 8.q: 135. According to the latest report of ‘Swachh Survekshan Gramin-2025’... which state has been declared the best-performing state in India’s Eastern Zone...?
Set 8.explanation: In Swachh Survekshan Grameen-2025 (SSG 2025), Bihar was declared the best-performing state in the Eastern Region. This assessment was made on the basis of parameters such as rural sanitation, ODF Plus/ODF sustainability, solid and liquid waste management, functionality of sanitation infrastructure, and public participation. In the Eastern Region ranking, Bihar was followed by Odisha in second place, Jharkhand in third place, and West Bengal in fourth place. At the district level, Bhagalpur and Supaul of Bihar performed notably well.

Set 8.q: 136. What is the name of the world’s first rainfall index for weather derivatives, launched in India by NCDEX... to strengthen agricultural risk management?
Set 8.explanation: Explanation: Commodity The and National Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) launched India’s first SEBI-approved, exchange-traded weather derivative contract named RAINMUMBAI from 29 May 2026. It is based on Mumbai’s monsoon rainfall. Its basis is the Monsoon Cumulative Deviation Rainfall method, under which Mumbai’s actual rainfall during June to September is compared with the Long Period Average (LPA). Its objective is not to forecast weather, but to help manage rainfall-related risks in sectors such as agriculture, construction, logistics, and energy.

Set 8.q: 138. During the ASCEND 2026 Conference organized by the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA) in Washington, D.C., which historic mission of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was honoured with the 2026 Goddard Astronautics Award?
Set 8.explanation: The American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA) honoured the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) with the 2026 Goddard Astronautics Award. This honour was given for Chandrayaan-3’s historic soft landing near the Moon’s south polar region and its scientific achievements. India’s Ambassador Vinay Kwatra received the award on behalf of ISRO during the ASCEND 2026 conference in Washington, D.C. Chandrayaan-3 successfully soft-landed on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to land near the Moon’s south polar region. Its Pragyan rover also played an important role in the in-situ analysis of the elemental composition of the lunar surface.

Set 8.q: 139. Which of the following statements is true with reference to the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI)?
options: Senior IAS officer Saurabh Vijay took charge as the new Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of UIDAI in May 2026.
UIDAI manages the country’s tax regulatory framework under financial policies.
The new CEO Saurabh Vijay is originally a 1998-batch IAS officer of the Bihar cadre.
UIDAI functions completely under the direct administrative control of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs.
Set 8.explanation: Senior IAS officer Saurabh Vijay, a 1998-batch officer of the Maharashtra cadre, assumed charge as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) on 18 May 2026. He is a civil engineer from IIT Delhi. Therefore, statement (a) is true. Statement (c) is incorrect because he is not an officer of the Bihar cadre, but of the Maharashtra cadre. UIDAI is a statutory authority established under the Aadhaar Act, 2016, and functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). It is related to Aadhaar enrolment, authentication, and life-cycle management; it does not manage the country’s tax regulatory framework and is not under the direct administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Set 8.q: 140. On May 20, 2026, in Rome, Italy, which specialized agency of the United Nations conferred the prestigious Agricola Medal on Prime Minister Narendra Modi...?
Set 8.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was presented the ‘FAO Agricola Medal-2026’ by FAO Director-General Dr. QU Dongyu at the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in Rome on 20 May 2026. It is FAO’s highest honour. This honour was given in recognition of efforts such as food security, sustainable agriculture, rural development, financial inclusion, direct income support to farmers, and the promotion of Shree Anna/millets at the global level. The Prime Minister dedicated this honour to Indian farmers and the agricultural scientific community. This was the first visit by an Indian head of government/Prime Minister to the FAO headquarters in the last 30 years.

Set 9.q: 2. In which state of India does the Southwest Monsoon arrive first?
Set 9.explanation: The South-West Monsoon sets in over the state of Kerala in India. A major part of Indian agriculture is still dependent on rainfall.

Set 9.q: 3. Which of the following is also called the ‘Molassis Basin’?
Set 9.explanation: Mizoram is also called the ‘Molasse Basin’. In geology, the term ‘molasse’ is used for sedimentary deposits that accumulate near mountainous regions. The terrain of Mizoram is associated with the folded mountain structure of north-eastern India, and soft, loose and unconsolidated sedimentary deposits are found here. Tertiary sedimentary rocks such as sandstone, shale and siltstone are predominant in this region.

Set 9.q: 4. The stratosphere is considered ideal for the flight of jet aircraft because
options: Due to the ozone present in this layer, fuel consumption is reduced.
The temperature remains uniform in this layer, which is a favourable condition for engine efficiency.
This layer is beyond the striking range of anti-aircraft weapons.
Clouds and other weather phenomena generally do not occur in this layer.
Set 9.explanation: The stratosphere is the second major layer of the Earth’s atmosphere. This layer lies between the troposphere and the mesosphere. The stratosphere is very dry, and the amount of water vapour in its air is very low. Therefore, clouds and other weather phenomena generally do not occur in this layer. The lower stratosphere is considered ideal for commercial jet aircraft because it helps them avoid atmospheric disturbances.

Set 9.q: 5. The Lesser Himalaya lies between
options: The Trans-Himalaya and the Great Himalaya
The Shiwalik and the Great Himalaya
The Shiwalik and the Outer Himalaya
Set 9.explanation: The Lesser Himalayas are situated between the Shivaliks and the Great Himalayas. The longitudinal divisions of the Himalayas from north to south are as follows— Great Himalayas → Lesser Himalayas → Shivalik Himalayas.

Set 9.q: 6. Assertion (A): During the winter season, most parts of India remain dry. Reason (R): During the winter season, most parts of the country remain under the influence of the northeast trade winds.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) does not correctly explain (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) correctly explains (A).
Set 9.explanation: During the winter season in India, the weather remains dry in most parts of the country. At this time, the north-east trade winds prevail over most parts of the country. These winds blow from land towards the sea. Therefore, they contain less moisture. Due to the lack of moisture, these winds do not cause rainfall in most parts of India. This is why most parts of India remain dry in winter. Hence, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Set 9.q: 7. According to Köppen’s climate classification, which of the following suitably describes Northeastern India including North Bengal?
options: Tropical Wet and Dry Climate (Monsoon Savanna) (Aw)
Humid Subtropical Climate with Dry Winter (Cwg)
Set 9.explanation: According to Köppen’s climatic classification, the climate of India is classified on the basis of temperature and the seasonal distribution of rainfall. The monsoonal influence is clearly visible in northern Bengal and most parts of north-eastern India. This region receives sufficient rainfall during the summer and rainy seasons from the Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon, but rainfall is comparatively low in winter. For this reason, this region is placed under Cwg, i.e. a humid subtropical climate with a dry winter.

Set 9.q: 8. Which of the following geographical regions of the country is the oldest?
options: The mountainous region of the Himalayas
The Great Plain of North India
Set 9.explanation: Among the geographical regions given in the question, the Indian Peninsular Plateau is the oldest. It was formed due to the weathering and displacement of Gondwana land.

Set 9.q: 9. The Radcliffe Line between India and Pakistan is an example of
Set 9.explanation: The Radcliffe Line between India and Pakistan is an example of a superimposed boundary. A superimposed boundary is a boundary that is imposed by an external power on local cultural, ethnic, linguistic or resource-related realities. In 1947, India and Pakistan shared the boundary imposed by the British-ruled Government of India.

Set 9.q: 11. The extra-peninsular mountains of India were formed in—
Set 9.explanation: The Himalayas and the extra-Peninsular mountains of northern and north-eastern India were formed in the Cenozoic Era. Extra-Peninsular mountains refer to the northern mountainous region located outside the Peninsular Plateau of India, especially the Himalayan mountain system. The Himalayas are counted among the young fold mountains of the world. They were formed due to the northward movement of the Indian Plate and its collision with the Eurasian Plate. This mountain building process became mainly active during the Cenozoic Era.

Set 9.q: 13. Which of the following seas has the highest average salinity?
Set 9.explanation: Among the options given in the question, the Dead Sea has the highest salinity, i.e. 238‰ or 238 ppt. It is a highly saline, closed-drainage water body. There is no outlet for water here, and due to intense evaporation in the dry climate, the concentration of salts increases. In the Black Sea, salinity remains low due to the fresh water brought by rivers. The Yellow Sea is also comparatively less saline, while the Mediterranean Sea has high salinity due to evaporation, but it is still much lower than that of the Dead Sea.

Set 9.q: 14. Match the following— A. Niagara Falls B. Land of a Thousand Lakes C. Eiffel Tower D. Roof of the World | 1. Pamir 2. Paris 3. Finland 4. United States of America
Set 9.explanation: Niagara Falls is located on the Niagara River in North America, on the border between Canada and the United States of America. Finland is called the Land of a Thousand Lakes. The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris. The Pamir Plateau is called the ‘Roof of the World’.
