Set 10.q: 17. On which date did the Anti-Bengal Partition Movement begin?
Set 10.explanation: The British Government announced the decision to partition Bengal on 20 July 1905. On 7 August 1905, the Swadeshi Movement was formally announced at a historic meeting held at Calcutta Town Hall. The historic boycott resolution was passed in this meeting. After this, the Anti-Partition of Bengal Movement formally began in a united manner in various parts of Bengal. The Partition of Bengal came into effect on 16 October 1905.

Set 10.q: 18. During the reign of which Sultan did Khalisa land develop on a large scale?
Set 10.explanation: Khalisa land was royal land whose revenue went directly to the Sultan’s central treasury. The main objective of Alauddin’s revenue and land-revenue system was to establish a powerful and autocratic state. He confiscated land from all those persons who had received it in the form of milk (state-granted property), inam, idrarat/pensions, and waqf (charitable land), etc. As a result, Khalisa land expanded on a large scale.

Set 10.q: 19. Consider the following statements: 1. The deliberations of the Third Round Table Conference culminated in the passing of the Government of India Act, 1935. 2. The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for the formation of an All-India Federation...
Set 10.explanation: The Round Table Conferences were part of the British Government’s process of considering constitutional reforms in India. After the Third Round Table Conference, the constitutional proposals were carried forward as the White Paper of 1933, the Report of the Joint Select Committee, and finally the Government of India Act,

Set 10.q: 20. 'The principle of European democracy cannot be applied to India without recognizing the fact of communal groups.' Who said this?
Set 10.explanation: The given statement was made by Muhammad Iqbal in his speech delivered on 29 December 1930 at the 25th annual session of the All India Muslim League held at Allahabad. In the same speech, he said that India was not a homogeneous socio political unit like Europe; rather, many communities existed here on the basis of religion, language, complete independence, was proposed for India. In place of separate electorates on a communal basis, it proposed joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities. In addition, the Constitution proposed by it included provisions for Fundamental Rights, including Indians’ rights to freedom of speech, to publish newspapers, to hold meetings, to form associations, etc. Thus, statement 1 is incorrect, while statements 2 and 3 are correct.

Set 10.q: 21. With reference to the period of the Indian freedom struggle, which of the following was/were recommended by the Nehru Report? 1. Complete Independence for India 2. Joint electorates for reservation of seats for minorities 3. Provision of fundamental rights...
Set 10.explanation: In the Nehru Report (1928), Dominion Status, instead of the continuity of the Rajya Sabha, as nearly as possible, one-third of its members retire every two years. Therefore, statement 3 is correct. The minimum age for becoming a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years, not 25 years. Therefore, statement 4 is incorrect. Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

Set 10.q: 22. Consider the following statements regarding the Vedic deity Indra: 1. He was the god of storms. 2. He punished sinners. 3. He was the protector of moral order. 4. He was the god of rain.
Set 10.explanation: In the Rigveda, Indra is described as the most powerful deity, to whom 250 hymns are dedicated. He was the most popular deity of the Rigvedic period. Indra is regarded as the war leader of the Aryans and the god of rain, storms, and tempests. Indra is known by names such as Vritrasura-hanta, meaning the slayer of the demon named Vritrasura; Purabhid, meaning the breaker of forts; Somapa, meaning one who drinks a large quantity of Soma; and Shatakratu, meaning the possessor of a hundred powers. Varuna was called the protector of moral order. In addition, in some hymns of the Rigveda, prayers are offered to Indra and Soma to punish sinners. This makes it clear that Indra also punished sinners. Hence, option (d) is correct.

Set 10.q: 23. Who among the following headed the lawyers who were pleading on behalf of the Azad Hind Fauj in the Red Fort Trial in 1945?
Set 10.explanation: In the famous trial of the officers of the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) held at the Red Fort in 1945, the defence was conducted by Kailash Nath Katju, Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru, Asaf Ali, Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai, and others. This group of lawyers was headed by Bhulabhai Desai.

Set 10.q: 24. Who among the following is famous as ‘Deshbandhu’?
Set 10.explanation: Chittaranjan Das was known as “Deshbandhu.” Deshbandhu means “friend of the nation.” After studying law in England, Chittaranjan Das returned to India and became a barrister. His greatest success as a lawyer was defending Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case. He founded the Swaraj Party along with Motilal Nehru.

Set 10.q: 25. The social status given by Manu to foreigners in Indian society was—
Set 10.explanation: In Indian society, Manu gave foreigners the social status of Vratya Kshatriyas. Vratya Kshatriya means those Kshatriya or warrior groups that were considered to have deviated from Vedic rites and prescribed social norms. According to Manu, groups such as the Yavanas, Shakas, Paradas, and Pahlavas were originally related to the Kshatriyas, but due to the non-performance of prescribed rites and lack of contact with Brahmanas, their status was considered lower.

Set 10.q: 26. In which inscription are the various achievements of Rudradaman I described?
Set 10.explanation: An inscription of Rudradaman has been found at Junagadh in Gujarat. On the same rock on which this inscription is engraved, a copy of Ashoka’s Fourteen Major Rock Edicts and two inscriptions of Skandagupta are also engraved. Rudradaman’s inscription is written in pure Sanskrit and the Brahmi script. It clearly highlights the various achievements of Rudradaman. It contains information about the repair of Sudarshana Lake, the administrative system, Rudradaman’s military valour, and his personal qualities.

Set 10.q: 27. Consider the following— 1. Tughlaqabad Fort 2. Lodi Garden 3. Qutub Minar 4. Fatehpur Sikri. The correct chronological order is—
Set 10.explanation: After establishing the Tughlaq dynasty, Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq (1320–1325 A.D.) founded a city in Delhi and named it ‘Tughlaqabad’. For its protection, he got a fort constructed. Lodi Garden was built during the Lodi period (1451–1526 A.D.). The construction of Qutub Minar was started by Qutbuddin Aibak (1206–1210 A.D.) and was completed during the reign of Iltutmish (1211–1236 A.D.). Fatehpur Sikri was founded and built by Akbar (1556–1605 A.D.).

Set 10.q: 28. Match List-I with List-II: (a) Iqta (b) Jagir (c) Amaram (d) Mokasa | 1. Marathas 2. Sultans of Delhi 3. Mughals 4. Vijayanagara
Set 10.explanation: During the Delhi Sultanate period, with Iltutmish’s accession to the throne, the ‘Iqta system’ was established in India as the foundation of the administrative system. The Jagirdari system was prevalent during the Mughal period. In Vijayanagara, the king gave special land grants to the Nayakas in lieu of salary or for the maintenance of their subordinate army. These land grants were called ‘Amaram’. In the Maratha administration, 66 percent of the income from Chauth was given to Maratha chiefs for maintaining cavalry, which was called ‘Mokasa’.

Set 10.q: 29. Who among the following was the only Jewish Viceroy of India?
Set 10.explanation: The only Jewish Viceroy of India was Lord Reading (1921–1926 A.D.). During his tenure, the Chauri Chaura incident took place, the Swaraj Party was formed, and the Rowlatt Act was repealed. Charles Metcalfe was a Jewish Governor-General. Therefore, the correct answer is (d).

Set 10.q: 30. Which aspect is highlighted in Kautilya’s ‘Arthashastra’?
Set 10.explanation: Kautilya’s ‘Arthashastra’ provides information about governance, administration, penal policy, and the state system during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya. In fact, it is not a historical or economic text, but a unique work of political science. It mainly throws light on political policies. Topics related to economic life are also found in it, but they appear not as an independent economic history, but in the context of state administration and revenue policy.

Set 10.q: 31. How many seats were given to the Depressed Classes in the Communal Award and the Poona Pact respectively?
Set 10.explanation: The Communal Award of 1932 was a representation scheme announced by British Prime Minister MacDonald, in which the Depressed Classes were given representation on the basis of separate electorates. The number of reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in the provincial legislatures was 71, which was increased to 148 in the Poona Pact: Madras—30, Bombay including Sindh—15, Punjab—8, Bihar and Orissa—18, Central Provinces—20, Assam—7, Bengal—30, and United Provinces—20. Along with this, 18 percent of the seats allotted to the general electorate in the Central Legislature were reserved for the Depressed Classes.

Set 10.q: 32. Arrange the following events of Akbar’s reign in chronological order— 1. Abolition of Jizya 2. Construction of Ibadat Khana 3. Signing of the Mahzar 4. Establishment of Din-i-Ilahi
Set 10.explanation: Akbar abolished the Jizya tax in 1564 A.D. He established the Ibadat Khana at Fatehpur Sikri in 1575 A.D., whose purpose was to hold debates on philosophical and religious subjects. In order to bring all religious matters under his control, Akbar issued the ‘Mahzarnama’ in 1579 A.D. This Mahzarnama was prepared by Sheikh Mubarak, the father of Abul Fazl. To establish harmony among all religions, Akbar founded ‘Tauhid-i-Ilahi’ or ‘Divine Monotheism’ in 1582 A.D.

Set 10.q: 33. Which of the following statements about Wood’s Despatch are true? 1. The grants-in-aid system was introduced. 2. The establishment of universities was recommended. 3. English was recommended as the medium of instruction at all levels.
Set 10.explanation: ‘Wood’s Dispatch’ or ‘Wood’s Declaration’ was issued in 1854 A.D. by Charles Wood, the President of the Board of Control of the British East India Company. In this dispatch, a comprehensive plan for Indian education was presented. It discussed the aims, medium, reforms, etc., of education. This dispatch is also called the ‘Magna Carta of English Education in India’. In this dispatch, the government made the spread of Western education its objective. Emphasis was laid on imparting higher education through the medium of English; however, importance was also given to the development of native languages. According to this dispatch, arrangements were to be made for the establishment of one university each in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras on the model of the University of London. It emphasized that education imparted in government educational institutions should be secular. It also recommended the introduction of the Grant-in-aid system to encourage private efforts in the field of education.

Set 10.q: 34. Who among the following called the Government of India Act, 1935 a “Charter of Slavery”?
Set 10.explanation: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru strongly criticized the ‘Government of India Act, 1935’, calling it a “Charter of Slavery” or a “Slave Charter”. In this Act, provincial autonomy was granted, but special powers, reserved powers, and British control remained with the Governors and the Governor General. In the entire history of British rule, the Act of 1935 was the longest and most extensive document. It contained 14 parts, 321 sections, and 10 schedules.

Set 10.q: 35. Who among the following shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Munger?
Set 10.explanation: Mir Qasim shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Munger around 1762 A.D. He transferred the capital with the objective of running a more independent administration away from the interference of the English East India Company.

Set 10.q: 36. The Cabinet Mission was sent to India for which of the following purposes? 1. For the establishment of a national government 2. To prepare a constitutional arrangement for the transfer of power 3. To work out the details of Jinnah’s demand for Pakistan
Set 10.explanation: The Cabinet Mission was sent to India to prepare a constitutional arrangement for the transfer of British power in India, not to work out the details of Jinnah’s demand for Pakistan, nor to establish a national government. The Mission gave importance to the formation of an interim government, but the establishment of a ‘full national government’ was not its direct objective.

Set 10.q: 37. Who among the following founded the “Lathi Club”?
Set 10.explanation: The Lathi Club, Hindu Akhara, Ganapati Festival, Shivaji Festival, etc., were established or started by Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Their objective was to develop physical courage, the spirit of self defence, and national consciousness among the youth.

Set 10.q: 38. Consider the following statements— 1. The Sun Temple of Multan has been mentioned by Hiuen Tsang, Abu Zaid, Al-Masudi and Al-Biruni. 2. The Sambapura Yatra festival was related to Sun worship.
Set 10.explanation: The Sun Temple of Multan has been mentioned by Hiuen Tsang, Abu Zaid, Al-Masudi, and Al Biruni. Therefore, statement (1) is correct. Al-Biruni clearly wrote that the Hindus of Multan celebrated the ‘Sambapur Yatra’ festival in honour of the Sun. Therefore, statement (2) is also correct.

Set 10.q: 39. The head of the military department under the reorganized central administrative system during Akbar’s reign was—
Set 10.explanation: Under the reorganized central administrative system during Akbar’s reign, the ‘Mir Bakshi’ was mainly the head of the military department; however, he cannot be called the Commander-in-Chief. His duties were related to soldiers’ salaries and military organization. He presented recommendations before Emperor Akbar regarding the appointment and promotion of Mansabdars. The recruitment of soldiers, arrangement of their arms, inspection of soldiers, etc., came under his duties.

Set 10.q: 40. Alam Khan, one of those who invited Babur to invade India—
options: was a relative of Ibrahim Lodi and a claimant to the throne of Delhi.
was a relative of Ibrahim Lodi, who had been ill-treated and expelled...
was the father of Dilawar Khan...
was an heir to the province of Punjab...
Set 10.explanation: Alam Khan was the uncle of Ibrahim Lodi. Claiming his right to the throne of Delhi, he invited Babur to invade India. In 1524 A.D., during Babur’s fourth campaign in India, relations between Ibrahim Lodi, the Sultan of Delhi, and Daulat Khan, the Governor of Punjab, had become bitter. Sultan Ibrahim Lodi had ordered Daulat Khan to come to the capital, but Daulat Khan disobeyed the order. Daulat Khan sent his son Dilawar Khan to Babur with the message that Babur should help depose Sultan Ibrahim Lodi from the throne of Delhi and place Ibrahim Lodi’s uncle, Alam Khan, on it instead. For Babur, this was a golden opportunity because he had also received an invitation from Rana Sanga, the ruler of Mewar. Therefore, Babur became convinced that the opportunity to conquer India had arrived.

Set 10.q: 41. The Hathigumpha inscription is a source of information about which ruler?
Set 10.explanation: An undated inscription of the ruler Kharavela has been found from the ‘Hathigumpha’ Cave on Udayagiri Hill near Bhubaneswar in Odisha. It gives a systematic account of Kharavela’s childhood, education, coronation, and the events of the thirteen years of his reign after becoming king. This inscription is the only source for knowing the history of Kharavela.

Set 10.q: 42. Match List-I (Ancient Sites) with List-II (Archaeological Discoveries): A. Lothal B. Kalibangan C. Dholavira D. Banawali | 1. Ploughed field 2. Dockyard 3. Terracotta replica of a plough 4. Harappan script inscription
Set 10.explanation: Among the sites of the Harappan Civilization mentioned in the question, evidence of a dockyard has been found at Lothal, which is located near the Gulf of Khambhat. Evidence of a ploughed field has been found at Kalibangan, situated on the bank of the Ghaggar River in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan. From Dholavira in Gujarat, an inscription containing 10 large-sized signs of the Harappan script has been found. From Banawali, located in Fatehabad district of Haryana, a terracotta replica of a plough has been found.

Set 10.q: 43. Match List-I with List-II: A. Abul Kalam Azad B. Sarojini Naidu C. Motilal Nehru D. Dr. Rajendra Prasad | 1. Amritsar, 1919 2. Bombay, 1934 3. Kanpur, 1925 4. Ramgarh, 1940
Set 10.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— (President) – (Session) Abul Kalam Azad – Ramgarh, 1940 Sarojini Naidu – Kanpur, 1925 Motilal Nehru – Amritsar, 1919 Dr. Rajendra Prasad – Bombay, 1934

Set 10.q: 44. Annie Besant— 1. was responsible for starting the Home Rule Movement. 2. was the founder of the Theosophical Society. 3. was once the President of the Indian National Congress.
Set 10.explanation: Annie Besant was responsible for starting the Home Rule Movement in India. Annie Besant established the Home Rule League in Madras in September

Set 10.q: 45. Consider the following statements— 1. In the First Round Table Conference, Dr. Ambedkar demanded separate electorates... 2. In the Poona Pact, special provisions were made... 3. The Indian National Congress did not participate in the Third Round Table Conference.
Set 10.explanation: In the First Round Table Conference, Dr. Ambedkar put forward the demand for a separate electorate for the Depressed Classes. The Congress did not participate in the First and Third Round Table Conferences. The Poona Pact provided that no disability would be attached to members of the Depressed Classes in elections to local bodies or appointments to public services, and it also mentioned efforts to secure fair representation. However, it did not provide a clear system of reserved representation in this respect.

Set 10.q: 46. Which one of the following statements about the guild system of ancient India is false?
options: A guild was an organization of traders and artisans.
The quality and price of the goods produced were determined by the concerned guild.
The guild also controlled the conduct of its members.
The guild system was prevalent only in North India.
Set 10.explanation: In ancient India, a group of people engaged in the same craft, trade, or profession was known as a shreni or guild. One important reason for their origin was the localization of crafts and industries during the Later Vedic period. Guilds controlled the trade and commerce of the country, determined the quality and prices of goods, and also regulated the conduct of their members. References to the prevalence of guilds are found not only in North India but also in South India.

Set 10.q: 47. The Mughal emperor who prohibited the use of tobacco was—
Set 10.explanation: Tobacco came to India during the Mughal period through foreign trade contacts and soon became popular in the form of smoking. Within a few years, the habit of smoking tobacco became so widespread among the people that Jahangir had to issue an order against tobacco smoking in 1617 to prevent this harmful habit.

Set 10.q: 48. The Governor-General who followed a vigorous Forward Policy towards Afghanistan was—
Set 10.explanation: The Forward Policy was an active and aggressive frontier policy of British India, under which efforts were made to keep Afghanistan under British influence and to check Russian influence in Central Asia. In 1876, when Lytton became Viceroy, there was a change in the policy adopted towards Afghanistan. In place of the policy of Masterly Inactivity, the Forward Policy began to be pursued.

Set 10.q: 49. Who discovered DNA?
Set 10.explanation: DNA was first identified in 1869 by the Swiss scientist Friedrich Miescher. He separated a substance from the nucleus of the cell, which he named nuclein. Later, this substance was identified as DNA. James Watson and Francis Crick proposed the model of the double-helix structure of DNA. Therefore, the credit for the discovery of DNA is given to Friedrich Miescher, while Watson and Crick are famous for the structure of DNA.

Set 10.q: 50. By which enzyme is glucose converted into ethyl alcohol?
Set 10.explanation: The enzyme zymase converts glucose into ethyl alcohol, i.e. ethanol, and this process of conversion is called fermentation. C6 H12 O6 (aq.) Zymase Yeast (Glucose) 2C2 H5 OH (aq.) Ethanol + 2CO2 Carbon dioxide

Set 10.q: 51. Which of the following vitamins helps in retaining the memory of a dream for a sufficiently long duration?
Set 10.explanation: Vitamin B6 is considered helpful in recalling dreams for a longer time. It plays a role in the formation of neurotransmitters in the brain, which may affect the process of sleep and dream recall. Vitamin A is mainly related to vision, Vitamin D to bones and calcium absorption, and Vitamin C to immunity. Therefore, the correct answer is Vitamin B6 .

Set 10.q: 52. What does the pH value indicate?
options: The quality of the chemical used to prepare a photograph from a negative
A measure of whether a solution is acidic or alkaline
A measure of the intensity of an earthquake
A measure to test the purity of milk
Set 10.explanation: The pH value is a number through which the acidity and alkalinity of substances are expressed. Its value lies between 0 and 14. Solutions with a pH value of less than 7 are acidic. Solutions with a pH value of more than 7 are alkaline. The pH value of a neutral solution is 7. The pH value is defined as the negative logarithm of the activity of hydrogen ions in solution (H+).

Set 10.q: 53. In medicinal chemistry, the classification of drugs is most useful on which basis?
Set 10.explanation: Drugs can be classified on several bases, such as pharmacological effect, drug action, chemical structure, and molecular targets. Classification on the basis of pharmacological effect is useful for doctors, while chemical structure helps in understanding drugs having similar structural features. For medicinal chemists, classification on the basis of molecular targets is the most useful, because drugs show their effect by interacting with the body’s biomolecules, such as proteins, enzymes, receptors, and nucleic acids. Therefore, the correct answer is (b) molecular targets.

Set 10.q: 54. The most reactive among the halogens is—
Set 10.explanation: Halogens are highly reactive non-metallic elements of Group 17 of the periodic table. The main halogens include fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine. The reactivity of halogens decreases on moving from top to bottom because, with the increase in atomic size, the tendency to gain an electron decreases. Therefore, fluorine, being the smallest and the most electronegative, is the most reactive among the halogens.

Set 10.q: 55. Who was the first person to go into space?
Set 10.explanation: On April 12, 1961, the then Soviet Union achieved the distinction of sending the first human into space aboard the spacecraft named Vostok 1. Yuri Gagarin was the first person to undertake human space travel.

Set 10.q: 56. Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
Set 10.explanation: Deficiency of Vitamin A causes an eye disease called night blindness. Deficiency of Vitamin D causes rickets, which generally occurs in children. Deficiency of Vitamin C causes scurvy, in which bleeding of the gums occurs. Beriberi, caused by deficiency of Vitamin B1 , is a malnutrition-related disease.

Set 10.q: 57. Which of the following statements about graphite and diamond is true?
options: They have the same crystal structure.
They have the same electrical conductivity.
They can undergo similar chemical reactions.
Set 10.explanation: Diamond and graphite are chemically identical. Both are made up of carbon atoms. However, their atomic and crystalline structures are completely different. In diamond, each carbon atom forms bonds with four other carbon atoms, resulting in a hard three-dimensional structure, whereas in graphite, each carbon atom forms bonds with three other carbon atoms in the same plane, resulting in a hexagonal array.

Set 10.q: 58. Assertion (A): In India, electricity distribution companies calculate electricity consumption in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Reason (R): In India, the power system operates at a frequency of 60 Hz.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Set 10.explanation: In India Electricity Distribution companies calculate electricity consumption in kwh. For the normal operation of the power grid, electricity transmission in India is fixed at a frequency of 50 hertz. A decrease or increase of up to 0.5 hertz is permissible. If the frequency goes below or above this permissible limit, the grid fails.

Set 10.q: 59. Energy is stored in the liver and muscles in the form of—
Set 10.explanation: The cells of the body require energy to function. This energy is obtained from the chemical reactions of sugars, fats and proteins. Sugar is converted into glucose in the body, which is a simple sugar. It is absorbed and reaches various organs and tissues through the blood. In the liver and muscles, glucose, as an energy reserve, is mainly stored in the form of glycogen.

Set 10.q: 60. Which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: The boiling point of an aqueous solution is higher than the boiling point of pure water.
Adding solutes to a solution increases its water potential.
The vapour pressure of water in a solution is lower than the vapour pressure of pure water.
When a solution is separated from water by a semipermeable membrane, the flow of water can be stopped by applying pressure to the solution.
Set 10.explanation: When a solute or any other soluble substance is added to water, the boiling point of water increases because the solute particles present at the surface reduce the rate of evaporation of water. Due to this, the vapour pressure of water in the solution is lower than the vapour pressure of pure water. By applying external pressure equal to the osmotic pressure on the solution, the entry of the solvent into the solution can be prevented. Thus, the statements in options (a), (c) and (d) are correct, whereas the statement in option (b) is not correct.

Set 10.q: 61. What is the unit of atmospheric pressure?
Set 10.explanation: The bar is used to express atmospheric pressure. The bar is a non-SI unit of pressure. The SI unit of pressure is pascal [Pa]. One bar is equal to 105 pascals or 105 newtons per square metre.

Set 10.q: 62. Which of the following options is incorrect?
options: An atom is electrically neutral due to the presence of protons and electrons inside the nucleus.
Electrons are negatively charged and their mass is negligible.
The atomic number is the number of protons in an atom of an element.
Isotopes are useful as nuclear fuel, in the medical field, in carbon dating, etc.
Set 10.explanation: An atom is electrically neutral because the number of protons present in its nucleus is equal to the number of electrons present outside the nucleus. Protons are positively charged, electrons are negatively charged, and neutrons are neutral particles. Protons and neutrons are found in the nucleus of an atom, whereas electrons remain in energy levels outside the nucleus.

Set 10.q: 63. Which of the following pairs is/are correct? A. Aspirin – Painkiller B. Cotton – Cellulose C. Honey – Glucose and fructose D. Chloromycetin – Anti-typhoid drug
Set 10.explanation: Aspirin is a pain relieving medicine. Cotton fibres are mainly made up of cellulose. Honey mainly contains fructose and glucose sugars. Chloromycetin, whose active ingredient is chloramphenicol, has historically been used as a medicine in the treatment of typhoid fever. Therefore, all the given pairs are correct and the correct answer is (c) A, B, C and D.

Set 10.q: 64. Golden Rice has been enriched with—
Set 10.explanation: Golden Rice is a variety of Oryza sativa rice developed through genetic engineering for the biosynthesis of beta-carotene, which acts as a precursor of vitamin A in the edible grain.

Set 10.q: 65. Which one of the following vegetables grown underground is a modified root?
Set 10.explanation: Sweet potato is a plant of the family Convolvulaceae. It is perennial in nature, but in cultivation it is generally grown as an annual crop. In sweet potato, the adventitious roots arising from the nodes of the stem enter the soil and become thick and fleshy due to food storage. Therefore, sweet potato is considered a modified storage root. In contrast, potato is an example of a stem tuber and elephant foot yam is an example of a corm. Hence, the correct answer is (b) sweet potato.

Set 10.q: 66. When an air bubble rises from the bottom of a lake and reaches the surface, its size will—
Set 10.explanation: When an air bubble rises upward from the bottom of a lake, the pressure decreases as it moves upward compared to the bottom. Due to this, the volume of the air bubble increases.

Set 10.q: 67. Which one of the following layers of the atmosphere is responsible for the deflection of radio waves?
Set 10.explanation: The ionosphere is responsible for the reflection or deflection of radio waves. In this layer, gases are ionised due to high-energy radiation coming from the Sun, producing free ions and electrons. These ionised particles help in bending radio waves back towards the Earth. For this reason, the ionosphere is important for long-distance radio communication. Hence, the correct answer is (d) ionosphere.

Set 10.q: 68. A firefly is a type of—
Set 10.explanation: Fireflies, also known as khadyot, are insects of the family Lampyridae. They belong to the beetle group. Fireflies produce bioluminescence in their bodies, which is mainly used for attracting mates and signalling. Their glow is produced by the chemical reaction of a substance called luciferin, the enzyme luciferase, oxygen and ATP.

Set 10.q: 69. The aqueous solution of copper sulphate is acidic because this salt undergoes—
Set 10.explanation: The aqueous solution of copper sulphate [CuSO4 ] is acidic because it is a salt formed from the strong acid H2 SO4 and the weak base Cu(OH)2 . On dissolving in water, the Cu2+ ion undergoes hydrolysis with water and increases the concentration of H+/H3 O+ ions. Due to this, the solution becomes acidic. Therefore, the correct answer is (c) hydrolysis.

Set 10.q: 70. Which of the following statements are correct? (i) The small pores visible in the epidermis of leaves are called stomata. (ii) The guard cells present in the stomata help in the exchange of gases... (iii) The process of transpiration takes place through stomata.
Set 10.explanation: Stomata are found between the epidermal cells of leaves. Through them, plants carry out gas exchange with the atmosphere and transpiration. Stomata remain open in the presence of light and closed in darkness. This process is controlled by the decrease or increase in the turgidity of guard cells.

Set 10.q: 71. Match List-I with List-II: A. Stethoscope B. Sphygmomanometer C. Caratometer D. Lux meter | 1. For measuring the intensity of light 2. For determining the purity of gold 3. For listening to heart sounds 4. For measuring blood pressure
Set 10.explanation: Heartbeats are heard with the help of a stethoscope. Blood pressure is measured with a sphygmomanometer. The purity of gold is determined with the help of a carat meter. A lux meter is used to measure light intensity.

Set 10.q: 72. Select the components of the Green Revolution with the help of the given code— 1. Seeds of high-yielding varieties 2. Irrigation 3. Rural electrification 4. Rural roads and marketing
Set 10.explanation: The Green Revolution was related to the use of modern agricultural techniques and supporting rural infrastructure to increase agricultural production. Its major components included seeds of high-yielding varieties, irrigation, fertilizers, and other technological measures. Along with this, rural electrification promoted tube wells, pump sets, and agricultural mechanization, while rural roads and marketing systems helped agricultural products reach markets.

Set 10.q: 73. In which year was the Local Area Bank (LAB) Scheme introduced?
Set 10.explanation: The Local Area Bank Scheme was started in 1996. RBI issued guidelines for setting up Local Area Banks in the private sector on August 24, 1996. These were small private-sector banks, whose area of operation was generally limited to a maximum of three contiguous districts. Their objective was to use local savings for local investment in rural and semi-urban areas and to increase the availability of credit. was seen in Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh.

Set 10.q: 74. Consider the following statements: 1. For every sugar season, the Central Government fixes the Statutory Minimum Price of sugarcane. 2. Under the Essential Commodities Act, sugar and sugarcane are essential commodities.
Set 10.explanation: In sugarcane pricing, the Fair and Remunerative Price is now used in place of the Statutory Minimum Price. This change was made after the amendment to the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, on October 22, 2009. Therefore, Statement 1 is incorrect. Sugar and sugarcane are included under the control framework of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955; therefore, Statement 2 is correct. Hence, the correct answer is (b) 2 only.

Set 10.q: 75. In Budget 2026-27, which item accounted for the largest share of total receipts?
options: Goods and Services Tax and Other Taxes
Set 10.explanation: In Budget 2026-27, the largest share in total receipts was from Borrowings and Other Liabilities, which was 24%. This was followed by Income Tax at 21%, Corporation Tax at 18%, and GST and Other Taxes at 15%. Therefore, the correct answer is (b) Borrowings and Other Liabilities.

Set 10.q: 76. Globalisation does not include—
options: free flow of foreign direct investment
Set 10.explanation: Globalization means an increase in economic integration among countries, which mainly takes place through foreign trade and foreign investment. Therefore, reduction in import duties, abolition of import licensing, and free flow of foreign direct investment are measures related to globalization. In contrast, disinvestment of public sector equity is a process related to privatization and public asset management. It is not a direct component of globalization.

Set 10.q: 77. The Human Development Index is a composite index of—
options: nutritional status, quality of life and per capita Gross Domestic Product
poverty, life expectancy and educational attainment
life expectancy, educational attainment and per capita Gross National Product
inflation, unemployment and per capita Gross Domestic Product
Set 10.explanation: Explanation: The Human Development Index is published by the United Nations Development Programme. It is a composite index of three major dimensions of human development—a long and healthy life, knowledge, and a decent standard of living. In this index, a long and healthy life is measured by life expectancy at birth, knowledge is measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling, and standard of living is measured by Gross National Income per capita.

Set 10.q: 78. Which states of India benefited the most from the Green Revolution?
options: Punjab, Haryana and Western Uttar Pradesh
Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala
Set 10.explanation: The Green Revolution was an agricultural transformation process associated with the use of seeds of high-yielding varieties, irrigation, fertilizers, and modern agricultural techniques. Its greatest benefit went to those regions where irrigation, fertile land, and agricultural infrastructure were better. In India, the most positive impact of the Green Revolution full-fledged banking institution in 1983. Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

Set 10.q: 79. Who among the following put forward the idea of self-help groups as an effective tool for poverty alleviation?
Set 10.explanation: Professor Muhammad Yunus is credited with popularizing the idea of small loans and group based financial assistance in poverty alleviation. He worked toward providing small loans to the poor, especially women, in Bangladesh. In 1976, he started the Grameen Bank project, which later developed into a

Set 10.q: 80. Consider the following statements with reference to the Minimum Support Price (MSP)— 1. MSP is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP). 2. The final decision on MSP is taken by the Central Government. 3. The Government of India fixes MSP for 22 mandated crops.
Set 10.explanation: Explanation: The Minimum Support Price (MSP) provides farmers with minimum price protection for their produce. The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices recommends MSP, but the final decision on MSP is taken by the Central Government. The Government of India fixes MSP every year for 22 mandated agricultural crops. The objective of MSP is to provide farmers with a minimum assured price, encourage agricultural production, and support the food security system through government procurement. Therefore, all three statements are correct, and the correct answer is (d) 1, 2 and 3.

Set 10.q: 81. What is the objective of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana?
options: To bring micro and small entrepreneurs into the formal financial system
To provide loans to poor farmers for the cultivation of special crops
To provide pension to elderly and destitute people
To fund voluntary organizations engaged in skill development and employment generation
Set 10.explanation: The objective of the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana is to connect micro and small entrepreneurs with the formal financial system. Its aim is to provide credit facilities to small and micro enterprises under the concept of “funding the unfunded.” This scheme was launched on April 8,

Set 10.q: 82. After the Santhal Uprising subsided, which measure/measures were taken by the colonial administration? 1. The territories called ‘Santhal Parganas’ were created. 2. It became illegal for a Santhal to transfer land to a non-Santhal.
Set 10.explanation: The Santhal Rebellion of 1855-56 AD was mainly a famous tribal movement of the then Bihar and Orissa region. This rebellion continued until 1856 AD, and the British Government succeeded in suppressing it after a major military action. The British Government accepted the demand for a separate “Santhal Parganas” area and established peace in the region. After this, in 1855 AD, the Santhal Parganas district was created by carving out parts of Bhagalpur and Birbhum. Also, the transfer of land by any Santhal tribal person to a non-Santhal became illegal.

Set 10.q: 83. Choose the correct ascending order of the following districts of Bihar according to decadal population growth (2001–2011).
options: More than one of the above
Set 10.explanation: As per the given options, the correct ascending order of the districts of Bihar according to decadal population growth (2001-2011) is—Siwan (22.70) < Kishanganj (30.40) < Madhepura (31.12). Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Set 10.q: 84. According to the report ‘Tipping Point to Zero: Evidence towards a Child Marriage Free India’ released at the United Nations General Assembly, which position did Bihar secure among the states that recorded the highest reduction in child marriages among girls?
Set 10.explanation: According to the report “Tipping Point to Zero: Evidence towards a Child Marriage Free India,” Bihar secured the third position among the states that recorded a reduction in child marriage among girls. In this list, Assam ranked first and Maharashtra ranked second. A significant decline was recorded in cases of child marriage in Bihar, which reflects the success of awareness and government efforts in the state.

Set 10.q: 85. Which of the following pairs of industry and place is not correctly matched?
Set 10.explanation: “Rail Coach and Engineering” is related to Bharat Wagon and Engineering Company Limited. Its major units were associated with Muzaffarpur and Mokama in Bihar, not with Bhagalpur. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 10.q: 86. ‘Gandak Project’ is a joint project of which two states?
Set 10.explanation: In December 1959, an agreement was signed between the Government of India and the Government of Nepal for the construction of the Gandak Barrage. The barrage was constructed on the Gandak River at Valmiki Nagar in West Champaran in 1968-69, with the objective of providing irrigation facilities to Nepal as well as to Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

Set 10.q: 87. Which IAS officer of the Bihar cadre has recently been appointed as the ‘Director of Census Operations/Director of Citizen Registration’ for Bihar at the Deputy Secretary level for a period of three years?
Set 10.explanation: Ranjita, a 2013 batch IAS officer of the Bihar cadre, has been appointed as the Director of Census Operations/Director of Citizen Registration, Bihar, for a period of three years. Her appointment has been made under the Central Staffing Scheme at the Deputy Secretary level. Her headquarters will be in Patna.

Set 10.q: 88. Under the modern eco-tourism centre being developed at a cost of ₹18 crore in Bihar’s only tiger reserve, ‘Valmiki Tiger Reserve’, a ‘Conservation Centre’ is being established for which specific species with the objective of environmental conservation?
Set 10.explanation: A vulture conservation centre is being established as part of the eco-tourism centre being developed at a cost of about Rs. 18 crore in Valmiki Tiger Reserve, Bihar’s only tiger reserve. Vultures play an important role in maintaining ecological balance by disposing of the remains of dead animals as natural scavengers.

Set 10.q: 89. Which district of Bihar touches the borders of both Nepal and Uttar Pradesh?
Set 10.explanation: West Champaran is the only district of Bihar that borders Nepal to the north and Uttar Pradesh to the west. Thus, it is the only district of Bihar that shares its border with both Nepal and Uttar Pradesh.

Set 10.q: 90. In collaboration with the Bihar Mausam Seva Kendra (BMSK), the Indian Space Research Organisation has announced the installation of state-of-the-art ‘Doppler Weather Radars’ in which two districts of Bihar?
Set 10.explanation: Explanation: In collaboration with ISRO and the Bihar Weather Service Centre, it was announced that advanced Doppler Weather Radars would be installed in the West Champaran and Bhagalpur districts of Bihar. These radars will help make nowcasting, that is, short term forecasting for 0–6 hours, more accurate by monitoring rainfall, storms, lightning and weather systems.

Set 10.q: 91. Identify the region of the revolt of indigo cultivators in Bihar during 1866–86—
Set 10.explanation: Explanation: Distressed by oppression and tired of their miserable life, the indigo-growing ryots of North Bihar revolted in 1866–67 AD. The fire of the revolt first broke out at the Jawkatia-Lal Saraiya indigo factory. From there, the revolt spread to Champaran and Muzaffarpur.

Set 10.q: 94. Kunwar Singh was one of the prominent heroes of the Revolt of 1857. He was associated with which of the following?

He was endowed with indomitable courage, bravery and the ideal qualities of a military commander. For this reason, he is rightly regarded as the ‘Lion of Bihar’ during the revolt. He overthrew British authority in the Shahabad and Ara region and established his own government. He advanced towards Kalpi to help Nana Sahib in a joint attack on Kanpur. He carried the torch of rebellion to Rohtas, Mirzapur, Rewa, Banda and Lucknow, where he was received with great respect. In his final victory, he decisively defeated the British near his hometown Jagdishpur. During this battle, Kunwar Singh was seriously injured, and he died on 26 April 1858. After his death, his brother Amar Singh continued the struggle against the British until December 1858.

Set 10.q: 95. For music concerts, the walls of a hall should—
Set 10.explanation: Most solid and hard surfaces reflect sound, while soft surfaces absorb sound. If the walls of a concert hall reflect sound, the audience will hear an echo. Therefore, to prevent echoes, the walls and ceiling of concert halls are made or treated with soft sound-absorbing materials such as fibreglass.

Set 10.q: 97. In India, tropical rainforests are found in—

These forests are mainly found in the high-rainfall areas of the Western Ghats, Lakshadweep, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the upper parts of Assam and along the coast of Tamil Nadu. They are well developed in areas that receive more than 200 cm of rainfall and have a short dry season.

Set 10.q: 98. The main objective of watershed or catchment development in the semi-arid regions of India is—
options: to create slopes on a large scale so that rainwater does not evaporate.
to retain rainwater locally, reduce surface runoff and preserve soil moisture.
to recharge deep tube wells so that water can be extracted from rock strata.
to establish a system of reservoirs by constructing embankments for the water of seasonal rivers.
Set 10.explanation: The main objective of watershed development in the semi-arid regions of India is to retain rainwater locally, reduce surface runoff, preserve soil moisture and increase groundwater recharge. For this purpose, soil bunds, contour bunds, soil-conservation measures, afforestation, pasture development and small water-harvesting structures are constructed.

Set 10.q: 99. Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Water vapour is a highly variable gas of the lower atmosphere.
The belt of maximum temperature is found along the Equator.
The frigid zone is found between the polar circles and the poles in both hemispheres.
Jet streams are very high-altitude winds that affect surface weather conditions.
Set 10.explanation: Statement (b) is not correct. Generally, the Sun’s rays fall directly near the Equator. Therefore, the temperature is high there. Even then, the belt of maximum temperature on the Earth is not found exactly along the Equator. The reason for this is that in equatorial regions, rainfall, humidity and evaporation are high, due to which the temperature cannot rise very much. In contrast, in subtropical deserts and continental interiors, the sky usually remains clear and land areas heat up rapidly. Therefore, the belt of high temperature is found away from the Equator. Hence, statement (b) is not correct. The other statements given in the question are correct.

Low, flat plains near river courses, which are prone to floods

Set 10.q: 105. Assertion (A): During neap tides, the high tide is lower than normal and the low tide is higher than normal. Reason (R): Neap tides, unlike spring tides, occur at the time of the new moon instead of the full moon.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Neap tides, unlike spring tides, do not occur on the full moon or new moon, but on the seventh or eighth day of the bright fortnight and the dark fortnight. Hence, statement (A) is correct, but reason (R) is incorrect.

Set 10.q: 110. Why is there a concern about copper smelting plants? 1. They may release lethal quantities of carbon monoxide into the environment. 2. Copper slag may cause the leaching of some heavy metals into the environment. 3. They may release sulphur dioxide as a pollutant.
Set 10.explanation: In copper smelting plants, copper is separated from its ore by smelting at high temperatures. The major ores of copper are generally sulphides. When these are smelted and oxidised, sulphur dioxide may be released. SO2 is an important air pollutant and may have adverse effects on respiratory health. Therefore, statement (3) is correct. During smelting, copper slag is also formed. It is a solid residue/ by-product. Depending on the ore and the smelting process, some heavy metals or metallic elements may remain in it. If such slag is not managed safely, these elements may leach under acidic rainwater or other environmental conditions and may pollute soil and water/groundwater. Therefore, statement (2) is also correct. Statement (1) is not correct because the emission of carbon monoxide in hazardous quantities is not considered a main environmental concern of copper smelting plants. CO may be formed during industrial heating or fuel combustion, but in the context of this question, the major concerns are the leaching of heavy metals from copper slag and SO2 emissions.

Set 10.q: 111. Which indicators are used as the basis for assessing sustainable development?
Set 10.explanation: Among the given options, all the options—ecological, economic, and social and cultural indicators—are included for assessing sustainable development. Sustainable development is the concept of development under which the needs of the present generation are met without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

Set 10.q: 112. Eutrophication in water bodies occurs due to—
options: immersion of idols in water bodies
excessive algal growth or algal bloom
excess of nitrogenous nutrients and orthophosphate
Set 10.explanation: Eutrophication means the excessive enrichment of a water body with nutrients. Nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus play the main role in this process. These nutrients generally reach water bodies through fertilizer runoff, domestic sewage, detergents, agricultural runoff and industrial wastes. When the amount of nitrate, ammonium, phosphate and orthophosphate increases in water, there is rapid growth of algae and phytoplankton. This excessive growth of algae is called an algal bloom. Later, when these algae die, a large amount of dissolved oxygen is consumed during their decomposition. This may cause oxygen deficiency in water and may even lead to the death of fish and other aquatic organisms. Therefore, from the examination point of view, remember that the basic cause of eutrophication is the excess of nutrients, whereas algal bloom and oxygen deficiency are its results. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Set 10.q: 113. Consider the following statements: 1. On January 1, 2026, Bulgaria became the 21st member of the eurozone. 2. At present, all 27 member states of the European Union (EU) have adopted the euro as their official currency.

Set 10.q: 141. If 1 January 2006 was a Wednesday, then what day would 31 December 2006 be?
Set 10.explanation: ∵ The first and last days of an ordinary year are the same. ∵ The day of the week on 1 January 2006 = Wednesday ∴ The day of the week on 31 December 2006 = Wednesday Hence, option (b) is correct.

Set 10.q: 142. In a certain code language, ‘FACED’ is written as ‘GZDDE’ and ‘VFCAY’ is written as ‘WEDZZ’. How will ‘LABOR’ be written in the same language?
Set 10.explanation: Just as, F A C E D  → G Z D D E +1 +1 +1–1–1 and V F C A Y  → W E D Z Z +1 +1 +1–1–1–1 Similarly, L A B O R  → M Z C N S–1–1 +1 +1 +1 Hence, option (b) is correct.

Set 10.q: 144. In this question, a statement is followed by two conclusions. Statement: Domestic demand is increasing faster than the production of indigenous crude oil. Conclusions: I. If the demand is to be met, crude oil should be imported. II. Domestic demand should be reduced.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follows.
Set 10.explanation: According to the statement, domestic demand is increasing rapidly compared with domestic crude oil production. Therefore, conclusion I, that crude oil should be imported if the demand is to be met, definitely follows, whereas conclusion II does not follow from the statement.
